<a id="Libpetri-Spec-CORE_036"></a>
## CORE-036: Arc semantics summary

`Libpetri.Spec.CORE_036` · Kind **B** · Scope all executors; the outcome line with output validation enabled (CONC-026, the default) · Source **verbatim** (spec/01-core-model.md) · Sign-off **pending** · Statement hash `78d3fa5e658ee902`

| Natural language | Plain reading | Lean statement |
|---|---|---|
| *While* an input place of the transition holds fewer tokens than the required count of its input arc, the transition *shall not* fire.<br><br>*While* a read place of the transition is unmarked, the transition *shall not* fire.<br><br>*While* an inhibitor place of the transition is marked, the transition *shall not* fire.<br><br>*While* the transition is enabled, it *shall* be able to fire, whatever its output places and reset places hold.<br><br>*When* the transition fires, each input place that is not a reset place *shall* lose the consumption count of its input arc, and gain what the firing deposits there.<br><br>*When* the transition fires, each place that is neither an input place nor a reset place *shall* lose no tokens, and gain what the firing deposits there.<br><br>*When* the transition fires, each reset place *shall* end holding exactly what the firing deposited there.<br><br>*When* the transition fires and the firing ends with its action, on an executor with output validation enabled ([CONC-026], the default), the places in which it deposits *shall* be exactly the places of one output branch of its output spec, each receiving one or more tokens.<br><br>*When* the transition fires and the firing ends with the timeout outcome, it *shall* deposit in every place as many tokens as the timeout outcome puts there ([IO-013], [IO-014]).<br><br>Deposits are compared per place: the order in which a firing deposits its tokens is not normative, and two deposits that put the same number of tokens in every place are the same deposit. | 1. For every transition t:<br>2. t does not fire from a marking in which an input place p holds fewer tokens than the required count c of its input arc;<br>3. t does not fire from a marking in which a read place p is unmarked;<br>4. t does not fire from a marking in which an inhibitor place p is marked;<br>5. from every marking at which t is enabled, some firing of t exists (to some marking);<br>6. every firing of t that deposits d leaves an input place p that is not a reset place with what it held, minus the consumption count of its arc, plus what d puts in p;<br>7. every firing of t that deposits d leaves a place p that is neither an input place nor a reset place of t with what it held plus what d puts in p;<br>8. every firing of t that deposits d leaves a reset place p with exactly what d puts in p;<br>9. every firing of t from m that deposits d either puts one or more tokens in each place of some output branch b of t and none in any other place, or puts in every place as many tokens as some timeout outcome d₀ of t for what the firing consumed from m. | <pre>fun {N} [DecidableEq N] F ↦<br>  ∀ (t : Reference.Trans N),<br>    (∀ (p : N) (c : Card),<br>        InputArc t p c → while fun m ↦ TokenCount m p &lt; requiredCount c, never Fire F t) ∧<br>      (∀ (p : N), ReadArc t p → while fun m ↦ ¬Marked m p, never Fire F t) ∧<br>        (∀ (p : N), InhibitorArc t p → while fun m ↦ Marked m p, never Fire F t) ∧<br>          (∀ (m : CountMarking N), Enabled t m → ∃ m', Fire F t m m') ∧<br>            (∀ (d : List N) (p : N) (c : Card),<br>                InputArc t p c →<br>                  ¬ResetArc t p →<br>                    on fun m m' ↦ F t m d m', shall fun m m' ↦<br>                      TokenCount m' p =<br>                        TokenCount m p - consumptionCount c (TokenCount m p) +<br>                          Deposits d p) ∧<br>              (∀ (d : List N) (p : N),<br>                  (∀ (c : Card), ¬InputArc t p c) →<br>                    ¬ResetArc t p →<br>                      on fun m m' ↦ F t m d m', shall fun m m' ↦<br>                        TokenCount m' p = TokenCount m p + Deposits d p) ∧<br>                (∀ (d : List N) (p : N),<br>                    ResetArc t p →<br>                      on fun m m' ↦ F t m d m', shall fun x m' ↦<br>                        TokenCount m' p = Deposits d p) ∧<br>                  ∀ (d : List N),<br>                    on fun m m' ↦ F t m d m', shall fun m x ↦<br>                      (∃ b, OutputBranch t b ∧ OnPlacesOf d b) ∨<br>                        ∃ d₀, TimeoutOutcome t (Consumes t m) d₀ ∧ SamePerPlace d d₀</pre> |

**Assumptions**

- A firing is read as one step from a marking to a marking (glossary: Fire); timing and priority play no part, so 'produced on complete' (Output) and 'consumed / removed on fire' (Input, Reset) both land in the one step. 'Able to fire' is read as 'some firing exists', to any target marking.
- Requires token? column. 'Yes' for an input arc is read as 'holds at least the required count' (glossary: Enabled, Required count), which is one token for One and All; 'Yes' for a read arc as 'marked'; 'No (blocks if present)' for an inhibitor arc as 'marked blocks'. The 'No' entries (output, reset, and the inhibitor arc while its place is unmarked) are read together as the fourth line: the table lists every token requirement, so a transition whose input, read and inhibitor arcs are all satisfied can fire whatever its output and reset places hold.
- Consumes? column. 'Yes' for an input arc is read as the consumption count of IO-007 (glossary: Consumption count). 'No' for output, inhibitor and read arcs is the sixth line: a place that only those arcs touch loses nothing. 'Yes (all)' for a reset arc is the seventh line (glossary: Deposit): a reset place that is also an output place keeps what the firing deposited there, and a reset place that is also an input place ends with the deposit too, so the fifth line excludes reset places.
- The fifth line uses truncated subtraction, as Seam.fireNC does; under the first line the subtraction never truncates, because a firing only starts when every input place holds at least its required count.
- Effect column, Output ('Token produced on complete') is the outcome line, the last line of the reading, which reads the eighth, ninth and tenth sentences quoted together. A firing relation does not record how a firing ended. As IO-012 says, a firing ends with its action when it does not end with the timeout outcome, and a firing whose deposit puts in every place as many tokens as some timeout-outcome deposit of the transition from the same marking may have ended with the timeout outcome. So the eighth and ninth sentences are read as one disjunction: the deposit marks exactly the places of an output branch (eighth: the branch fixes which places receive tokens, one or more each, not how many; glossary: Output branch, Produced set), or it equals a timeout outcome per place (ninth: as many tokens in every place). A transition with no output spec has the one empty branch, so it deposits nothing. Read ('Token remains') is the sixth line. Inhibitor ('Disables transition') is the third line.
- Tenth sentence (deposits are compared per place). Every line of the reading reads the deposit d only through Deposits d (the produced set of d is the set of places p with Deposits d p ≠ 0), so two deposits that put the same number of tokens in every place satisfy it alike and the order of d plays no part: core036_c8_perPlace shows it for the outcome line, and core036_perPlace_closed shows that closing any firing relation under per-place equal deposits keeps CORE-036. Lines 5 to 7 already compare per place.
- The outcome line is scoped by CONC-026: F is read as the firing relation of an executor with output validation enabled, the default. With the CONC-026 skip enabled a firing that ends with its action deposits what the action wrote, as CONC-026 says, and the outcome line is not claimed of it; lines 1 to 7 hold of every executor.
- TimeoutOutcome reads the first Timeout node in pre-order. A transition that builds holds at most one Timeout node and no ForwardInput outside a Timeout child (IO-013, IO-014), so that node's outcome is the timeout outcome. Transitions that building rejects (IO-011 to IO-014) are not transitions of any net (CORE-022); the statement still ranges over every Trans, and the reference semantics satisfies it for all of them, so it needs no well-formedness premise. That at most one output branch matches a deposit (IO-012) is not part of CORE-036: the outcome line asks for some branch.
- Read, 'provides value': the value of the read token is not visible at token-count granularity; that the action receives it is CORE-032 AC3, not encoded here.
- Input token order (FIFO, CORE-030 AC2) and output token timestamps (CORE-035 AC2, IO-014 AC5) are below token-count granularity and not encoded here.
- AC1 (each arc type behaves exactly as described in the table) is the whole statement: one line per cell of the 'Requires token?' column (lines 1 to 4) and of the 'Consumes?' and 'Effect' columns (lines 5 to 7 and the outcome line), as laid out in the assumptions above.
- AC2 (an action that writes two tokens into one place of the branch it satisfies fires, and the marking receives all of them) is CORE_036_allows_multi: CORE-036 holds of a firing relation in which t: a → and(b, c) fires with the write b, b, c, and that firing leaves 2 tokens in b and 1 in c. That such a write is deposited at all is IO-015 and IO-016 AC4; CORE-036 only has to allow it.
- AC3 (two firings that deposit the same number of tokens in every place, in different orders, deposit the same outcome) is core036_c8_perPlace and core036_perPlace_closed, and concretely CORE_036_allows_multi: the write c, b, b of the same transition is allowed alike and leaves the same marking.
- InputArc names the first input arc on a place (glossary: Input arc); CORE-030 rejects a transition with two input arcs on one place at build, so for every well-formed transition it is the only one.

## CORE-037: Dead Arc Warning

`Libpetri.Spec.CORE_037` · Kind **F** · Scope the dead-arc report of every executor backend and of the SMT verifier; the events and report lines are the second block of this ID · Source **verbatim** (spec/01-core-model.md) · Sign-off **pending** · Statement hash `6cadeee8338fe6be`

| Natural language | Plain reading | Lean statement |
|---|---|---|
| The dead-arc report *shall* contain a read, inhibitor or reset arc of a transition of the net exactly when no transition has an input arc on the arc's place, no transition's output spec names that place anywhere in its tree (every `And` and `Xor` branch, the `Timeout` child and the `ForwardInput` target included), the place is not an environment place and the initial marking holds no token on it, and *shall* contain nothing else.<br><br>The dead-arc report *shall* list each dead arc once, as its own entry (two dead arcs on one place are two entries), in the order the net holds its transitions (the order they were added to the builder) and, within a transition, its read arcs, then its inhibitor arcs, then its reset arcs, each kind in the order the transition declares those arcs.<br><br>The warning text of a read, inhibitor or reset arc of a transition *shall* be `&lt;kind> arc of '&lt;transition>' on '&lt;place>': no transition produces into or consumes from it and it starts empty; &lt;effect>.` with `&lt;kind>` the arc's kind (`read`, `inhibitor` or `reset`), `&lt;transition>` the name of the transition that declares the arc, `&lt;place>` the name of its place, and `&lt;effect>` `the transition can never be enabled` for a read arc, `the arc never blocks` for an inhibitor arc and `the arc has no effect` for a reset arc. | 1. For every dead-arc report Rep and warning text Msg on nets whose places are their names:<br>2. for every net X, environment places env and initial marking m0, an entry is in Rep X env m0 exactly when some transition t of X carries the entry's transition name and has an arc of the entry's kind on the entry's place, and that place is dead: no transition of X has an input arc on it or names it anywhere in its output spec (outPlaces: both children of an And, both branches of an Xor, the Timeout child, the target of a ForwardInput), env does not hold it and m0 puts no token on it;<br>3. Rep X env m0 is the list of every read, inhibitor and reset arc of X in report order (deadArcCandidates: the transitions in the order X holds them, within a transition its read, then inhibitor, then reset arcs, each kind in the transition's own order), keeping exactly the entries Rep X env m0 holds, each as often as X lists it;<br>4. the warning text of a read arc entry (t, p) is the template with kind `read`, the transition name t, the place name p and effect `the transition can never be enabled`;<br>5. the warning text of an inhibitor arc entry is the template with kind `inhibitor` and effect `the arc never blocks`;<br>6. the warning text of a reset arc entry is the template with kind `reset` and effect `the arc has no effect`. | <pre>fun Rep Msg ↦<br>  (∀ (X : Reference.Net String) (env : String → Bool) (m0 : String → ℕ)<br>      (a : DeadArc String),<br>      a ∈ Rep X env m0 ↔<br>        ∃ t ∈ X.transitions,<br>          a.transition = t.core.name ∧<br>            (a.kind = DeadArcKind.read ∧ ReadArc t a.place ∨<br>                a.kind = DeadArcKind.inhibitor ∧ InhibitorArc t a.place ∨<br>                  a.kind = DeadArcKind.reset ∧ ResetArc t a.place) ∧<br>              DeadPlace X env m0 a.place) ∧<br>    (∀ (X : Reference.Net String) (env : String → Bool) (m0 : String → ℕ),<br>        Rep X env m0 =<br>          List.filter (fun a ↦ decide (a ∈ Rep X env m0)) (deadArcCandidates X)) ∧<br>      (∀ (t p : String),<br>          Msg { kind := DeadArcKind.read, transition := t, place := p } =<br>            "read arc of '" ++ t ++ "' on '" ++ p ++<br>              "': no transition produces into or consumes from it and it starts empty; the transition can never be enabled.") ∧<br>        (∀ (t p : String),<br>            Msg { kind := DeadArcKind.inhibitor, transition := t, place := p } =<br>              "inhibitor arc of '" ++ t ++ "' on '" ++ p ++<br>                "': no transition produces into or consumes from it and it starts empty; the arc never blocks.") ∧<br>          ∀ (t p : String),<br>            Msg { kind := DeadArcKind.reset, transition := t, place := p } =<br>              "reset arc of '" ++ t ++ "' on '" ++ p ++<br>                "': no transition produces into or consumes from it and it starts empty; the arc has no effect."</pre> |

**Assumptions**

- The model is a pair: a dead-arc report Rep from a net (Reference.Net String: its transitions, in order), its environment places (a predicate on places) and its initial marking (token counts) to a list of entries (kind, name of the declaring transition, place), and a warning text Msg of one entry. The environment places and the initial marking are parameters, as in all three runtimes (`dead_arcs` in the dead_arcs module of the Rust core crate, `findDeadArcs` in typescript/src/core/internal/dead-arcs.ts, `ArcDiagnostics.deadArcs` in Java): an executor passes the environment places registered for the run and the initial marking it was given, the verifier its own initial marking and environment places ([VER-001]). 'Starts empty' and 'the initial marking holds no token' are m0 p = 0.
- Places and transitions are identified by name (ruling D10), so a place of the model is its name and `<place>` in the text is that string, written as is. A text that prints some other rendering of the place, such as a Java Place record, is killed (CORE_037_forbids_recordMsg). Java tests whether a place is fed on its Place record (name and token type, the divergence MOD-024 records), Rust and TypeScript on its name; a net with two same-named places of different token types is that divergence and is not encoded. Lines 1 and 2 hold of refDeadArcs at every place type (core037_line1_ref, core037_line2_ref).
- Transition order is the order of the net's transition list. That this list is the order in which the transitions were added to the builder is CORE-040's line under ruling D32 (wave W2, RefNetBuild); the W2 integrator may then add a [CORE-040] link to the second sentence. Within one kind the order is the transition's own arc list (NTransition.reads, inhibitors, resets), which is the order the transition declares the arcs in all three runtimes. A transition that lists one place twice under one arc kind declares two arcs, and line 2 lists both, which is the sentence's 'each dead arc once, as its own entry'; whether a builder accepts such a transition is not this block's subject.
- The text lines fix Msg on every read, inhibitor and reset arc entry, dead or not, as the third sentence says: the text is a pure template of the entry, and an implementation uses it only for the entries of the report.
- The output-spec clause of line 1 is outPlaces: the place of a Place node, both children of an And, both branches of an Xor, the child of a Timeout and the target of a ForwardInput. The source of a ForwardInput is not named by the output spec; IO-014 requires it to be an input place of the transition, so the input-arc clause covers it.
- The section's definition is its bullets (ruling D20, clash core-b#1): the lead-in ends at 'is dead when:', because 'nothing can ever put a token on P' is not equivalent: a place with an input arc but no producer, no initial token and no injection also stays empty for the whole run, yet its read arc is not dead, so the report holds nothing for it (core037_gap_nonvacuous). The sentence 'No firing ever puts a token on such a place, …' is a consequence on the reference firing semantics: a dead place is empty in every reachable marking (core037_dead_stays_empty), so a dead read arc's transition is never enabled (core037_deadRead_never_enabled), a dead inhibitor never blocks (core037_deadInhibitor_never_blocks) and a dead reset clears nothing (core037_deadReset_clears_nothing). Reach has no injection step: an environment place is not dead by line 1, and the sentence's 'a host injects tokens only into environment places' is ENV-001's; that the Rust and Python executors accept an injection into a place that is not registered, under a host assumption (ruling D89, clash env-a), is the environment requirements' subject, not this block's.
- The executor bullet (one log-message event per dead arc when the executor is constructed, through the CORE-072 AC4 mechanism: logger `libpetri.runtime`, level `WARN`, the declaring transition's name, emitted only where events are recorded and never changing execution) and the verifier bullet (one report line per dead arc, the warning text prefixed with `WARNING: `, no result field and no verdict depending on it) are SHOULD sentences over the event model and the verifier pipeline. They are the second block of this ID (kind B, wave W11: RefEvents for EVT-013, RefVerifier for VER-001) and are not encoded here. Their text 'One message per dead arc, not per place: two dead arcs on one place are two messages.' and 'Arcs are reported in transition order and, within a transition, read, inhibitor, then reset.' is lines 1 and 2 of this block: a report with one entry per place loses an entry line 1 requires (CORE_037_forbids_perPlace), a report in kind order across transitions breaks line 2 (CORE_037_forbids_kindMajor), and so do a report with the kinds in another order within a transition (CORE_037_forbids_resetFirst) and a report with one kind's arcs in reverse order (CORE_037_forbids_reverseWithinKind).
- AC1 (a reset arc on a place no transition consumes from or produces into, not an environment place and empty in the initial marking, gives exactly one warning naming the transition and the place) is line 1 and the reset text; CORE_037_nonvacuous checks the test derivation's net (`hub_kill` resets `answer/IN`) and the message bytes of AC1's example; a report that counts a reset arc as consuming its place drops AC1's arc (CORE_037_forbids_resetConsumes), and a text with another reset effect (CORE_037_forbids_resetMsg) or with the transition and the place swapped (CORE_037_forbids_swapNames) is killed. That the warning is one WARN log-message event and one `WARNING:` report line is the B block (W11).
- AC2 (the same for a read arc and an inhibitor arc, with their effects) is line 1 and the read and inhibitor texts, checked by CORE_037_nonvacuous; a text that swaps the read and inhibitor effects is killed (CORE_037_forbids_swapMsg).
- AC3 (no warning when the initial marking puts a token on the place, when it is an environment place, when any transition has an input arc on it, or when any transition's output spec contains it in any branch) is line 1, the clauses of DeadPlace; CORE_037_nonvacuous checks a seeded place, an environment place, a consumed place and a place only a Timeout child inside an Xor names, and core037_outSpec_nonvacuous a place only an And child names and a place only a ForwardInput target names. Reports that ignore the initial marking (CORE_037_forbids_ignoreInit), ignore the environment places (CORE_037_forbids_ignoreEnv), count producers only (CORE_037_forbids_producersOnly), read only a top-level output place (CORE_037_forbids_topOnly), skip the Timeout child (CORE_037_forbids_noTimeout) or skip the ForwardInput target (CORE_037_forbids_noForward) are killed.
- AC4 (the warning never rejects a net and never changes execution, a verdict or a result field): the report is a total function with no failure value, and no line of this block constrains a builder, a firing or a verdict; that a dead arc never makes a builder reject is CORE-040's (W2), and that execution, verdicts and result fields do not depend on the warning is the B block (W11).
- The SHOULD priority applies to the requirement: an implementation that reports dead arcs follows the three shall sentences.
- The test derivation (a transition `kill` that resets `x`, nothing else touching `x`, one warning naming `kill` and `x` with an empty initial marking and none with `x` seeded; the same with a read and an inhibitor arc, and with `x` produced by another transition's Xor branch) is CORE_037_nonvacuous on the reference report: `kill` with a read, an inhibitor and a reset arc on untouched places, a seeded place, and a place only an Xor branch of `use` names. The event, the report line and their counts are the B block's.

<a id="Libpetri-Spec-CORE_040"></a>
## CORE-040: Net Builder

`Libpetri.Spec.CORE_040` · Kind **F** · Scope all net builders used without composition or fusion sets · Source **verbatim** (spec/01-core-model.md) · Sign-off **pending** · Statement hash `10650af697be3624`

| Natural language | Plain reading | Lean statement |
|---|---|---|
| The sentences below concern a net builder used without composition ([MOD-020], [MOD-025], [MOD-027]) and without fusion sets ([MOD-060], [MOD-061]), which rewrite arcs, drop places or reject at build under their own requirements.<br><br>*When* a net is built from transitions, each added once, whose names are pairwise distinct ([TIME-010]), the net *shall* hold exactly the added transitions, in the order they were added, which is the declaration order of its transitions.<br><br>*When* a net is built, every declared place, every declared terminal place ([EXEC-042]), every place that an input, inhibitor, read or reset arc of an added transition names and every place in the `allPlaces` set of the output specification of an added transition ([IO-017]) *shall* be a place of the net.<br><br>*When* a net is built, the net *shall not* hold any other place, and *shall not* hold a place twice ([CORE-002]).<br><br>Building a net that declares no terminal place ([EXEC-042]) *shall* succeed.<br><br>Which nets that declare terminal places build, and which terminal places a built net holds, are stated by [EXEC-042]. | 1. For every transition builder B and every net builder NB over B's instances:<br>2. if NB returns the net b for the input inp and the added transitions of inp have pairwise distinct names, the transitions of b are the definitions of the added transitions, in the order added;<br>3. if NB returns b for inp, every declared place of inp, every declared terminal place of inp and every place an added transition has an arc on (an arc place: input, read, inhibitor or reset) or holds in the allPlaces set of its output specification (an output arc, IO-017) is a place of b;<br>4. if NB returns b for inp, every place of b is a declared place, a declared terminal place or a place an added transition has an arc on or holds in the allPlaces set of its output specification, and no place of b appears twice;<br>5. for every input inp that declares no terminal place, NB returns a net. | <pre>fun {N A} [DecidableEq N] B NB ↦<br>  (∀ (inp : NetIn B) (b : BuiltNet N A),<br>      NB inp = Except.ok b →<br>        (List.map (fun x ↦ (B.defOf x).core.name) inp.trans).Nodup →<br>          b.trans = List.map B.defOf inp.trans) ∧<br>    (∀ (inp : NetIn B) (b : BuiltNet N A),<br>        NB inp = Except.ok b →<br>          ∀ (p : N),<br>            (p ∈ inp.places ∨<br>                p ∈ inp.terminals ∨<br>                  ∃ x ∈ inp.trans,<br>                    ArcPlace (B.defOf x).toTrans p ∨ OutputArc (B.defOf x).toTrans p) →<br>              p ∈ b.places) ∧<br>      (∀ (inp : NetIn B) (b : BuiltNet N A),<br>          NB inp = Except.ok b →<br>            (∀ p ∈ b.places,<br>                p ∈ inp.places ∨<br>                  p ∈ inp.terminals ∨<br>                    ∃ x ∈ inp.trans,<br>                      ArcPlace (B.defOf x).toTrans p ∨ OutputArc (B.defOf x).toTrans p) ∧<br>              b.places.Nodup) ∧<br>        ∀ (inp : NetIn B), inp.terminals = [] → ∃ b, NB inp = Except.ok b</pre> |

**Assumptions**

- A net builder (NetBuilder B) is the build call of one implementation's net builder, read as a function from what the host added (NetIn B: the declared places in the order declared, the added transitions in the order added, as instances of the transition builder B, and the declared terminal places) to a built net (BuiltNet: its places, its transitions' definitions, its terminal places) or a rejection with a message (a panic or an exception, read as `.error msg`). A net holds only what a transition builder returned (BuiltNet.FromBuilder; the W2 tracer decision), so the added transitions are instances of B, not bare definitions. Places are the abstract place type N, identity = equality on N; how a host place object maps to N (by name in TypeScript, Rust and Python, by name and token type in Java) is CORE-002's (PlaceKeyed).
- Scope. The block concerns a builder used without composition (MOD-020 instance composition, MOD-025 direct composition, and MOD-027's rejection of an arc on a port place that instance composition bound) and without fusion sets (MOD-060, MOD-061), as its first quoted sentence says. Fusion rewrites the arcs of every transition (rust/libpetri-core/src/petri_net.rs:918, rewriter::apply_fusion), which breaks line 1, and removes non-canonical members from the place set (:920-938), which breaks line 2; build panics or throws on fusion overlap (:878-888) and on an arc naming a port place that instance composition bound (MOD-027, :695-697, :707-731) with no terminal place declared, which breaks line 4 (Java: java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/core/PetriNet.java build at :1000, throws at :1032-1056). What a composed or fused net holds is the composition model's (W8), stated over the same net builder extended. Rust's second public constructor PetriNet::map_transitions (rust/libpetri-core/src/petri_net.rs:156-165) is not a net builder: its documented, unchecked precondition is that the mapping introduces no place the net does not already declare, so a net it returns meets line 2 only when the caller keeps that precondition.
- Line 1 is the declaration order of ruling D32 (a): the order the transitions were added is the net's transition order, which EXEC-002 (FIFO among equal priorities) and CORE-037 (the order of the dead-arc report) read. Its premise is the shared unique-names assumption of rulings D10 and D23 (a) (spec/03-timing.md, TIME-010: the transitions of one net have pairwise distinct names), on the added transitions, read over the list of additions (the quoted 'each added once'), so one transition instance added twice has its name twice and is outside the premise; no builder checks it. Outside it the runtimes differ: given one transition instance twice, Java and TypeScript hold it once (a set) and Rust twice (a Vec, a clone keeps its identity) (clash core-b#5, rust/libpetri-core/src/petri_net.rs:30, rust/libpetri-core/src/transition.rs:32). A builder that reverses the transitions (core040_reverseNB) violates line 1 and meets the order-free reading (CORE_040_mutant_orderFree).
- Line 2 is AC3 made a MUST by ruling D32 (a): the places of every arc of all five kinds are collected, the arc places of the glossary (input, read, inhibitor, reset; ArcPlace in Spec/GlossaryTime.lean) and every place of the output specification (OutputArc; IO-017's AllPlaces, so the target of a ForwardInput and every place of a Timeout child count). All three runtimes do so (rust/libpetri-core/src/petri_net.rs:319-339, java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/core/PetriNet.java:320-328, typescript/src/core/petri-net.ts:212-230). A declared terminal place is declared as a place too in all three (rust/libpetri-core/src/petri_net.rs:301-308, java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/core/PetriNet.java:362-367, typescript/src/core/petri-net.ts:199-203). A builder that collects only input and output places (core040_inOutOnlyNB, the pre-D32 reading, CORE_040_mutant_inOutOnly) or drops a declared place no arc names (core040_dropDeclaredNB, CORE_040_mutant_arcPlacesOnly) violates line 2, and so does one that collects the source of a ForwardInput instead of its target and nothing from a Timeout child (core040_outSlipNB, CORE_040_forbids_outSlip: place 5 of the example is the target of a ForwardInput inside a Timeout). The quoted sentence collects the allPlaces set of IO-017, which holds a ForwardInput's target only; its source is collected all the same, as an input place: the transition builder rejects a forward from a place that is not an input of the transition (IO-014 AC3, Spec/Glossary.lean WellFormedOut), and the added transitions are its outputs. Line 2 is what discharges the hypothesis hDecl (Novel.Seam.ArcsDeclared) of the postfix soundness theorems for every builder that meets CORE-040 (core040_arcsDeclared), not only for the reference (refNetBuild_arcsDeclared_toNNetB).
- Line 3: the net holds no place other than those of line 2 and no place twice, both on N. Ruling D66 (a) keeps 'no place twice' a MUST and records TypeScript as a defect (RD-03 in spec/runtime-defects.md): place(name) returns a fresh object (typescript/src/core/place.ts:25-27) and the builder's place set compares by reference (typescript/src/core/petri-net.ts:158, :212-227), so two place objects named 'A' give PetriNet.places two entries of one name; only the compiled net dedupes by name (typescript/src/runtime/compiled-net.ts:93). Under name identity (N := String) TypeScript's net violates line 3 until that defect is fixed (a runtime change, not made here). A builder that keeps a place twice (core040_noDedupNB, CORE_040_mutant_dupsAllowed) or adds a place nobody declared or named (core040_extraNB, CORE_040_mutant_extraAllowed) violates line 3. The order of the places is not stated: ruling D32 orders transitions only, and the reference keeps the last occurrence of a place where the runtimes keep the first.
- Line 4: the net builder rejects nothing of its own. Its one rejection in scope is EXEC-042 AC5 (a declared terminal place that an added transition consumes from or reads, NetIn.TerminalClash); on an input with no terminal place it cannot arise. Over an input with terminal places, EXEC-042's build block (EXEC_042_build, kind F, over every abstract net builder, not over the reference only) says both directions: its line 1 rejects a clash, its line 2 builds every input without one, so a builder that also rejects a terminal place on an inhibitor or reset arc violates EXEC_042_build line 2 on exec042_netInh (as EXEC_042_build_mutant_rejectAll_killed shows for the builder that rejects every terminal place). EXEC_042_build's own scope note reads its line 2, with no terminal place declared, as this line 4. A transition definition the transition builder rejects never reaches the net builder: the added transitions are instances, and CORE-020 says which inputs build. Without line 4 a builder that rejects everything meets lines 1 to 3 vacuously; one that rejects an empty net (core040_rejectEmptyNB, CORE_040_mutant_noAccept) violates it. Only success and failure are stated, not a message.
- Terminal places of the built net (BuiltNet.terminals). None of CORE-040's four lines reads them; a declared terminal place enters the net as a place by line 2. That the built net's terminal places are exactly the declared ones is EXEC_042_build line 3, over every abstract net builder; a builder that drops them (exec042_dropTerminalsNB, the TypeScript EMPTY_TERMINALS choice at typescript/src/core/petri-net.ts:736-741 made unconditionally) violates it (EXEC_042_build_forbids_dropTerminals). How often a terminal place is listed is stated nowhere: EXEC_042_build line 3 reads the terminal places as a set, all three runtimes keep each once (rust/libpetri-core/src/petri_net.rs:301-308, Java's LinkedHashSet, TypeScript's Map by name) and the reference keeps them once each in declaration order (refNetBuild_terminals); no requirement reads the multiplicity.
- AC1 (the builder can add places and transitions) is lines 1, 2 and 4 together: a declared place and an added transition are in the net, and building succeeds (CORE_040_nonvacuous). The builder pattern as an API shape is a Q-kind test (ruling D99 (a)).
- AC2 (build produces an immutable net) is CORE-041's subject: here a built net is a value (BuiltNet), and that a handle on it shows the same net after later builder calls is CORE-041's line over BuilderApi, whose builder trace (copyBuilder_trace) shows refNetBuild's net. TypeScript's builder that hands out its live sets (aliasBuilder) is CORE-041's recorded defect under ruling D66 (a) (RD-02).
- AC3 (places referenced by transitions are auto-collected) is line 2; its parenthesis ('implementations that auto-collect from arcs SHOULD do so') is replaced by the MUST of ruling D32 (a). The test derivation (build a net with transitions and verify all places from arcs are present) is line 2 on CORE_040_nonvacuous's example, whose transitions have arcs of all five kinds, with an output specification of every node kind but Xor: Place, And, Timeout and a ForwardInput inside the Timeout (a bare ForwardInput does not build, IO-014). The example's second transition has priority 5 and the first priority 0, so the order added (line 1) is not the priority order: a builder that sorts the transitions by priority (core040_prioSortNB, CORE_040_forbids_prioSort) violates line 1 on it.

<a id="Libpetri-Spec-CORE_041"></a>
## CORE-041: Net Immutability

`Libpetri.Spec.CORE_041` · Kind **B** · Scope all net builders used without composition or fusion sets · Source **verbatim** (spec/01-core-model.md) · Sign-off **pending** · Statement hash `9c29a517ee57b461`

| Natural language | Plain reading | Lean statement |
|---|---|---|
| After construction, a Petri net definition is immutable.<br><br>The set of places, transitions, and their connections cannot be modified.<br><br>*When* the build call of a net builder used as [CORE-040] describes is made, the call *shall* give the net that [CORE-040] describes, or report the rejection that [EXEC-042] describes, for all the places, transitions and terminal places added to that builder before the call, including those added before an earlier build call.<br><br>*When* a net builder used as [CORE-040] describes has built a net and is used again, to add places, transitions or terminal places or to build again, the net it built *shall* keep the places, transitions and terminal places it had when it was built. | 1. For every transition builder B, every net builder NB over B's instances and every builder state machine BA:<br>2. for every history of uses of a new builder (calls and builds, in the order made), the handle the next build returns shows, right after that build, NB's result (a built net or a rejection) on every call of the history, in the order made (NetIn.ofOps of the calls; a build adds nothing and resets nothing);<br>3. for every history of uses of a new builder and every later history of uses, the handle the build after the first history returns shows after the later history what it showed right after that build. | <pre>fun {N A} [DecidableEq N] B NB BA ↦<br>  (∀ (pre : List (BUse B)),<br>      BA.view (BA.build (runUses BA BA.init pre)).1<br>          (BA.build (runUses BA BA.init pre)).2 =<br>        NB (NetIn.ofOps (callsOf pre))) ∧<br>    ∀ (pre post : List (BUse B)),<br>      BA.view (runUses BA (BA.build (runUses BA BA.init pre)).1 post)<br>          (BA.build (runUses BA BA.init pre)).2 =<br>        BA.view (BA.build (runUses BA BA.init pre)).1<br>          (BA.build (runUses BA BA.init pre)).2</pre> |

**Assumptions**

- A builder state machine (BuilderApi in Reference/Build.lean) is the net builder of one implementation: its calls declare a place, add a built transition or declare a terminal place (BOp), build returns a handle on the built net, and view is what a handle shows (a built net, or the rejection the build reported: a Java exception or a Rust panic is read as a handle that shows the rejection). The net builder NB is the function CORE-040 is stated over. On its own, line 0 pins the handle relative to NB only: the blind builder, whose handle always shows the empty net, meets CORE-041 against the net builder that always returns the empty net (core041_blind_constEmpty). Read together with CORE-040 over the same NB, line 0 says that the handle shows CORE-040's built net (the builder trace, design note 3.8): every NB that meets CORE-040 lines 2 and 4 puts a declared place into the net, and then the blind builder violates line 0 (core041_blind_killed_declared). The joint statement over one shared NB is the integrator's (Spec/ConsistencyStructure.lean).
- Line 0 is the first quoted shall sentence. Without it the block is satisfied by a builder whose handle always shows the empty net (design note S6: core041_blindBuilder satisfies line 1, CORE_041_mutant_stableOnly_killed). Line 0 equates the handle with NB's whole result, so the build rejects exactly when NB rejects; in scope that is the rejection of EXEC-042 AC5 (CORE-040 line 4: the net builder rejects nothing of its own). A history may hold earlier builds; a build adds nothing to what the builder holds and resets nothing, so a second build shows every call made so far, including those made before the first build, as Java, TypeScript and the Python binding do (the Python NetBuilder clones the accumulated builder, rust/libpetri-py/src/model.rs:1143). A builder that empties itself at build meets line 0 on histories without an earlier build and line 1, and violates line 0 at its second build (core041_resetBuilder, CORE_041_mutant_firstBuild_killed). Rust consumes the builder (rust/libpetri-core/src/petri_net.rs:678), so in Rust no use follows a build and both lines speak of the first build only.
- Line 1 is the second quoted shall sentence and the body's two sentences ('After construction, a Petri net definition is immutable.' and 'The set of places, transitions, and their connections cannot be modified.'): a net's connections are the arcs of its transitions, which the built net carries in its transition definitions (TransDef), so a built net that keeps its places, transitions and terminal places keeps its connections. Later uses are calls and builds alike: a builder that keeps only the last built net, so that a later build changes the net an earlier handle shows, violates it (core041_slotBuilder, CORE_041_mutant_callsOnly_killed, the reading that allows later calls only).
- Ruling D66 (a): the MUST stands and the TypeScript builder is a recorded defect (RD-02 in spec/runtime-defects.md). Its build passes the builder's own place and transition sets to the net (typescript/src/core/petri-net.ts:740-741, stored as given by the constructor at :55-69), so a transition added after build appears in the built net; that is aliasBuilder (CORE_041_forbids_alias, and CORE_041_mutant_traceOnly_killed: it meets line 0). Java copies the sets into unmodifiable ones (java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/core/PetriNet.java:70-71). Fixing TypeScript is a runtime change and is not part of this block.
- Scope: a net built without fusion sets, instance composition or retired ports, as in CORE-040, which both quoted shall sentences name ('a net builder used as [CORE-040] describes'); those rewrite arcs and drop places, and belong to the composition model (W8). Nets derived from a built net (binding actions, CORE-042; composition) are new nets built through a builder, not changes to the built net, and are outside this block. What a handle shows is the net's places, transitions with their definitions and terminal places; the net's name and subnet membership are not modelled.
- AC1 (no mutation methods exist on the constructed net) and AC2 (collections returned by the net are unmodifiable or copies) are API shape, tested and not proven (kind Q): the model has no method that changes a built net, and a host that changed a returned collection would be changing the net, which line 1 forbids for the builder's own uses only. In TypeScript the returned sets are read-only by type only. The test derivation ('build a net; verify no mutation API exists') is AC1. As in CORE-040 (ruling D99 (a)), these API-shape criteria stay in the markdown unmarked.

**Evidence**

- ✓ **holds** `Libpetri.Spec.CORE_041_reference` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.CORE_041): ✓ The reference builder state machine with the reference net builder satisfies CORE-041: `build` keeps `refNetBuild` of what was added (line 0, with `copyBuilder_view_built`) and later uses never change a kept net (line 1).
  <pre>∀ {N A : Type} [inst : DecidableEq N] (B : TBuilder N A),<br>  CORE_041 B refNetBuild (copyBuilder B)</pre>
- ✗ **forbids** `Libpetri.Spec.CORE_041_forbids_alias` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.CORE_041): ✗ The aliasing builder, the TypeScript builder today, violates CORE-041 (line 1): build a new builder, then declare place 0, and the handle the build returned shows place 0.
  <pre>¬CORE_041 core041B refNetBuild (aliasBuilder core041B)</pre>

<a id="Libpetri-Spec-CORE_042"></a>
## CORE-042: Action Binding Separation

`Libpetri.Spec.CORE_042` · Kind **F** · Scope Java, TypeScript, Rust (net-level bindActions, both forms); Python rides on the Rust binding and exposes no net-level binding · Source **verbatim** (spec/01-core-model.md) · Sign-off **pending** · Statement hash `1c6ac8b527ea189e`

| Natural language | Plain reading | Lean statement |
|---|---|---|
| The net's static structure (places, transitions, arcs, timing, priority) MUST be separable from the runtime behavior (actions).<br><br>A `bindActions()` operation takes a structure and a mapping of transition names to actions, producing a new net with actions bound.<br><br>*When* actions are bound to a net, in either form, the new net *shall* have the name, the places and the terminal places of the original net and, for each transition of the original net, in the same order, a transition with the same name, arcs, output specification, timing and priority.<br><br>*When* actions are bound with a resolver that returns an action for a transition's name, the transition *shall* carry that action in the new net.<br><br>*When* actions are bound with a resolver that returns no action (`null`/`None`) for a transition's name, the transition *shall* carry in the new net the action it carried before.<br><br>*When* actions are bound with a mapping that maps a transition's name to an action, the transition *shall* carry that action in the new net.<br><br>*When* actions are bound with a mapping whose values are actions and that does not map a transition's name, the transition *shall* carry in the new net either the passthrough action or the action it carried before, and an implementation makes the same one of these two choices for every transition, every net and every mapping, so a transition that carried passthrough still carries passthrough.<br><br>Binding actions to a net *shall* return a new net for every net and every resolver or mapping, and *shall* leave the original net unchanged.<br><br>Binding is lazy and total: it never rejects, so a partially bound net is a legitimate intermediate value and an action MAY be bound after instantiation ([MOD-031] AC7); the declared structure is reconciled against the bound behaviour at compile time ([CORE-043]).<br><br>**Divergence:** the map form substitutes passthrough for every transition the map omits in Java and TypeScript (so a second call clobbers the first's bindings) but leaves them untouched in Rust; only the resolver form, where a `null`/`None` result defers a transition, binds in stages identically across implementations.<br><br>In Java a mapping may hold a name with a `null` value, and the map form then defers that transition as the resolver form does; TypeScript substitutes passthrough for a `null` or `undefined` value. | 1. For every resolver-form binding Bind and map-form binding BindMap:<br>2. for every built net b and every resolver r, the net Bind b r and the net BindMap b r each have b's places and b's terminal places, and their transition lists match b's position by position (same length, same order), each transition with b's name and arcs (core), output specification, timing and priority;<br>3. for every b and r, the transition at each position of Bind b r carries the action a whenever r answers that position's name in b with a;<br>4. for every b and r, the transition at each position of Bind b r carries the action b's transition there carried whenever r answers that name with none (defers it);<br>5. for every b and every map m, the transition at each position of BindMap b m carries the action a whenever m maps that position's name in b to a;<br>6. either, for every b and m, the transition at each position of BindMap b m carries passthrough whenever m does not map that name, or, for every b and m, it carries the action b's transition there carried whenever m does not map that name. | <pre>fun {N A} Bind BindMap ↦<br>  (∀ (b : BuiltNet N A) (r : String → Option (Act A)),<br>      ∀ f ∈ [Bind, BindMap],<br>        (f b r).places = b.places ∧<br>          (f b r).terminals = b.terminals ∧<br>            List.Forall₂<br>              (fun d' d ↦<br>                d'.core = d.core ∧<br>                  d'.out = d.out ∧ d'.timing = d.timing ∧ d'.priority = d.priority)<br>              (f b r).trans b.trans) ∧<br>    (∀ (b : BuiltNet N A) (r : String → Option (Act A)),<br> **Assumptions**

- A binding is a function from a built net (BuiltNet: places, transition definitions in declaration order, terminal places; Reference/Build.lean) and a resolver or map to a built net. A resolver and a map are both read as a function from names to an optional action: the resolver's null/None and a name the map does not hold are none. An action is read as its identity tag (Act: the built-in passthrough or another action named by an opaque id); what an action does is CORE-050's and the action model's (W3).
- The lines range over mappings whose values are actions (the body's 'a mapping of transition names to actions', and the quoted line 5 sentence's 'a mapping whose values are actions'). A mapping that holds a name with a null value, which Java's map allows, is outside them and outside every quoted shall sentence: the quoted Java sentence records what the runtimes do with it (Java defers that transition, since getOrDefault returns the held null and the resolver form keeps a transition whose resolver gives null, java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/core/PetriNet.java:202 and :219; TypeScript substitutes passthrough, typescript/src/core/petri-net.ts:80-82; a Rust map holds only actions). Read as none, such a mapping would make Java's map form keep some omitted transitions and clobber others within one call, which line 5 forbids; the line 5 sentence names mappings whose values are actions so that it does not.
- The sentence that binding returns a new net for every net and every resolver or mapping and leaves the original net unchanged is not a line: it holds of every binding in the model, where a binding is a function on immutable values, so it returns a net for every net and every resolver or map and cannot change its argument b; in the runtimes it is tested directly. 'Total, it never rejects' is its first half: it includes a resolver or map that leaves some transitions with passthrough or answers a name that is no transition (that name is never asked for, so it is ignored). 'Lazy' is read as: binding checks nothing, neither comparing a bound action with the transition's output specification nor requiring every transition to be bound, so a partially bound net is a legitimate value, and reconciling it with the declared output specifications is the compile-time check of CORE-043. Binding after instantiation (MOD-031 AC7) and per-instance binding, including an override key that names no transition (ruling D87), are MOD-030's and MOD-031's (W8).
- The lines are stated per position, not per name, so they do not need the shared unique-names assumption (NetNamesDistinct, rulings D10 and D23): with two transitions of one name every runtime asks the resolver once per transition and binds both (java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/core/PetriNet.java:215-229, typescript/src/core/petri-net.ts:92-105, rust/libpetri-core/src/petri_net.rs:187-202), and so does the statement. Under that assumption binding by position is binding by name.
- Line 1 is the body's first sentence: binding changes no field of the static structure. It names the terminal places (EXEC-042) and the output specification, which the body's list '(places, transitions, arcs, timing, priority)' does not: both are static structure and all three runtimes keep them (java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/core/PetriNet.java:228, typescript/src/core/petri-net.ts:104-105, rust/libpetri-core/src/petri_net.rs:165-174). The quoted sentence asks for a transition with the same fields, not the same transition: all three runtimes rebuild a rebound transition through the transition builder (Java and TypeScript rebuildWithAction; Rust rebuild_with_action, rust/libpetri-core/src/petri_net.rs:195-200 and rust/libpetri-core/src/transition.rs:614-643, with a fresh TransitionId), so the identity of a rebound transition (CORE-021) is not kept, and the line compares the fields position by position. The net's name, which the quoted sentence also names, is not a field of BuiltNet; every runtime keeps it (the same three places) and a test checks it outside the model. The subnet membership metadata is kept as MOD-026 says (the mapping survives a re-bind unchanged) and the declared-to-actual place correspondence as MOD-031 says (the rebuild that swaps the action carries it forward); neither is modelled here. A binding that rebuilds a transition and drops its read arcs (CORE_042_forbids_dropReads) violates line 1, and so does one that keeps only what firing reads and resets the priority (CORE_042_mutant_firingView_killed).
- The sentence 'When actions are bound to a net, in either form, a transition that has a match specification ([NU-020]) shall have the same match specification in the new net.' is not quoted by this block and no line here states it; its coverage is deferred to the NU-020 block (W9), which quotes it once a line over the ν-net definition states it. It is outside this model: the match specification (NU-020) is not a field of TransDef but of the ν-net model's definition that extends it (CORE-020's assumes, W9), so no binding on BuiltNet can drop it, and a rebuild that binds the action and drops the match specification has exactly refBind as its shadow on BuiltNet and meets every line here. All three runtimes carry the match specification forward and warn that dropping it would turn a join correlated by name into a plain join (java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/core/PetriNet.java:261-266, typescript/src/core/petri-net.ts:1020-1026, rust/libpetri-core/src/transition.rs:632-634). The sentence is a line over the ν-net definition and is handed to the NU-020 block (W9).
- Lines 2 and 3 are the resolver form, which all three runtimes share: an answered name gets the action, a null/None result defers the transition, which keeps its action. A binding that ignores the resolver (CORE_042_forbids_ignoreResolver) violates line 2, and so does one that binds only transitions still carrying passthrough (CORE_042_mutant_onlyUnbound_killed). A resolver form that replaces a deferred action by passthrough (the map form's Java reading applied to the resolver) violates line 3 (CORE_042_mutant_deferPassthrough_killed).
- Lines 4 and 5 are the map form's common part (ruling D20 (a) on clash core-b#4: the common part, and the divergence recorded). Rust keeps an omitted transition's action (mapKeep, rust/libpetri-core/src/petri_net.rs:177-183) and Java and TypeScript substitute passthrough (mapClobber, java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/core/PetriNet.java:202, typescript/src/core/petri-net.ts:80-82); both readings satisfy the block (CORE_042_reference_keep, CORE_042_reference_clobber) and they differ on a net whose omitted transition carries another action (CORE_042_mapForms_undecided). Line 5 asks for one reading per map form, as each runtime has: every omitted transition of every net carries passthrough, or every one keeps its action. A map form that keeps some omitted transitions and clobbers others meets the per-transition reading and violates line 5 (CORE_042_mutant_perTransition_killed). A map form that ignores the map (CORE_042_forbids_ignoreMap) violates line 4, and so does one whose map binds only transitions still carrying passthrough (CORE_042_mutant_mapOnlyUnbound_killed). Line 5 is stronger than AC4 alone: a map form that resets an omitted transition's action to a fixed other action meets AC4 and violates line 5 (CORE_042_mutant_ac4Only_killed).
- AC1 (a net can be created with no actions, all transitions using passthrough) is the builder default: a transition built without an action carries passthrough (TransIn.resolve, resolve_action_none in Reference/Build.lean), which is CORE-051's line (W3) and is not restated here; CORE_042_nonvacuous starts from such a net.
- AC2 (bindActions(mapping) produces a new net with actions bound by transition name) is line 4 with line 1.
- AC3 (the original net is not modified) is the second half of the quoted sentence that binding leaves the original net unchanged, which holds of every binding in the model (above) and is not a line.
- AC4 (unbound transitions retain the passthrough action) is line 5 on a transition that carried passthrough, and line 3 for the resolver form. The test derivation (bind 2 of 3 transitions, the third still has passthrough) is CORE_042_nonvacuous, for the resolver form and both map readings.
- The paragraph on SubnetDef.bindActions (the same argument forms, keyed by unprefixed names, a new definition) is the operation on a subnet definition, MOD-051's paragraph 'Binding actions on a definition' with its AC8, and is quoted there (W11). The Python binding exposes binding on instances and subnet definitions only (rust/libpetri-py/src/model.rs:667, :893), not on a net; it rides on the Rust binding.

**Evidence**

- ✓ **holds** `Libpetri.Spec.CORE_042_reference_clobber` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.CORE_042): ✓ The reference binding satisfies CORE-042 with the map read as Java and TypeScript read it: an omitted name gets passthrough.
  <pre>∀ {N A : Type}, CORE_042 refBind refBindMapClobber</pre>
- ✓ **holds** `Libpetri.Spec.CORE_042_reference_keep` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.CORE_042): ✓ The reference binding satisfies CORE-042 with the map read as Rust reads it: an omitted name keeps its action.
  <pre>∀ {N A : Type}, CORE_042 refBind refBindMapKeep</pre>
- ✗ **forbids** `Libpetri.Spec.CORE_042_forbids_dropReads` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.CORE_042): ✗ A binding that drops the read arcs when it rebuilds a transition violates CORE-042 (line 1): the example's transition `a` loses its read arc on place 3.
  <pre>¬CORE_042 core042_dropReadsBind refBindMapKeep</pre>
- ✗ **forbids** `Libpetri.Spec.CORE_042_forbids_ignoreMap` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.CORE_042): ✗ A map form that ignores the map violates CORE-042 (line 4): the example's `a` keeps passthrough although the map maps it to action 1.
  <pre>¬CORE_042 refBind core042_ignoreBind</pre>
- ✗ **forbids** `Libpetri.Spec.CORE_042_forbids_ignoreResolver` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.CORE_042): ✗ A binding that ignores the resolver violates CORE-042 (line 2): the example's `a` keeps passthrough although the mapping answers it with action 1.
  <pre>¬CORE_042 core042_ignoreBind refBindMapKeep</pre>
- ? **undecided** `Libpetri.Spec.CORE_042_mapForms_undecided` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.CORE_042): ? The map form's two readings both satisfy CORE-042 and give different nets: binding the example's bound net with a map that holds only `a` keeps `b`'s action 2 under Rust's reading and replaces it by passthrough under Java's and TypeScript's (the spec's documented divergence, clash core-b#4). Which one an implementation follows is not settled by the block.

<a id="Libpetri-Spec-CORE_043"></a>
## CORE-043: Output-Declaring Transitions Must Produce

`Libpetri.Spec.CORE_043` · Kind **F** · Scope every compile step and every verification entry point (state-class graph and SMT), under every property and option setting the entry point accepts · Source **verbatim** (spec/01-core-model.md) · Sign-off **pending** · Statement hash `60f1373540a49a6a`

| Natural language | Plain reading | Lean statement |
|---|---|---|
| *If* a net holds a transition that declares an output spec, a `Timeout`-only spec included, and carries the built-in passthrough action ([CORE-051]), whether bound explicitly, carried because a `bindActions` mapping omitted it ([CORE-042]), or left in place as the builder default, *then* compiling the net *shall* fail with an error that names the first such transition in declaration order.<br><br>*If* no transition of a net both declares an output spec and carries the built-in passthrough action, *then* compiling the net *shall not* fail under this requirement.<br><br>*If* a transition declares no output spec, or carries an action other than the built-in passthrough, a `fork()` action ([CORE-052]) or a hand-written action that produces nothing included, *then* compiling the net *shall not* fail under this requirement naming that transition.<br><br>*When* a net is submitted to a verification entry point (state-class graph or SMT), under any property and option the entry point accepts, the entry point *shall* fail under this requirement exactly when compiling the submitted net does, with an error that names the same transition. | 1. For every compile check C and every verification entry check V, each a function from a built net to none (the check passes) or some name (the check fails naming that transition):<br>2. if the transitions of net b, in declaration order, are l1, then d, then l2, d declares an output specification and carries the built-in passthrough, and no transition of l1 does both, then C b fails naming d;<br>3. if no transition of net b both declares an output specification and carries the built-in passthrough, then C b passes;<br>4. for every net b, V b is C b: the verification entry point fails on exactly the nets compiling fails on, naming the same transition. | <pre>fun {N A} C V ↦<br>  (∀ (b : BuiltNet N A) (l₁ : List (TransDef N A)) (d : TransDef N A)<br>      (l₂ : List (TransDef N A)),<br>      b.trans = l₁ ++ d :: l₂ →<br>        d.out ≠ none →<br>          d.action = Act.passthrough →<br>            (∀ e ∈ l₁, e.out ≠ none → e.action ≠ Act.passthrough) →<br>              C b = some d.core.name) ∧<br>    (∀ (b : BuiltNet N A),<br>        (∀ d ∈ b.trans, d.out ≠ none → d.action ≠ Act.passthrough) → C b = none) ∧<br>      ∀ (b : BuiltNet N A), V b = C b</pre> |

**Assumptions**

- A compile check (C) is the CORE-043 check of one implementation's compile step, read as a function of the built net: none when the check passes, some n when it fails (a panic or an exception) with an error naming transition n. A verification entry check (V) is the same check at one verification entry point of that implementation under one property and one option setting the entry point accepts: the state-class-graph entry point and the SMT entry point are each their own V, each setting gives its own V, and the block holds for every such V (CORE_043 C V once per entry point and setting). Other reasons a compile step or a verifier may refuse a net are not this block's subject. The message bytes are not stated: they differ by one word across the runtimes (rust/libpetri-core/src/petri_net.rs:792-799 and typescript/src/core/internal/output-action-check.ts:13-19 against java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/core/internal/OutputActionCheck.java:32-36); only that the error names the transition is stated, read as the returned name.
- An action is read as its identity tag (Act): the built-in passthrough or another action named by an opaque id. That the built-in is one stable instance and that the identity predicate accepts it and rejects every other action is CORE-051's (line 3 of its AC list); this block reads 'carries the built-in passthrough' as action = passthrough. The third quoted sentence is lines 1 and 2 together, under the shared unique-names assumption (ruling D23): a transition that declares no output specification, or carries fork(), a hand-written action that produces nothing or any other action than the built-in, is no offender, so either the net has no offender and line 2 passes it, or line 1 names the first offender, which is another transition with another name (core043_nonOffender_unnamed, through core043_pin: the three lines determine both checks). Without unique names a non-offender that shares the first offender's name gets the same returned name, which no check over names can tell apart; the lines themselves need no unique-names premise. CORE_043_nonvacuous checks a sink, a fork()-bound and a no-op transition together, alone and next to an offender; CORE_043_forbids_extensional kills the check that also refuses the hand-written one.
- 'Declares an output spec' is read as 'has an output specification' (out is not none): an empty And or Xor cannot be built (rust/libpetri-core/src/output.rs:47, java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/core/Arc.java:274-275, typescript/src/core/out.ts:68-69), so 'non-empty output spec' (AC1) and 'output spec' name the same transitions. A Timeout-only spec, Timeout(d, ForwardInput(P, Q)), is an output specification like any other: the ForwardInput branch is deposited by the executor on the timeout outcome (IO-014), which passthrough never reaches, and line 1 does not exempt it (CORE_043_mutant_timeoutExempt_killed).
- 'The first such transition in declaration order' is the order of the built net's transitions, the order in which they were added (CORE-040, ruling D32). All three runtimes walk the net's transitions and throw on the first offender (rust/libpetri-runtime/src/compiled_net.rs:66, java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/runtime/CompiledNet.java:101, typescript/src/runtime/compiled-net.ts:80). A check that names another offender violates line 1: the last one (CORE_043_mutant_someOffender_killed), or the one with the least name, as a walk over the transitions sorted by name would (CORE_043_forbids_nameSorted); core043_netTwo declares its offenders b then a, so both are told apart from the first. Every transition is checked, a source with no input arc included: a check placed inside the walk over input arcs skips sources and violates line 1 (CORE_043_forbids_skipSource). Transitions are identified by name (ruling D10, with the shared unique-names assumption of ruling D23).
- The lines range over every built net, including one no builder produced; the check reads only each transition's name, output specification and action, so a net a host can submit (one that holds only builder outputs, BuiltNet.FromBuilder) is one case of them. How a transition came to carry passthrough plays no part: the check reads the net handed to the compile step, after the builder default (CORE-051), either bindActions form (CORE-042: refBind with a resolver; mapKeep, where an omitted transition keeps its prior action, which is passthrough when it was never bound; mapClobber, where an omitted transition gets passthrough), binding on a subnet definition (MOD-051), per-instance binding (MOD-030) and channel merge (MOD-021). The first quoted sentence's 'carried because a bindActions mapping omitted it' covers both map forms. The theorems core043_builderDefault and core043_mapOmitted show the builder default and the mapClobber substitution reaching the reference check; subnet binding, per-instance binding and channel merge are the composition model's (W8), which rebuilds through the builder, so the lines already range over the nets it builds and their evidence is W8's.
- The verification entry point is checked against the net submitted to it, under every property and option setting it accepts. A net the verifier derives from it, such as the in-flight split of VER-004 and NU-052 under PrioritySemantics CONFLICT (whose start half keeps a sink's name and action and gains an output place), is not the submitted net and is not checked under this requirement. Checking such a derived net is a verifier defect in all three runtimes and in Python, not a reading of line 3: the user kept line 3 as a MUST and recorded the defect for a runtime fix (RD-08 in spec/runtime-defects.md; the fix runs the check once, on the submitted net, before any rewrite). TypeScript runs the check after prepare() on the split net (typescript/src/verification/smt-verifier.ts:1215-1216); Java builds the state-class graph on the split net (java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/smt/SmtVerifier.java:1885-1888), whose initial class checks again (java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/analysis/StateClassGraph.java:630); Rust runs the whole pipeline on the split net (rust/libpetri-verification/src/smt_verifier.rs:872-879), whose start half keeps the sink's action and gains the in-flight output (rust/libpetri-verification/src/in_flight.rs:390-403), and checks it again in verify_name_scg (rust/libpetri-verification/src/nu_scg_verifier.rs:277) and StateClassGraph::build_core (rust/libpetri-verification/src/state_class_graph.rs:160), and its error then says the sink declares an output spec, which it does not; the Python binding rides on Rust. So a net that compiles is refused under CONFLICT in every runtime. The environment transitions of a VER-022 contract are not transitions of the submitted net (spec/07-verification.md:2160-2161) and are not checked. Until the verifier model (W10) exists, the reference entry check is refVerifyEntry = refCompile (refVerifyEntry_eq), so line 3's holds evidence is true by definition today; W10 replaces refVerifyEntry with its modelled entry check and proves line 3 for it.
- The body's 'compiling or verifying such a net MUST fail' is lines 1 and 3; 'one check there covers the builder default, either bindActions form, binding on a subnet definition, per-instance binding and channel merge alike' is the reading above that the check reads the net, not the binding. 'Such a transition can never fire usefully' is a consequence: an output specification never offers an empty deposit to an action outcome (core043_no_empty_action_deposit, every branch names a place: branches_ne_nil_mem), so under IO-015 the empty output of passthrough fails validation on every firing (IO_015_ac6); on a net that passes the check, a transition carrying passthrough has no output specification and its empty deposit is the one its spec offers (core043_passthrough_sink). 'Verification does not compensate' and 'the rule is unconditional' (it does not depend on the CONC-026 validation opt-out) are why the check exists, not further lines: the check reads no executor option.
- AC1 (compiling errors when a transition with a non-empty output spec carries passthrough, bound explicitly, substituted by a bindActions mapping or left as the builder default, a Timeout-only spec included) is line 1, with the readings above; a compile step that never refuses (a check made at bind time only, which misses the builder default) violates it (CORE_043_forbids_bindTimeOnly), and so does one that exempts a Timeout-only spec (CORE_043_mutant_timeoutExempt_killed) or skips a source transition (CORE_043_forbids_skipSource). CORE_043_nonvacuous computes the four cases of the test derivation on the reference, and a source transition.
- AC2 (the error names the offending transition, the first one in declaration order when there are several) is line 1's 'fails naming d'.
- AC3 (submitting the same net to a verification entry point fails the same way) is line 3, once per entry point and option setting; a verification entry point that never refuses violates it (CORE_043_forbids_verifyNever), and so do the readings 'refuses at least the nets compiling refuses' (CORE_043_mutant_verifyCovers_killed) and 'refuses the same nets, naming any transition' (CORE_043_mutant_sameNets_killed).
- AC4 (a sink may carry passthrough; CORE-042 is untouched) is line 2 on a net whose transitions carrying passthrough have no output specification, and the third quoted sentence on a net that also holds an offender. That binding stays lazy and total is CORE-042's line, not restated here.
- AC5 (the built-in is recognised by identity, so a hand-written action that produces nothing is not claimed) is line 2 and the third quoted sentence read over the identity tag; the extensional reading of the whole check (an output-declaring transition is refused when its action produces nothing) is CORE_043_mutant_extensional, killed by the extensional check. That such an action fails at run time is IO-015's.

**Evidence**

- ✓ **holds** `Libpetri.Spec.CORE_043_reference` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.CORE_043): ✓ The reference checks satisfy CORE-043: `refCompile` names the first transition in declaration order that declares an output specification and carries passthrough, passes a net without one, and `refVerifyEntry` is `refCompile`.
  <pre>∀ {N A : Type}, CORE_043 refCompile refVerifyEntry</pre>
- ✗ **forbids** `Libpetri.Spec.CORE_043_forbids_bindTimeOnly` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.CORE_043): ✗ A compile step that never refuses (the check at bind time only) violates CORE-043 (line 1, AC1): the net whose transition carries the builder default compiles.
  <pre>¬CORE_043 core043_never core043_never</pre>
- ✗ **forbids** `Libpetri.Spec.CORE_043_forbids_extensional` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.CORE_043): ✗ The extensional check violates CORE-043 (line 2, AC5): it refuses the net whose output-declaring transitions carry `fork` and a hand-written no-op.
  <pre>¬CORE_043 (core043_extCompile core043_isNoop) (core043_extCompile core043_isNoop)</pre>
- ✗ **forbids** `Libpetri.Spec.CORE_043_forbids_nameSorted` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.CORE_043): ✗ The name-sorted check violates CORE-043 (line 1, AC2): of the offenders declared `b` then `a` it names `a`, the least name, not the first.
  <pre>¬CORE_043 core043_nameSorted core043_nameSorted</pre>
- ✗ **forbids** `Libpetri.Spec.CORE_043_forbids_skipSource` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.CORE_043): ✗ The check that skips source transitions violates CORE-043 (line 1, AC1): the net of the source `src`, which declares `Place(q)` and carries the builder default, compiles.
