<a id="Libpetri-Spec-CORE_050"></a>
## CORE-050: Transition Action

`Libpetri.Spec.CORE_050` · Kind **B** · Scope all executors · Source **verbatim** (spec/01-core-model.md) · Sign-off **pending** · Statement hash `0e01354c5393cdc4`

| Natural language | Plain reading | Lean statement |
|---|---|---|
| *When* a transition fires, its action *shall* receive a transition context holding the tokens the firing consumed from each input place and the tokens its read arcs read ([EXEC-010], [EXEC-012]).<br><br>*When* a firing ends with the completion of its action, the firing *shall* deposit exactly the output tokens the action completed with, whether the action wrote them through the context or returned them.<br><br>*If* the executor admits the completion of a firing's action ([EXEC-020]), the transition has no match specification ([NU-020]) and the output tokens fill one output branch ([IO-015]), *then* the firing *shall* end with that completion. | 1. Let Q be the queue firings (Q t M δ e M': t fires from the queue marking M, delivers δ to its action, emits e and leaves M') and AF the action firings (AF a t M δ e M': such a firing under the action a that ends with the completion of a, which emitted e).<br>2. For every action a, transition t, delivery δ and emission e: every firing in AF a is a firing in Q with the same delivery, emission and markings, so the action receives exactly what the firing delivers.<br>3. For every action a, transition t, delivery δ and emission e: if AF a has a firing of t delivering δ and emitting e, then a completes with e on t and δ.<br>4. For every action a, transition t, delivery δ and emission e whose places, in emission order, are one output branch of t and that a completes with on t and δ: every firing of t in Q delivering δ and emitting e is a firing in AF a. | <pre>fun {N T} [DecidableEq N] Q AF ↦<br>  (∀ (a : ActionRel N T) (t : Reference.Trans N) (δ : Delivered N T) (e : List (N × T)),<br>      on fun M M' ↦ AF a t M δ e M', shall fun M M' ↦ Q t M δ e M') ∧<br>    (∀ (a : ActionRel N T) (t : Reference.Trans N) (δ : Delivered N T) (e : List (N × T)),<br>        on fun M M' ↦ AF a t M δ e M', shall fun x x_1 ↦ a t δ (Except.ok e)) ∧<br>      ∀ (a : ActionRel N T) (t : Reference.Trans N) (δ : Delivered N T)<br>        (e : List (N × T)),<br>        OutputBranch t (List.map Prod.fst e) →<br>          a t δ (Except.ok e) →<br>            on fun M M' ↦ Q t M δ e M', shall fun M M' ↦ AF a t M δ e M'</pre> |

**Assumptions**

- The model is the pair (Q, AF). Q is the queue firing relation (QFireRel, Spec/GlossaryQueue.lean; glossary: Queue order): Q t M δ e M' says that t fires from the queue marking M, delivers δ to its action (the tokens it consumed from each input place and the tokens its read arcs read, Delivered), emits e (places and tokens, in emission order) and leaves M'. AF is the action firing relation (ActFireRel, Spec/GlossaryAction.lean): AF a t M δ e M' is a firing of t under the action a that ends with the completion of a, which emitted e. A plain QFireRel cannot carry AF: it does not record how a firing ended, and a firing that ends with the timeout outcome deposits tokens no action produced (IO-013). The witness pair is RefQFire and refActionFire, the reference queue firings whose emission fills one output branch and that the action completes with.
- An action (glossary: Action; ActionRel in Spec/GlossaryAction.lean) is a relation from a transition and the delivery to how the action ends: completing with an emission or failing with a message (EXEC-030). It is a relation, not a function, because an action may read the world. The transition context is read as the delivery δ; its accessors (input, inputs, inputToken, read, output) are CORE-060 to CORE-063's, stated over the same delivery.
- Line 1 reads the first sentence as 'the action receives what the firing delivers': the delivery of a firing in AF is that of a firing in Q. Which tokens Q delivers is EXEC-010's second line (from each input place, its consumed oldest tokens) and EXEC-012 (one head per read arc), stated over the same Q in the joint model; CORE-050 does not restate them. An executor that hands the action every token of each input place violates line 1 against the reference Q (CORE_050_mutant_wholePlaces_killed).
- Line 2 reads the second sentence: the emission of a firing in AF a is one a completes with on that delivery, and the firing in Q (line 1) deposits exactly that emission; 'exactly' is Q's effect rule (EXEC-020: appended at the tail, in emission order; CORE-035). An executor that deposits tokens of its own in the places the action wrote violates it (CORE_050_mutant_placesOnly_killed), and so does one that counts a timed-out firing as a firing that ends with an action that never completes (CORE_050_forbids_timeout). Whether the action wrote its tokens through the context or returned them, they reach the firing as the emission it completes with; the context's output buffer is CORE-062's.
- Line 3 reads the third sentence. The model has no stop, no immediate termination and no Timeout budget, so 'the executor admits the completion' is read as 'the action completes': an admitted completion is never that of a firing that ended with its timeout outcome or that a stop on a terminal place or an immediate termination abandoned (glossary: Admitted completion; EXEC-020), and which completions the executor admits is the executor model's (RefExec). A transition of the model has no match specification (Trans, ruling D16), which is the sentence's scope: on a correlated join the relay check of NU-054 may reject a completion that fills a branch (EXEC-021). An executor whose firings never end with their action violates the line (CORE_050_mutant_soundOnly_killed: the first draft, lines 1 and 2 alone, held of it).
- Line 3 is stated on the granularity of the reference: the places of the emission, in emission order, are one output branch as Out.branches lists it (glossary: Output branch, one token per place, the IO-016 convention). RefQFire compares the emitted places with an offered deposit as a list, so a completion that fills a branch with its places in another order, or that puts more than one token in a place of a branch, is no firing of RefQFire, and line 3 says nothing of it. That such a completion passes validation and deposits in the order the action produced its tokens is IO-015's set comparison and EXEC-020, stated at count level.
- Line 3 is relative to Q, so CORE-050 alone holds of the empty pair. In the joint model Q covers every reference firing (QCovers) and delivers the reference delivery (EXEC-010, EXEC-012), so every completion with an output branch of an enabled transition is a firing in AF (core050_fires), every firing in AF, counted, is a firing of the count semantics (core050_projects), and every firing in Q ends with the completion of an action or with IO-013's timeout outcome (core050_endsBy).
- Ruling D17: 'ends with the completion of its action' is the admitted completion (glossary: Admitted completion). A completion that is not admitted (after the timeout outcome, a stop on a terminal place, an immediate termination) is not one line 2 speaks of. AF a holds a tuple only if a completes with its emission on its delivery (line 2), so an action that fails ends no firing in AF (EXEC-030), and an executor that counts a failed action as completing with no token violates line 2 (CORE_050_forbids_failAsEmpty). A tuple does not record how the firing ended: the child of a Timeout node is also an action branch, so the tuple of a firing that ended with the timeout outcome is in AF a whenever a can complete with the same emission (core050_timeout_overlap), and EndsByActionOrTimeout is a cover, not a partition; CORE_050_forbids_timeout therefore uses an action that never completes. Tokens an action publishes before it completes (the IO-015 flush, Rust and Python) are not in the atomic model, as in EXEC-020. The ν-correlated inputs of NU-020 are not modelled: RefQFire consumes oldest first from every input place (ruling D16).
- Q models an executor with output validation enabled, the default (CONC-026), as RefQFire does: a completion whose emission fills no output branch ends no firing (EXEC-021). The deposit of the action's write under the validation skip is CONC-026's.
- A built transition carries its action as an identity tag (Act, CORE-020); the action a tag names is Act.interp I, the passthrough tag naming the action that completes with no token (CORE-051). By line 2 a firing under the passthrough tag deposits nothing (core050_passthrough_nil), the firing-level fact CORE-043 rests on (passthrough_never_offered).
- AC1 (the action receives a context with consumed input tokens and read token values) is line 1 together with EXEC-010 and EXEC-012 on the same Q; the context's accessors are CORE-060 and CORE-061.
- AC2 (the action produces output tokens via the context or a return value) is line 2: through either channel the tokens are the emission the action completes with. That both channels exist is API shape.
- AC3 (the action is asynchronous: it returns a future, a promise or a completion stage) is API shape, a Q-kind test, not encoded. That an action starts at one step and completes at a later one is CONC-002's, over the executor model (RefExec).
- The test derivation (an action that reads its input, transforms it and produces output) is CORE_050_nonvacuous: an action that doubles the value it is handed, fired on a place holding 7 then 8, receives the oldest token 7 and the firing deposits 14.

  <pre>∀ {N T : Type} [inst : DecidableEq N], CORE_050 RefQFire refActionFire</pre>

  <pre>¬CORE_050 RefQFire core050_failAsEmpty</pre>
- ✗ **forbids** `Libpetri.Spec.CORE_050_forbids_timeout` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.CORE_050): ✗ It violates line 2: on `Timeout(Place 1)` under an action that never completes, its timed-out firing deposits a token 99 the action did not produce.

<a id="Libpetri-Spec-CORE_051"></a>
## CORE-051: Passthrough Action

`Libpetri.Spec.CORE_051` · Kind **F** · Scope all implementations · Source **verbatim** (spec/01-core-model.md) · Sign-off **pending** · Statement hash `c0c0369f056e10a2`

| Natural language | Plain reading | Lean statement |
|---|---|---|
| *When* a transition fires under the built-in passthrough action, the action *shall* complete with no output token and *shall not* fail.<br><br>The identity predicate *shall* accept the built-in passthrough action and reject every other action, including `fork()` ([CORE-052]) and a hand-written action that produces no token.<br><br>*When* a transition is built without an action, the built transition *shall* carry the built-in passthrough action.<br><br>Every retrieval of the built-in passthrough action *shall* yield the same instance, which the identity predicate accepts. | 1. Let interp be the action each identity tag names, isPT the identity predicate, B the transition builder and pt k the k-th retrieval of the built-in.<br>2. For every transition t, delivery δ and outcome r: the passthrough tag ends with r on t and δ exactly when r is completion with no token.<br>3. For every tag x: isPT x holds exactly when x is the passthrough tag.<br>4. For every call k on an input i that gives no action: if the call returns an instance x, the definition of x carries the passthrough tag.<br>5. For all retrievals k and j: pt k equals pt j, and isPT holds of pt k. | <pre>fun {N T A} interp isPT B pt ↦<br>  (∀ (t : Reference.Trans N) (δ : Delivered N T) (r : Except String (List (N × T))),<br>      interp Act.passthrough t δ r ↔ r = Except.ok []) ∧<br>    (∀ (x : Act A), isPT x = true ↔ x = Act.passthrough) ∧<br>      (∀ (k : ℕ) (i : TransIn N A) (x : B.I),<br>          B.build k i = Except.ok x →<br>            i.action = none → (B.defOf x).action = Act.passthrough) ∧<br>        ∀ (k j : ℕ), pt k = pt j ∧ isPT (pt k) = true</pre> |

**Assumptions**

- The model is the tuple (interp, isPT, B, pt). An action is read as its identity tag (Act, Reference/Build.lean): the built-in passthrough or another action named by an opaque id; this is the tag CORE-020, CORE-042 and CORE-043 carry on a built transition (TransDef). interp tag is the action relation (ActionRel, Spec/GlossaryAction.lean) the tag names; the reference is Act.interp I, the passthrough tag naming refPassthrough and other x naming I x, for every table I of other actions. isPT is the identity predicate on tags; the reference is Act.isPassthrough, the predicate the CORE-043 compile check reads (refCompile). B is CORE-020's transition builder (TBuilder); the reference is refTransBuild. pt k is the tag the k-th retrieval of the built-in returns (Rust passthrough(), Java TransitionAction.passthrough(), TypeScript passthrough(), Python libpetri.passthrough); the reference is refRetrievePassthrough.
- Two actions are the same instance exactly when their tags are equal. A runtime action is an object compared by reference (Rust Arc::ptr_eq, rust/libpetri-core/src/action.rs:75-77; Java ==, java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/core/TransitionAction.java:65-67; TypeScript ===, typescript/src/core/transition-action.ts:32-34); a fresh closure per retrieval is a fresh tag (CORE_051_forbids_freshPerRetrieval). Python's built-in is the enum member BuiltinAction.Passthrough, mapped to Rust's singleton (rust/libpetri-py/src/model.rs:238-243), so Python carries the tag itself; a Python callable that produces nothing is another action. Python exposes no identity predicate; line 2 is read there through the Rust one the compile check calls.
- An explicitly bound null or undefined is not an action and is outside the model: the model's only absent action is TransIn.action = none, Rust cannot express a null action, and Python's builder raises TypeError on one (rust/libpetri-py/src/model.rs:276-287). Java's Transition.Builder.action(null) and TypeScript's action(null) store it (java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/core/Transition.java:367-370, typescript/src/core/transition.ts:222-225); the identity predicate rejects it, so CORE-043's check passes such a transition and every firing then fails. That acceptance is recorded as a Java and TypeScript builder defect (RD-06 in spec/runtime-defects.md: the setter should reject null as Python does), not read as 'built without an action', and line 3 is not weakened for it.
- Line 1 reads the first sentence at the level of the action: on every transition and delivery the passthrough tag completes, with no token, and has no other outcome, so it never fails (rust/libpetri-core/src/action.rs:86-88 returns Ok(()), java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/core/TransitionAction.java:80-81 returns a completed future, typescript/src/core/transition-action.ts:24 is async () => {}; Python runs Rust's Passthrough, rust/libpetri-py/src/model.rs:238-243). A passthrough that copies its input token to every output place is fork() (CORE-052): it agrees with passthrough on a sink and violates line 1 on a transition with an output place (CORE_051_mutant_sinkOnly_killed); a passthrough that fails violates it on every delivery (CORE_051_forbids_failing). That a firing under the passthrough tag deposits nothing is line 1 with CORE-050's line 2 (core051_fire_nil), and that a transition built without an action deposits nothing when a firing ends with its action is line 3 on top (core051_default_fire_nil).
- The body's 'consumes input tokens' describes the firing, not the action: what a firing consumes is CORE-030's and EXEC-010's, whatever its action. 'Completes immediately' (AC1) is line 1 for 'completes'. 'Immediately' (no task dispatch, the action runs inline on the orchestrator thread) is a claim about thread placement, kind Q: the Lean model has no threads, so no Lean block states it, and it is checked by tests (CONC-011 AC1, 'Passthrough actions execute inline without task dispatch').
- Line 2 reads 'recognisable by identity' as an exact characterisation over tags: the predicate accepts the built-in and rejects every other tag, whatever that action does. An extensional predicate that also accepts a hand-written action producing no token violates it (CORE_051_mutant_acceptsBuiltin_killed). fork() is rejected because its tag is not the passthrough tag: on a one-place self-loop that delivers one token, an action satisfying CORE-052 emits a copy of it, while line 1 allows the passthrough tag no token there, so the tag of every fork satisfying CORE-052 differs from the passthrough tag and line 2 rejects it (core051_fork_ne); at the example table, other fork names the reference fork refFork (core051_reference_fork). Every predicate satisfying line 2 is Act.isPassthrough (core051_isPT_eq), so CORE-043's check, stated over action = passthrough, reads the same nets under any such predicate.
- Line 3 reads the body's 'This is the default action for transitions without explicitly bound actions' at build time: a transition built without an action carries the built-in (rust/libpetri-core/src/transition.rs:256, java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/core/Transition.java:247, typescript/src/core/transition.ts:152, and Python's builder rust/libpetri-py/src/model.rs:421-424, None => passthrough()). Line 3 is conditional on a successful build; that a transition given no action builds at all is CORE-020's line 4, and with it such a transition exists and carries the built-in (core051_default_builds). A builder that requires an action fails every build without one, satisfies line 3 vacuously, and is rejected by CORE-020's line 4 (core051_requiredAction_joint). Binding later (bindActions) is CORE-042's, which keeps the tag of an unbound transition. A builder whose default is a hand-written no-op behaves the same at every firing and violates the line (CORE_051_mutant_behaviouralDefault_killed): CORE-043's check would then miss an output-declaring transition left at the default.
- Line 4 reads 'a stable singleton rather than a fresh closure per call' and the first half of AC3: every retrieval yields one instance and the predicate accepts it. A retrieval whose first call returns the built-in and whose later calls return fresh actions violates it (CORE_051_mutant_firstRetrieval_killed), and so does one that returns a fresh action on every call (CORE_051_forbids_freshPerRetrieval). By line 2, line 4 says every retrieval is the passthrough tag (core051_pt_eq). Python's retrieval is the module constant libpetri.passthrough (python/libpetri/model.py:23, the enum member BuiltinAction.Passthrough), so every access yields the same instance and line 4 holds there by construction.
- AC1 (passthrough action completes immediately) is line 1 for 'completes'; 'immediately' is left to tests (CONC-011 AC1) as above.
- AC2 (no output tokens are produced) is line 1: the only outcome is completion with no token.
- AC3 (repeated retrieval yields the same instance, and an identity predicate accepts the built-in and rejects every other action, including fork()) is lines 4 and 2, with core051_fork_ne for fork().
- The test derivation (fire a sink transition with passthrough and see no output token; retrieve the built-in twice and see identity) is CORE_051_nonvacuous: the reference action firing of a sink under the passthrough tag deposits nothing, two retrievals are equal and accepted, and the predicate rejects fork() and a hand-written no-op.

**Evidence**

- ✓ **holds** `Libpetri.Spec.CORE_051_reference` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.CORE_051): ✓ The reference satisfies CORE-051 (`core051_reference_table` at the table that knows nothing about the other actions).
  <pre>∀ {N T A : Type} [inst : DecidableEq N] [inst_1 : ToString N],<br>  CORE_051 (Act.interp refAnyAction) Act.isPassthrough refTransBuild<br>    refRetrievePassthrough</pre>
- ✗ **forbids** `Libpetri.Spec.CORE_051_forbids_failing` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.CORE_051): ✗ A passthrough that fails violates CORE-051 (line 1): on the sink delivery it does not complete with no token.
  <pre>¬CORE_051 core051_failInterp Act.isPassthrough refTransBuild refRetrievePassthrough</pre>
- ✗ **forbids** `Libpetri.Spec.CORE_051_forbids_freshPerRetrieval` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.CORE_051): ✗ A fresh action per retrieval violates CORE-051 (line 4): the first retrieval is not the second, and the identity predicate rejects both.
  <pre>¬CORE_051 (Act.interp core051_I) Act.isPassthrough refTransBuild core051_freshPT</pre>
- ✗ **mutant** `Libpetri.Spec.CORE_051_mutant_acceptsBuiltin_killed` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.CORE_051): ✗ The extensional predicate kills the mutant: it accepts the built-in, but it also accepts the hand-written no-op, which is not the built-in (line 2).
  <pre>CORE_051_mutant_acceptsBuiltin (Act.interp core051_I) core051_extIsPT refTransBuild<br>    refRetrievePassthrough ∧<br>  ¬CORE_051 (Act.interp core051_I) core051_extIsPT refTransBuild refRetrievePassthrough</pre>
- ✗ **mutant** `Libpetri.Spec.CORE_051_mutant_behaviouralDefault_killed` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.CORE_051): ✗ The no-op default kills the mutant: the default behaves as passthrough on every delivery, but the sink built without an action carries `other "noop"`, not the built-in (line 3), so the CORE-043 check would not see it.

- ✗ **mutant** `Libpetri.Spec.CORE_051_mutant_firstRetrieval_killed` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.CORE_051): ✗ The first-call singleton kills the mutant: the first retrieval is the built-in, but the second is a fresh action, not the same instance (line 4).

- ✗ **mutant** `Libpetri.Spec.CORE_051_mutant_sinkOnly_killed` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.CORE_051): ✗ The copying passthrough kills the mutant: on a sink it emits nothing, but on `u` (input place 0, output `Place 1`) it emits the delivered 7 in place 1 (line 1).

<a id="Libpetri-Spec-CORE_052"></a>
## CORE-052: Fork Action

`Libpetri.Spec.CORE_052` · Kind **F** · Scope all implementations (the built-in fork action; Python rides on the Rust action) · Source **verbatim** (spec/01-core-model.md) · Sign-off **pending** · Statement hash `b67572cce63eec54`

| Natural language | Plain reading | Lean statement |
|---|---|---|
| A built-in fork action that copies a single input token value to all declared output places.<br><br>*When* the fork action runs for a transition with exactly one input place and the firing consumed exactly one token from that place, the action *shall* complete with one token carrying that token's value in every place the output spec names and with no token in any other place.<br><br>*If* the transition does not have exactly one input place, *then* the fork action *shall* fail.<br><br>*When* the firing consumed two or more tokens from the single input place, the fork action *shall* either fail or complete with one token carrying the oldest consumed token's value in every place the output spec names and with no token in any other place.<br><br>**Divergence:** when the firing consumed two or more tokens from the single input place, the fork action copies the oldest consumed token to every output place in Java, Rust and Python and fails in TypeScript.<br><br>**Note:** The fork action writes every place the output spec names, so on an output spec `Xor(a, b)` with two different places it writes both, and an executor with output validation enabled rejects its completion ([IO-015], [EXEC-021]). | 1. For every value projection val and every fork action function Fork, for every transition t and every delivery δ:<br>2. for every place i and token x, if i is the sole input place of t (the input places of t, as a set, are {i}) and δ delivers exactly [x] from i, then Fork t δ completes with an emission e such that, for every place p, the values of the tokens e sends to p are [val x] if t's output spec names p and [] otherwise;<br>3. if t has no sole input place (it has none, or two or more) and every input place of t delivered at least one token in δ, then Fork t δ fails with some message;<br>4. for every place i and tokens x, y, ys, if i is the sole input place of t and δ delivers x :: y :: ys from i (x the oldest), then Fork t δ either fails with some message or completes with an emission e such that, for every place p, the values of the tokens e sends to p are [val x] if t's output spec names p and [] otherwise. | <pre>fun {N T V} [DecidableEq N] val Fork ↦<br>  ∀ (t : Reference.Trans N) (δ : Delivered N T),<br>    (∀ (i : N) (x : T),<br>        core052_soleInput t i →<br>          δ.inputs i = [x] →<br>            ∃ e,<br>              Fork t δ = Except.ok e ∧<br>                ∀ (p : N),<br>                  List.map val (EmittedTo e p) = if OutputArc t p then [val x] else []) ∧<br>      ((¬∃ i, core052_soleInput t i) →<br>          (∀ p ∈ inPlaces t, δ.inputs p ≠ []) → ∃ msg, Fork t δ = Except.error msg) ∧<br>        ∀ (i : N) (x y : T) (ys : List T),<br>          core052_soleInput t i →<br>            δ.inputs i = x :: y :: ys →<br>              (∃ msg, Fork t δ = Except.error msg) ∨<br>                ∃ e,<br>                  Fork t δ = Except.ok e ∧<br>                    ∀ (p : N),<br>                      List.map val (EmittedTo e p) = if OutputArc t p then [val x] else []</pre> |

**Assumptions**

- The fork action is read as an action function (ActionFn, Spec/GlossaryAction.lean): from the transition and the delivery δ (the consumed tokens per input place in consumption order, oldest first, and the read tokens per read place) to a completion with an emission (places and tokens, in emission order) or a failure. It reads nothing else, so a function, not a relation. Where the tokens it completes with go is CORE-050's line 2 (the firing deposits exactly them, AF := refActionFire with the action ActionFn.rel Fork).
- Values, not tokens: val x is the value a token carries (CORE-003's projection; none for a unit token when V is an Option). Every runtime deposits a new token with a fresh created_at carrying the consumed value (Rust epoch_now in the output path, Java and TypeScript ctx.output), so lines 1 and 3 compare (EmittedTo e p).map val with [val x]. A fork that emits the consumed token itself (refFork) and one that emits a new token with the same value (CORE_052_allows_freshStamp) both satisfy them; a fork that emits another value violates them (CORE_052_forbids_otherValue).
- 'Exactly one input place' is a set condition (core052_soleInput): the input places are the places of t's input arcs, read and reset arcs excluded. Java and TypeScript count the declared input places (ctx.inputPlaces()); Rust counts input_place_names, the keys of the consumed-input map, which are the input places that delivered a token. The two counts agree on every delivery in which each input place delivered at least one token, and every firing is such a delivery (IO-002, IO-004 AC1: every input arc requires at least one token). Line 2 is stated for those deliveries only, so a fork that counts as Rust does satisfies the block (CORE_052_allows_rustCount). Lines 1 and 3 need no such premise: the sole input place delivered there. A transition with two input arcs on one place is rejected when it is built (CORE-030) and is covered by the set reading either way.
- 'Every place the output spec names' is OutputArc (glossary: Output arc; IO-017's set): every place of the spec, Xor alternatives, the Timeout child and ForwardInput targets included (Rust output_place_names over allowed_outputs, Java Transition.outputPlaces, TypeScript ctx.outputPlaces()). A transition without an output spec names no place, so fork completes with no token there. Lines 1 and 3 compare per place, not as a list: Rust iterates a HashSet of output places, so the emission order is not fixed and the block does not fix it.
- Line 1 has three parts, each with a wrong fork that meets a plausible weaker reading: every output place gets a copy (the fork that writes only the first output place meets 'tokens only in output places, carrying the value', CORE_052_mutant_onlyOutputs_killed); exactly one copy (a fork that writes two copies meets the old AC2, 'produces the input value to all output places', CORE_052_mutant_ac2Literal_killed_double); and nothing elsewhere (a fork that also writes back to its input place meets the same reading, CORE_052_mutant_ac2Literal_killed_echo). AC2 is reworded to state the three parts.
- Line 2 includes zero input places: AC1 says 'requires exactly one input place', and all three runtimes fail on any count other than one (rust/libpetri-core/src/action.rs Fork::run_sync, java TransitionAction.fork, typescript transition-action.ts fork), with the message 'Fork requires exactly 1 input place, found n'. AC3 said 'more than one input place' and is reworded to 'not exactly one' under ruling D20 (R-CB6). A fork that completes with no token on a transition without input places meets AC3's old wording and violates line 2 (CORE_052_mutant_ac3Literal_killed); a fork that accepts two input places and copies the first violates it too (CORE_052_forbids_acceptTwo). The message text is not stated.
- Ruling D50 (a): line 1 is stated for a firing that consumed exactly one token from the sole input place, and the batch case (two or more, from an Exactly(n), All or AtLeast input) is left undecided between the runtimes' two behaviours: Java and Rust copy the oldest consumed token (Java ctx.input returns the first token of the batch, Rust's fork reads input_raw, which takes the first token), Python rides on Rust, and TypeScript fails (ctx.input throws on a count other than one). Both satisfy the block (CORE_052_reference, CORE_052_reference_strict) and differ on a batch (CORE_052_batch_undecided); the spec records which runtime does which in its Divergence note. Line 3 changes no runtime and picks neither: it only excludes what neither runtime does and what the headline 'copies a single input token value' excludes, a fork that copies every token of the batch and one that copies the newest (CORE_052_mutant_noBatch_killed_all, CORE_052_mutant_noBatch_killed_newest). AC4 states line 3.
- The same option (exactly-one premise, batch undecided) is taken for input() in CORE-060. The runtimes' batch behaviour differs between the two in Rust and Python, where fork reads input_raw (the oldest token) and input() reports an error, so the two Divergence notes put Rust on different sides. A delivery of no token from the sole input place does not arise from a firing (IO-002, IO-004 AC1); both readings fail on it and the block says nothing of it.
- Consequence with CORE-050 and IO-015 (core052_xor_never_fires), the Note: fork writes every place of the spec, so on Xor(a, b) with a ≠ b its emission fills no output branch and no reference action firing ends with the fork action; the executor's output validation rejects the completion (EXEC-021). Under the validation skip of CONC-026 the completion is not checked, which is CONC-026's. The block does not restate this; it follows from line 1 and refActionFire.
- That every output place must accept the input value's type (Java's javadoc) is CORE-003's compatibility, owed by the net's author; a null value is propagated as a value like any other. That fork is a built-in with a constructor (fork() in each language, BuiltinAction in Python) is API shape. Whether it runs synchronously (Rust is_sync) is CONC-011's.
- AC1 (requires exactly one input place) is line 2 with line 1's premise. AC2 (exactly one token carrying the input value in each output place and none elsewhere) is line 1. AC3 (throws or errors if the transition does not declare exactly one input place) is line 2. AC4 (on two or more consumed tokens, fails or copies the oldest as in AC2) is line 3. The test derivation (fork with one input and three outputs; all three receive the same value) is CORE_052_nonvacuous: on And(Place 1, And(Place 2, Place 3)) the reference fork completes with 7 in places 1, 2 and 3, and the reference action firing deposits them.

<a id="Libpetri-Spec-CORE_053"></a>
## CORE-053: Transform Action

`Libpetri.Spec.CORE_053` · Kind **F** · Scope implementations that provide transform() · Source **verbatim** (spec/01-core-model.md) · Sign-off **pending** · Statement hash `029216b274201bbe`

| Natural language | Plain reading | Lean statement |
|---|---|---|
| *When* a transition fires under the transform action, the action *shall* call its function with the transition context of that firing, and *shall* complete or fail with the outcome of one such call.<br><br>*When* the function returns a value, the transform action *shall* complete with the output tokens the function wrote through the context, followed in every place the output spec names by one token carrying that value. | 1. Let X be the transform: X f is the action built from the host's function f; f t δ (ok (w, v)) says that one call of f, handed the transition t and the delivery δ, may return v after writing w through the context, and f t δ (error m) that one call may fail; val reads the value a token carries.<br>2. For every function f, transition t, delivery δ and emission e: if the action X f, handed t and δ, completes with e, then some single call of f on that same t and δ wrote w and returned v, and in every place the output specification of t names e holds the tokens w sent there followed by exactly one token carrying v, and in every other place exactly the tokens w sent there.<br>3. For every function f, transition t, delivery δ, writes w and value v that some token carries: if one call of f, handed t and δ, may write w and return v, then X f, handed t and δ, may complete with an emission of that shape for w and v.<br>4. For every function f, transition t, delivery δ and message m: if the action X f, handed t and δ, fails with m, then some call of f on that same t and δ fails. | <pre>fun {N T V} [DecidableEq N] val X ↦<br>  (∀ (f : TransformFn N T V) (t : Reference.Trans N) (δ : Delivered N T)<br>      (e : List (N × T)),<br>      X f t δ (Except.ok e) →<br>        ∃ w v, f t δ (Except.ok (w, v)) ∧ TransformCopies val t w v e) ∧<br>    (∀ (f : TransformFn N T V) (t : Reference.Trans N) (δ : Delivered N T)<br>        (w : List (N × T)) (v : V),<br>        f t δ (Except.ok (w, v)) →<br>          (∃ x, val x = v) → ∃ e, X f t δ (Except.ok e) ∧ TransformCopies val t w v e) ∧<br>      ∀ (f : TransformFn N T V) (t : Reference.Trans N) (δ : Delivered N T) (m : String),<br>        X f t δ (Except.error m) → ∃ m', f t δ (Except.error m')</pre> |

**Assumptions**

- The model is the pair (val, X). X is the transform combinator: from the host's function f (TransformFn: a relation from the transition and what the firing delivered to the outcome of one call, either the tokens the function wrote through the context and the value it returned, or a failure) it gives the action X f (ActionRel, Spec/GlossaryAction.lean; glossary: Action). val : T → V reads the value a token carries, so tokens are compared on their values, never on their identity or creation stamp: the stamp of a copied token is the host's (CORE-011), and Rust stamps each copy at its own output call (rust/libpetri-core/src/context.rs output_raw). The witness is refTransform val.
- The function is a relation, not a function, because it may read the world: one delivery may give more than one value, or a value on one call and a failure on another. That is what makes 'one such call' a line: a transform that calls the function once per output place may copy a different value to each place (CORE_053_mutant_perPlace_killed), and a transform whose emission is the writes of two calls is no single call's writes.
- How many times the function is called beyond the call that accounts for the outcome is not observable in a relational model, and a transform that makes an extra call and discards its result is not excluded: the first sentence says which call the outcome comes from, not how many calls are made.
- Line 1 reads both sentences from the completion's side: the function is called on the transition context of the firing (the transition and the delivery the action was handed; CORE-050 line 1 makes that the firing's delivery), and the completion is one call's writes followed by the copies. Its accessors (input, inputs, inputToken, read, output) are CORE-060 to CORE-063's. A transform that hands the function an empty context (CORE_053_forbids_blind), that drops what the function wrote (CORE_053_forbids_dropWrites), that puts the copy before what the function wrote (CORE_053_forbids_copiesFirst), that writes only the first output place (CORE_053_forbids_firstOnly) or that copies once per occurrence of a place the output specification names twice (CORE_053_forbids_rawList) violates it.
- Line 1 is stated per place (EmittedTo): the order of the copies across places is not stated. Rust iterates a hash set of the output places, Java and TypeScript iterate the transition's output place set; each place receives exactly one copy, after what the function wrote there, which is what the marking sees (EXEC-020 appends per place in emission order).
- Line 2 reads the second sentence's 'shall complete' from the side of the call: a call of the function that returns a value gives a completion. A transform that never ends, with neither a completion nor a failure, holds of lines 1 and 3 alone (CORE_053_mutant_soundOnly_killed). The premise that some token carries v holds in every runtime (any value can be put in a token) and keeps the line true at every model type.
- Line 3 reads 'complete or fail with the outcome of one such call' and the second sentence's 'shall complete' from the side of a failure: the transform fails only when a call of its function on the same transition and delivery fails, so a transform that may fail after its function returned, such as a copy loop whose output call can fail, violates it (CORE_053_mutant_noFailLine_killed). The failure's message is not compared. Rust's function returns a value and has no failure channel, and its copy loop names only declared output places, so its output call does not fail there and the Rust transform never fails; Java and TypeScript catch the function's exception and fail the action, as the reference does with the call's message.
- Whether a failing call must make the transform fail, and how a failure is handled, are EXEC-030's. The function's own writes are output calls through the context, so which places they may name is CORE-062 and CORE-063's: when every write list the function returns is built by output calls of a context that meets CORE-062 line 1, the transform writes through that context (refTransform_throughCtx), and an action that writes through a context whose output calls append only on output places deposits only in output places (ctx_deposits_outputs, core053_deposits_outputs). The execution context of CORE-064 is not modelled.
- The place set is the glossary's output arc (OutputArc: every place the output specification names, all branches of an XOR, the child of a Timeout, the destination of a ForwardInput), the same set every runtime hands the context (rust/libpetri-core/src/output.rs all_places; Java Transition.outputPlaces; TypeScript TransitionContext.outputPlaces). On a specification with more than one output branch the copies fill every branch, so the completion fills no single branch and the firing ends with no completion of the action (IO-015, EXEC-021; core053_xor_never_fires). The markdown's note under CORE-053 says so for the reader.
- In the joint model a firing that ends with the completion of the transform deposits that completion (CORE-050 line 2), so it deposits one call's writes followed by one copy per output place (core053_firing_copies).
- AC1 (the function receives the transition context) is line 1: the call that accounts for the completion is a call on the transition and the delivery the action was handed (CORE_053_forbids_blind).
- AC2 (the return value is produced to all output places) is lines 1 and 2: every completion carries one token with the returned value in every place the output specification names, and every returned value gives such a completion (CORE_053_forbids_firstOnly). transform(place, fn), transformFrom and transformAsync are API shape, not encoded.
- The test derivation (a transform that doubles an integer input; all outputs receive the doubled value) is CORE_053_nonvacuous: the doubling function on a delivery of 7, under AND(Place 1, Place 2), completes with 14 in place 1 and 14 in place 2, and the reference action firing deposits both; besides, a function that fails makes the reference transform fail, so the premise of line 3 is met.

<a id="Libpetri-Spec-CORE_054"></a>
## CORE-054: Produce Action

`Libpetri.Spec.CORE_054` · Kind **F** · Scope the built-in produce action of Java, TypeScript and Rust (the Python binding exposes no produce built-in) · Source **verbatim** (spec/01-core-model.md) · Sign-off **pending** · Statement hash `acb467a056e6b53c`

| Natural language | Plain reading | Lean statement |
|---|---|---|
| *When* the built-in produce action of a place and a value runs on a transition whose output spec names that place, the action *shall* complete with exactly one output token, which carries that value and goes to that place, and with no output token in any other place.<br><br>*If* the built-in produce action of a place and a value runs on a transition whose output spec does not name that place, *then* the action *shall* fail. | 1. For every value projection value and every produce action family produce (produce p v is the built-in action that produces the value v to the place p), every place p, value v, transition t and delivery δ:<br>2. if the output specification of t names p and some token carries v, produce p v ends on t and δ in some way;<br>3. if the output specification of t names p, every way produce p v ends on t and δ is a completion with the emission [(p, x)] for a token x whose value is v: exactly one output token, in p, and no token in any other place;<br>4. if the output specification of t does not name p, produce p v ends on t and δ in some way;<br>5. if the output specification of t does not name p, every way produce p v ends on t and δ is a failure. | <pre>fun {N T V} [DecidableEq N] value produce ↦<br>  (∀ (p : N) (v : V) (t : Reference.Trans N) (δ : Delivered N T),<br>      OutputArc t p → (∃ x, value x = v) → ∃ r, produce p v t δ r) ∧<br>    (∀ (p : N) (v : V) (t : Reference.Trans N) (δ : Delivered N T)<br>        (r : Except String (List (N × T))),<br>        OutputArc t p → produce p v t δ r → ∃ x, r = Except.ok [(p, x)] ∧ value x = v) ∧<br>      (∀ (p : N) (v : V) (t : Reference.Trans N) (δ : Delivered N T),<br>          ¬OutputArc t p → ∃ r, produce p v t δ r) ∧<br>        ∀ (p : N) (v : V) (t : Reference.Trans N) (δ : Delivered N T)<br>          (r : Except String (List (N × T))),<br>          ¬OutputArc t p → produce p v t δ r → ∃ m, r = Except.error m</pre> |

**Assumptions**

- The model is the pair (value, produce). value : T → V reads a token's value; T is the queue model's token identities, each carrying its value and its creation timestamp. produce p v is an action (ActionRel, Spec/GlossaryAction.lean): a relation from a transition and the delivery to how the action ends, completing with an emission (places and tokens, in emission order) or failing with a message. The value is fixed: on every transition whose output spec names p, whatever the delivery, every completion of produce p v carries v (line 2), so every such firing produces the same value. The witness is refProduce value, the single output call output(p, v) on the reference context refCtx (core054_ctxProduce), which mirrors the three runtimes (rust/libpetri-core/src/action.rs:165-168, java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/core/TransitionAction.java:179-184, typescript/src/core/transition-action.ts:89-93: one ctx.output call, then completion).
- ActionRel records the ways an action ends, not whether every run ends: an action that ends on some runs and not on others is the relation of its endings, so a run that does not end is outside this block, and lines 1 and 3 rule out only an action that has no way to end at all. The three runtimes end after the one output call (Rust run_sync returns, Java returns a completed future, the TypeScript async function returns or throws).
- The block states the value, not the token: line 2 fixes the place and the value of the one token, and the token's creation timestamp is out of scope for this block. That an output token carries the epoch clock reading at its output call is CORE-035 AC2 and CORE-011, whose executor line is the W11 block; a produce action that builds its token once and hands that same token to every firing (the Java metadata overload ctx.output(Place, Token), java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/core/TransitionContext.java:295) meets this block and is for that line to reject. The runtimes stamp at the output call (rust/libpetri-core/src/context.rs:401-416, created_at from the epoch clock). The premise of line 1 that some token carries v holds of every runtime's token type, which carries any value of its type; it is there because the block is stated over an abstract token type.
- 'A transition whose output spec names that place' is OutputArc t p (glossary: Output arc; CORE-035, IO-017). On a place the output specification does not name, the output call reports an error and leaves no entry behind (CORE-062 AC5, CORE-063 AC3), and lines 3 and 4 say the produce action passes that error on: it fails, and it never completes, so it cannot complete with no token (refProduce_undeclared). Every runtime does so: Rust returns the error with ?, Java throws IllegalArgumentException from the output call and the TypeScript output call throws inside the async action. A transition with no output specification names no place, so the produce action of any place fails on it. Whether the one-token emission is a deposit the output specification offers is the firing's question (IO-015, CORE-050 line 3): on Place p it is (core054_fires), on And(Place p, Place q) it is not and validation fails the firing (EXEC-021).
- Line 1 says that the action ends on a declared place, so an action that never ends there violates it (CORE_054_mutant_noComplete_killed: lines 2 to 4 hold of it). Line 2 says what every way of ending on a declared place is, so an action that fails there violates it (CORE_054_forbids_fails), and so do one that writes two tokens (CORE_054_forbids_twoTokens) and one that writes the token it consumed instead of the value (CORE_054_forbids_echo). 'Exactly one output token in that place and none in any other' is stronger than AC1's 'the place receives a token with the value': an action that writes the value to every output place meets the AC1 reading and violates line 2 (CORE_054_mutant_ac1_killed). Line 3 says that the action ends on an undeclared place (CORE_054_mutant_noEndUndeclared_killed: an action that never ends there meets lines 1, 2 and 4). Line 4 says that every way it ends there is a failure (CORE_054_mutant_swallowSometimes_killed: an action that fails on some runs and completes with no token on others meets lines 1 to 3), and an action that always swallows the error and completes with no token violates it (CORE_054_forbids_swallow).
- The produce action writes through the context: every emission it completes with is a buffer built by successful output calls (refProduce_throughCtx), so CORE-062's and CORE-063's context lines and ctx_deposits_outputs apply to it.
- AC1 (the specified place receives a token with the fixed value) is lines 1 and 2 at the action, and at the firing through CORE-050: on a transition whose output specification is Place p, an enabled firing ends with the completion of produce p v (core054_fires), and every firing that ends with it deposits exactly one token of value v in p and nothing elsewhere (core054_emits). Lines 3 and 4 have no acceptance criterion of CORE-054; they are CORE-062 AC5 and CORE-063 AC3 at the produce action.
- The test derivation (produce action with value "hello" to place P; P receives "hello") is CORE_054_nonvacuous: on a transition consuming one token from place 0 and producing to Place 1, the reference action firing under refProduce for the value "hello" deposits one token carrying "hello" in place 1, and on place 2, which the transition does not name, the reference action fails.

**Evidence**

- ✓ **holds** `Libpetri.Spec.CORE_054_reference` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.CORE_054): ✓ The reference produce action satisfies CORE-054, for every value projection: on a place the output specification names, it completes with one token carrying the value in that place, and only so; on a place it does not name, it fails, and only fails.
  <pre>∀ {N T V : Type} [inst : DecidableEq N] (value : T → V), CORE_054 value (refProduce value)</pre>
- ✗ **forbids** `Libpetri.Spec.CORE_054_forbids_echo` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.CORE_054): ✗ Writing the consumed input violates line 2: on `u` with the token `("in", 1)` delivered from place 0, the produce action of place 1 and the value "hello" writes a token carrying "in".
  <pre>¬CORE_054 Prod.fst core054_echo</pre>
- ✗ **forbids** `Libpetri.Spec.CORE_054_forbids_fails` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.CORE_054): ✗ Failing on a declared place violates line 2: on `u` the produce action of place 1 fails.
  <pre>¬CORE_054 Prod.fst core054_fails</pre>
- ✗ **forbids** `Libpetri.Spec.CORE_054_forbids_swallow` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.CORE_054): ✗ Swallowing the error violates line 4: on `u` the produce action of place 2, which `u` does not name, completes with no token. At the firing, on a sink transition it would consume the input and deposit nothing, where every runtime fails the firing.
  <pre>¬CORE_054 Prod.fst (core054_swallow Prod.fst)</pre>
- ✗ **forbids** `Libpetri.Spec.CORE_054_forbids_twoTokens` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.CORE_054): ✗ Writing two tokens violates line 2: on `u` the produce action of place 1 completes with two tokens.
  <pre>¬CORE_054 Prod.fst (core054_twoTokens Prod.fst)</pre>
- ✗ **mutant** `Libpetri.Spec.CORE_054_mutant_ac1_killed` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.CORE_054): ✗ The everywhere action kills the mutant: it meets the AC1 reading, but on `w`, whose output specification is `And(Place 1, Place 2)`, the produce action of place 1 writes a token to place 2 as well (line 2).
  <pre>CORE_054_mutant_ac1 Prod.fst (core054_everywhere Prod.fst) ∧<br>  ¬CORE_054 Prod.fst (core054_everywhere Prod.fst)</pre>

<a id="Libpetri-Spec-CORE_060"></a>
## CORE-060: Context Input Access

`Libpetri.Spec.CORE_060` · Kind **F** · Scope the transition context of every implementation; line 3 and the inputToken part of line 4 only where the context gives access to tokens: Java and TypeScript · Source **verbatim** (spec/01-core-model.md) · Sign-off **pending** · Statement hash `2937b87cb602ef92`

| Natural language | Plain reading | Lean statement |
|---|---|---|
| *When* an action calls `inputs(place)` on an input place of its transition, the call *shall* return the values of the tokens the firing consumed from that place, in the order the firing consumed them ([EXEC-010]).<br><br>*When* an action calls `input(place)` on an input place from which the firing consumed exactly one token, the call *shall* return the value of that token.<br><br>*Where* the transition context gives access to tokens (Java, TypeScript), *when* an action calls `inputToken(place)` on an input place from which the firing consumed exactly one token, the call *shall* return that token, with its creation timestamp.<br><br>*If* an action calls `inputs(place)`, `input(place)` or `inputToken(place)` (where it exists) on a place that does not resolve to an input place of its transition ([MOD-031]), *then* the call *shall* report an error ([CORE-063]).<br><br>What `input(place)` and `inputToken(place)` return when the firing consumed more than one token from the place is not specified; an action reads a batch with `inputs(place)`. | 1. For every value projection value and every context C, every transition t, every delivery δ (the tokens the firing consumed from each input place and the tokens its read arcs read) and every place p:<br>2. if p is an input place of t and δ delivered at least one token from p, inputs on t, δ and p returns the values of the tokens δ delivered from p, in the order δ delivered them;<br>3. if p is an input place of t and δ delivered exactly one token x from p, input on t, δ and p returns the value of x;<br>4. if p is an input place of t and δ delivered exactly one token x from p, inputToken on t, δ and p returns x itself;<br>5. if p is not an input place of t and δ delivered no token from p, inputs, input and inputToken on t, δ and p each report an error. | <pre>fun {N T V} [DecidableEq N] value C ↦<br>  (∀ (t : Reference.Trans N) (δ : Delivered N T),<br>      ∀ p ∈ inPlaces t,<br>        δ.inputs p ≠ [] → C.inputs t δ p = some (List.map value (δ.inputs p))) ∧<br>    (∀ (t : Reference.Trans N) (δ : Delivered N T) (p : N) (x : T),<br>        p ∈ inPlaces t → δ.inputs p = [x] → C.input t δ p = some (value x)) ∧<br>      (∀ (t : Reference.Trans N) (δ : Delivered N T) (p : N) (x : T),<br>          p ∈ inPlaces t → δ.inputs p = [x] → C.inputToken t δ p = some x) ∧<br>        ∀ (t : Reference.Trans N) (δ : Delivered N T),<br>          ∀ p ∉ inPlaces t,<br>            δ.inputs p = [] →<br>              C.inputs t δ p = none ∧ C.input t δ p = none ∧ C.inputToken t δ p = none</pre> |

**Assumptions**

- The model is the pair (value, C). C is a transition context (Ctx, Spec/GlossaryContext.lean): its accessors inputs, input and inputToken take the transition, the delivery and a place, and return none when the call reports an error. A delivery (Delivered, Spec/GlossaryQueue.lean) is what the firing hands its action: the tokens it consumed from each input place, in the order consumed, and the tokens its read arcs read. Tokens are the queue model's token identities T, each carrying its value and its creation timestamp; value : T → V reads a token's value, so input (a value) and inputToken (the token, with its timestamp) are told apart. The witness is the reference context refCtx.
- The block is a function of the delivery, not of the marking: line 1 keeps the order in which the firing delivered the tokens, and which tokens the firing consumes, and in which order, is not CORE-060's. For an input that is not a correlated input of a ν-net match specification it is EXEC-010's: the oldest tokens of the place, in queue order. core060_inputs_oldest derives that for any context that satisfies CORE-060 and any queue firing relation that satisfies EXEC-010, and core060_input_oldest gives the value of the oldest token for input on an arc that consumes one token. A correlated input (NU-020) takes the matched tokens of the chosen name, oldest first among them, and can pass over an older token of another name, so for it the delivered tokens are not the oldest of the place. The block holds for whatever delivery that firing makes; the two joint theorems do not reach it, because the queue firing relation of EXEC-010 carries no match specification (ruling D16).
- Lines 1 and 4 range over the deliveries a firing makes at the place: line 1 takes an input place from which the delivery holds at least one token, line 4 a place that is not an input place and from which the delivery holds none. Every firing meets both premises: each input arc requires and consumes at least one token (IO-002, IO-004 AC1), and a firing consumes through its input arcs only. A delivery that breaks them is made by no firing, and the block makes no claim on it.
- The premises accept the Rust and Python check, which is key presence in the map of delivered tokens, not membership in the input places: Rust's input and inputs answer from self.inputs.get(place_name) (rust/libpetri-core/src/context.rs:278-302), the backends insert a key only when they push a token (rust/libpetri-runtime/src/bitmap_backend.rs:785-808), and Python copies those keys (rust/libpetri-py/src/action.rs:329-365). That context, core060_keyedCtx, satisfies CORE-060 (CORE_060_allows_keyed), and on every delivery that holds tokens from exactly the input places it answers as refCtx at every place (core060_keyed_agrees).
- Line 1 compares lists: the values in the order delivered, with their repetitions. A context that returns them in reverse order meets the reading 'inputs returns all consumed values' as a multiset and violates line 1 (CORE_060_mutant_anyOrder_killed).
- Lines 2 and 3 carry the premise that exactly one token was delivered from the place (ruling D50 (a), clash core-c#1). With more than one, the runtimes differ: input reports an error in Rust (rust/libpetri-core/src/context.rs:278-287), TypeScript (typescript/src/core/transition-context.ts:114-123) and Python (rust/libpetri-py/src/action.rs:207-217), and Java returns the value of the oldest token (java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/core/TransitionContext.java:164-168, against its own javadoc at :162, a recorded defect, RD-09 in spec/runtime-defects.md); inputToken returns the oldest token in Java (:190-194) and TypeScript (typescript/src/core/transition-context.ts:133-138). The block leaves the case open: CORE_060_batch_undecided shows two contexts that both satisfy it and differ there, on input and on inputToken. A firing never consumes zero tokens from an input place (IO-002 and IO-004 AC1: every input arc requires at least one token), so 'other than one' is 'more than one' at a firing. No line claims anything on an input place with an empty delivery, which no firing makes: lines 2 and 3 need exactly one token, line 1 at least one.
- A context whose input always reports an error, so that an action must use inputs, meets the reading 'input returns a consumed value when it returns one' and violates line 2 (CORE_060_mutant_soundOnly_killed). A context whose inputToken re-mints the token with the same value and another timestamp meets the reading 'inputToken returns a token with the consumed value' and violates line 3 (CORE_060_mutant_valueOnly_killed): the metadata the token carries is the consumed token's own.
- A context is a function of the transition, the delivery and the place, so a context that keeps state across firings is modelled as a different context at each firing. Java's precompiled executor reuses one context per transition and clears its token store before each firing (java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/runtime/PrecompiledNetExecutor.java:2320-2324); a context that kept the tokens of the previous firing ahead of its own violates lines 1 to 3 (CORE_060_forbids_staleStore).
- Line 3, and the inputToken part of line 4, are scoped to the implementations whose context gives access to tokens (ruling D50 (a), clash core-c#2): Java's and TypeScript's inputToken. The Rust and Python contexts expose values only (rust/libpetri-core/src/context.rs:278-327, python/libpetri/_libpetri.pyi), so line 3 has no accessor there; Rust's take_inputs empties the context and serves the executor, not an action. The Lean line is the same under every scope.
- Line 4 reads 'results in an error' as 'the call reports an error' (none): Rust returns an error, Java and TypeScript throw, Python raises. A place that is not an input place includes a read place (no place is both, ruling D15), an output place and a place of no arc of the transition. A context that answers such a place with the empty list meets the reading 'an undeclared place has no consumed values' and violates line 4 (CORE_060_mutant_emptyList_killed). So does one that keeps the consumed and the read tokens in one store and serves a read place through inputs (CORE_060_forbids_sharedStore), or through an inputToken that lost its input-place guard (CORE_060_forbids_unguardedToken): TypeScript's context and Java's precompiled executor keep one such store (typescript/src/core/transition-context.ts:114-160, java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/runtime/PrecompiledNetExecutor.java:2341-2347), so each accessor depends on its own guard. The read accessor is CORE-061's, the output accessor CORE-062's, and the three error lines together are CORE-063's.
- The error sentence names the place the call resolves to (MOD-031), and the block reads every place that way: after instancing or port binding, Java and TypeScript map a declared place the action names to the composed place first (MOD-031, W8). A type mismatch between the place and the value (Rust's downcast error) is API shape and not modelled: V is one type of values. Further accessors (Java's inputTokens, Rust's input_raw and input_tokens_raw) are not part of the block.
- AC1 (input(place) returns the single consumed value) is line 2, under the exactly-one premise of ruling D50 (a).
- AC2 (inputs(place) returns all consumed values, for multi-token cardinality) is line 1.
- AC3 (inputToken(place) returns the token with metadata, including its timestamp) is line 3, scoped to Java and TypeScript.
- AC4 (accessing an undeclared input place results in an error) is line 4.
- The test derivation (fire a transition consuming 3 tokens, verify inputs() returns 3 values) is CORE_060_nonvacuous: the reference firing of a transition whose input arc takes exactly 3 tokens delivers the 3 oldest, and the reference context returns their 3 values, in queue order.

**Evidence**

- ✓ **holds** `Libpetri.Spec.CORE_060_reference` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.CORE_060): ✓ The reference context satisfies CORE-060, whatever the value projection.
  <pre>∀ {N T V : Type} [inst : DecidableEq N] (value : T → V), CORE_060 value (refCtx value)</pre>
- ✓ **allows** `Libpetri.Spec.CORE_060_allows_keyed` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.CORE_060): ✓ The keyed context satisfies CORE-060: the premises of lines 1 and 4 (tokens delivered from an input place, none from any other place) are what every firing gives, and they are exactly what the key-presence check relies on.
  <pre>∀ {N T V : Type} [inst : DecidableEq N] (value : T → V),<br>  CORE_060 value (core060_keyedCtx value)</pre>
- ✗ **forbids** `Libpetri.Spec.CORE_060_forbids_sharedStore` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.CORE_060): ✗ It violates line 4: on `t3`, the read place 1 is no input place and the firing consumes no token from it, and its `inputs` answers with the value 7 read there instead of an error.
  <pre>¬CORE_060 Prod.fst (core060_sharedCtx Prod.fst)</pre>
- ✗ **forbids** `Libpetri.Spec.CORE_060_forbids_staleStore` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.CORE_060): ✗ After the first firing of `u` from `core060_M`, which consumed `(10, 1)`, the uncleared context serves the second firing, which consumes `(11, 2)`, with `(10, 1)`: line 3 fails.
  <pre>¬CORE_060 Prod.fst (core060_staleCtx (qDelivered core060_M core060_u) Prod.fst)</pre>
- ✗ **forbids** `Libpetri.Spec.CORE_060_forbids_unguardedToken` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.CORE_060): ✗ It violates line 4: on the reference firing of `t3`, `inputToken` on the read place 1 answers the read token `(7, 0)` instead of an error. Its `inputs` and `input` are guarded, so `CORE_060_forbids_sharedStore` does not cover it.
  <pre>¬CORE_060 Prod.fst (core060_unguardedTokenCtx Prod.fst)</pre>
- ? **undecided** `Libpetri.Spec.CORE_060_batch_undecided` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.CORE_060): ? The batch case is open. On the firing of `t3`, which consumes 3 tokens from place 0, the reference context and Java's reading both satisfy CORE-060 and differ on `input` (an error against the value 10 of the oldest token), and the reference context and the strict reading both satisfy it and differ on `inputToken` (the oldest token `(10, 1)` against an error).
  <pre>CORE_060 Prod.fst core060_ref ∧<br>  CORE_060 Prod.fst (core060_oldestCtx Prod.fst) ∧<br>    CORE_060 Prod.fst (core060_strictCtx Prod.fst) ∧<br>      core060_ref.input core060_t3 (qDelivered core060_M core060_t3) 0 = none ∧<br>        (core060_oldestCtx Prod.fst).input core060_t3 (qDelivered core060_M core060_t3)<br>              0 =<br>            some 10 ∧<br>          core060_ref.inputToken core060_t3 (qDelivered core060_M core060_t3) 0 =<br>              some (10, 1) ∧<br>            (core060_strictCtx Prod.fst).inputToken core060_t3<br>                (qDelivered core060_M core060_t3) 0 =<br>              none</pre>
- ✗ **mutant** `Libpetri.Spec.CORE_060_mutant_anyOrder_killed` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.CORE_060): ✗ The reversing context kills the mutant: it meets the multiset reading, but on `t3` it returns 12, 11, 10 for the tokens consumed as 10, 11, 12 (line 1).

- ✗ **mutant** `Libpetri.Spec.CORE_060_mutant_soundOnly_killed` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.CORE_060): ✗ The context without `input` kills the mutant: it meets the soundness reading, but on `u`, which consumes the one token `(10, 1)`, its `input` reports an error (line 2).

- ✗ **mutant** `Libpetri.Spec.CORE_060_mutant_valueOnly_killed` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.CORE_060): ✗ The re-minting context kills the mutant: it meets the value reading, but on `u`, which consumes the token `(10, 1)`, its `inputToken` returns `(10, 0)` (line 3).

- ✓ **nonvacuous** `Libpetri.Spec.CORE_060_nonvacuous` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.CORE_060): ✓ CORE-060 is not vacuous. The test derivation: `t3` fires from `core060_M` (a reference queue firing), consuming the 3 oldest tokens of place 0, and the reference context returns their 3 values in queue order. On `u`, which consumes one token, `input` returns the value 10 of the oldest token and `inputToken` the token `(10, 1)` with its timestamp. <a id="Libpetri-Spec-CORE_061"></a>
## CORE-061: Context Read Access

`Libpetri.Spec.CORE_061` · Kind **F** · Scope the transition context of every implementation · Source **verbatim** (spec/01-core-model.md) · Sign-off **pending** · Statement hash `5b633acdce70d774`

| Natural language | Plain reading | Lean statement |
|---|---|---|
| *When* an action calls `read(place)` on a read place of its transition, the call *shall* return the value of the token the read arc read from that place, the oldest token the place holds ([EXEC-012]).<br><br>The call consumes nothing: by [EXEC-012] the firing leaves the read token in the place, unless the transition also has a reset arc there, which drains the place ([EXEC-013]).<br><br>*If* an action calls `read(place)` on a place that does not resolve to a read place of its transition ([MOD-031]), *then* the call *shall* report an error, also when the place is an input place of the transition. | 1. For every value projection value and every context C, every transition t, every delivery δ (the tokens the firing consumed from each input place and the tokens its read arcs read) and every place p:<br>2. if p is a read place of t, δ consumed no token from p and the first token δ read at p is x, read on t, δ and p returns the value of x;<br>3. if p is not a read place of t and δ read no token at p, read on t, δ and p reports an error, whether or not p is an input place of t. | <pre>fun {N T V} [DecidableEq N] value C ↦<br>  (∀ (t : Reference.Trans N) (δ : Delivered N T) (p : N) (x : T),<br>      ReadArc t p →<br>        δ.inputs p = [] → (δ.reads p).head? = some x → C.read t δ p = some (value x)) ∧<br>    ∀ (t : Reference.Trans N) (δ : Delivered N T) (p : N),<br>      ¬ReadArc t p → δ.reads p = [] → C.read t δ p = none</pre> |

**Assumptions**

- The model is the pair (value, C). C is a transition context (Ctx, Spec/GlossaryContext.lean): its accessor read takes the transition, the delivery and a place, and returns none when the call reports an error. A delivery (Delivered, Spec/GlossaryQueue.lean) is what the firing hands its action: the tokens it consumed from each input place and the tokens its read arcs read, per place. Tokens are the queue model's token identities T; value : T → V reads a token's value. The witness is the reference context refCtx.
- The block is a function of the delivery, not of the marking. Which token a read arc reads is not CORE-061's but EXEC-012's: the head of the read place, after input consumption and before reset draining. core061_read_head derives, for any context that satisfies CORE-061, any pair (Build, Q) that satisfies EXEC-012 and whose Q satisfies EXEC-010, that on a firing of a transition with no input arc and read arc on one place read returns the value of the oldest token of the read place, and that the firing leaves the queue of a read place that is not a reset place as it was, followed by the tokens it deposits there (identity and order). That is the clause 'the oldest token the place holds' of the first quoted sentence. The second quoted sentence states EXEC-012 line 2 as a consequence for the action and is not a line of this block: it is the 'without consuming it' of AC1 and the 'token still in place' of the test derivation, and its exception names EXEC-013, under which a reset arc drains the place. The context itself is a function and consumes nothing.
- The premises 'δ consumed no token from p' (line 1) and 'δ read no token at p' (line 2) are a property of the firing, not of the context: a firing delivers read tokens only at the read places of its transition and consumed tokens only at its input places (core061_ByArcs). The reference queue firing has it (core061_refQFire_byArcs, from qDelivered_reads_off and qDelivered_inputs_off), and every runtime builds its delivery that way. EXEC-010's line 3 (no consumed token from a place that is not an input place) and EXEC-012's line 7 (no read token from a place that is not a read place) state it for every executor, so every queue firing relation that meets both delivers by arcs (core061_byArcs_of). Under them the third quoted sentence holds at every firing (core061_read_off, from EXEC-012 alone), and the first does through core061_read_head.
- Line 1 takes the first token read at the read place, from a delivery that holds no consumed token there. At a firing of a transition that builds both premises are what the firing gives: every token a firing delivers at a read place is the head of its queue (EXEC-012 line 1), so the first is the only value there is, and a transition with two read arcs on one place gets the head twice; and no read place is an input place (ruling D15), so under core061_ByArcs the firing consumed no token from it. On a delivery no firing makes, with two different read tokens at one place, line 1 still asks for the first: that is a deliberate choice, and every runtime takes the first entry (Rust tokens[0], rust/libpetri-core/src/context.rs:337-347; Java's and TypeScript's TokenInput, java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/core/TokenInput.java:70-76). A context that answers the last read token agrees with refCtx at every firing and is rejected only on such a delivery. The premise that the delivery holds a read token at the read place holds at every firing, because a transition fires only while its read places are marked (CORE-032). On a read place from which the delivery holds no token, which no firing makes, the block makes no claim; refCtx and every runtime report an error there (Rust 'No tokens for read place', Python 'read place ... is empty', Java and TypeScript TokenInput.get).
- Java and TypeScript keep the consumed and the read tokens in one store (rawInput), filled with the consumed tokens first and the read tokens after them (java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/runtime/BitmapNetExecutor.java:1671-1699, java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/runtime/PrecompiledNetExecutor.java:2323-2345, typescript/src/runtime/bitmap-net-executor.ts:1055-1075, typescript/src/runtime/precompiled-net-executor.ts:1080-1116), and read checks its guard requireRead and then answers the first entry of that store at the place (java/src/main/java/org/libpetri/core/TransitionContext.java:235-239, typescript/src/core/transition-context.ts:156-160). That context, core061_guardedSharedCtx, satisfies CORE-061 (CORE_061_allows_guardedShared), because line 1 takes a delivery with no consumed token at the read place, and at every firing of a transition that builds, under core061_ByArcs, it answers read as refCtx at every place (core061_guarded_agrees). Without the premise, line 1 would reject it on a delivery no firing makes (core061_strict_rejects_guarded). The same store served through a read without its guard is forbidden (CORE_061_forbids_sharedStore).
- A context whose read always reports an error meets the reading 'read returns a read value when it returns one' and violates line 1 (CORE_061_mutant_soundOnly_killed).
- Line 2 reads 'results in an error' as 'the call reports an error' (none): Rust returns an error, Java and TypeScript throw, Python raises. 'An undeclared read place' is any place that is not a read place of the transition: an input place, an output place, or a place of no arc of the transition. A context with one allowed set for inputs and reads, which answers read on an input place with the value of a consumed token, meets the reading 'read reports an error on a place the transition does not declare at all' and violates line 2 (CORE_061_mutant_anyDeclared_killed). No place is both an input place and a read place of a transition that builds (ruling D15, EXEC-012), so the two lines never meet on one place at a firing.
- Line 2 accepts the Rust and Python check, which is key presence in the map of read tokens, not membership in the read places: Rust's read answers from self.reads.get(place_name) (rust/libpetri-core/src/context.rs:337-347), the backends insert a key only when they push a read token (rust/libpetri-runtime/src/bitmap_backend.rs:823-832, rust/libpetri-runtime/src/precompiled_backend.rs:866-877), and Python copies those keys (rust/libpetri-py/src/action.rs:226-236, :367-381). That context, core061_keyedCtx, satisfies CORE-061 (CORE_061_allows_keyed), and on every delivery that holds read tokens at exactly the read places it answers read as refCtx at every place (core061_keyed_agrees). It is correct only under core061_ByArcs, which is why that property is named above.
- The third quoted sentence is word for word the second quoted sentence of CORE-063, and line 2 is the same formula as CORE-063's line 2. CORE-061 is the requirement that states the rule, as its AC2; CORE-063 depends on CORE-061 and collects the error lines of CORE-060 to CORE-062, so the citation runs from CORE-063 to CORE-061 and not back.
- The error sentence names the place the call resolves to (MOD-031), and the block reads every place that way: after instancing or port binding, Java and TypeScript map a declared place the action names to the composed place first (MOD-031, W8), and Python falls back through its local name map. A type mismatch between the place and the value (Rust's downcast error) is API shape and not modelled: V is one type of values. Further accessors (reads(place) in Java, TypeScript, Rust and Python, Rust's read_tokens_raw) are not part of the block.
- AC1 (read(place) returns the read value without consuming it) is line 1, with 'without consuming it' from EXEC-012 line 2 through core061_read_head.
- AC2 (accessing an undeclared read place results in an error) is line 2, and at a firing core061_read_off.
- The test derivation (fire a transition with a read arc, verify read() returns the value, verify the token is still in place) is CORE_061_nonvacuous: a reference firing of a transition with an input arc on place 0 and a read arc on place 1, which holds 7 then 8, delivers the token of value 7 at place 1, the reference context returns 7, the firing leaves 7 and 8 in place 1, and read on the input place 0 and on the output place 2 reports an error. CORE_061_joint_example derives the same answers through core061_read_head and core061_read_off from EXEC-012's reference pair.
