<a id="Libpetri-Spec-ENV_002"></a>
## ENV-002: Environment Place Registration

`Libpetri.Spec.ENV_002` · Kind **B** · Scope executors whose inject takes an environment-place handle (Java, TypeScript) · Source **verbatim** (spec/06-environment-places.md) · Sign-off **pending** · Statement hash `14a2f6d4b95be3d0`

| Natural language | Plain reading | Lean statement |
|---|---|---|
| Environment places must be registered with the executor before execution begins.<br><br>The executor maintains a set of registered environment places.<br><br>Where inject takes an environment-place handle (Java, TypeScript), only registered environment places accept injections.<br><br>Where inject takes an environment-place handle (Java, TypeScript), attempting to inject into a non-environment place returns an error.<br><br>The set of registered environment places is fixed when the executor is built; no step of a run adds or removes one.<br><br>*Where* an executor's inject takes an environment-place handle (Java, TypeScript), *if* a caller injects into a place that is not a registered environment place, *then* the executor *shall* answer with an error, and *shall not* answer with a refusal even when it is draining, closed, stopped or finished.<br><br>*Where* an executor's inject takes an environment-place handle (Java, TypeScript), *if* a caller injects into a place that is not a registered environment place, *then* the executor *shall* leave its state unchanged: it *shall not* queue the token and *shall not* change the marking.<br><br>*Where* an executor's inject takes an environment-place handle (Java, TypeScript), the executor *shall* answer an injection into a place that is not a registered environment place with an error in every state of the run, before and after the run finishes.<br><br>*Where* an executor's inject takes an environment-place handle (Java, TypeScript), the executor *shall not* answer an injection into a registered environment place with an error, in any state of the run.<br><br>*Where* an executor's inject takes an environment-place handle (Java, TypeScript), *while* the run has not finished and the executor is not draining, closed or stopped, the executor *shall* accept an injection into a registered environment place. | 1. For every executor R, every configuration C, every place p and every token x:<br>2. if p is not one of C's environment places, a request step that asks to inject x into p answers with an error;<br>3. if p is not one of C's environment places, a request step that asks to inject x into p leaves the executor state as it was;<br>4. if p is one of C's environment places, a request step that asks to inject x into p does not answer with an error. | <pre>fun {N T} [DecidableEq N] R ↦<br>  ∀ (C : Cfg N T) (p : N) (x : T),<br>    (p ∉ C.envs →<br>        (∀ (r : Reply),<br>            on fun s s' ↦ R C s (XLbl.request p x r) s', shall fun x x_1 ↦<br>              r = Reply.error) ∧<br>          ∀ (r : Reply),<br>            on fun s s' ↦ R C s (XLbl.request p x r) s', shall fun s s' ↦ s' = s) ∧<br>      (p ∈ C.envs →<br>        ∀ (r : Reply),<br>          on fun s s' ↦ R C s (XLbl.request p x r) s', shall fun x x_1 ↦ r ≠ Reply.error)</pre> |

**Assumptions**

- The model is an executor R : XRel N T (glossary GlossaryExec.lean): R C s l s' says that under configuration C the step labelled l leads from executor state s to s'. The label request p x r is the outside step of a caller asking to inject token x into place p, with the executor's answer r: accepted (queued), refused (the executor is draining, closed, stopped or finished, ENV-006) or error (not an environment place). The witness is the reference executor RefExec (Reference/Exec.lean), whose request rule answers replyFor C s p and changes the state only on an accepted answer.
- Scope (ruling D89 (a)): Java and TypeScript, whose inject takes an EnvironmentPlace handle and tests registration first (BitmapNetExecutor.inject and PrecompiledNetExecutor.inject return a failed future; the TypeScript inject rejects its promise and injectNoAwait throws). Rust and Python take a place name and deposit into the place it names whatever the registration (executor_handle.rs inject, executor_core/executor.rs handle_signal): the name-keyed executor env002_nameKeyed violates lines 1 and 2 (ENV_002_forbids_nameKeyed). For them the second block of this ID, ENV_002_host (kind A), states the host assumption instead.
- The registered environment places are the configuration field C.envs (kind N): the quoted 'Environment places must be registered with the executor before execution begins.' and 'The executor maintains a set of registered environment places.' are that encoding. AC1 (the builder accepts registrations) is that field: every builder of the three languages fills it (Java Builder.environmentPlaces, TypeScript options.environmentPlaces, Rust ExecutorOptions.environment_places); it is configuration, not a step. That the reference's answer to an unregistered place depends on the configuration alone, in every state, is env002_registration_fixed (cited for ENV-001 AC3).
- The quoted 'The set of registered environment places is fixed when the executor is built; no step of a run adds or removes one.' is lines 1 and 3 together: under ENV-002 a request step answers with an error exactly when its place is not in C.envs, in every state (env002_error_iff), so the registrations an executor honours are C.envs throughout the run. An executor that adds a place during a run breaks line 1. One that removes the registrations once a ticket has been drawn breaks line 3 (env002_shrinks, ENV_002_forbids_shrinks): the shape of a Java builder that keeps the caller's set instead of a copy, from which the host then removes a place. One that ignores the registrations and answers every injection with an error breaks line 3 (env002_neverMatches, ENV_002_forbids_neverMatches): the shape of a registration set built from the handles while inject tests the names.
- Line 1 is the first EARS sentence. Its 'shall not answer with a refusal even when it is draining, closed, stopped or finished' is the order of the two tests: registration before the lifecycle, as Java (inject, then the closed and draining flags) and TypeScript (the throw, then the closed, draining and terminal flags) do. An executor that tests the lifecycle first answers a closed executor's unregistered injection with a refusal (ENV_002_forbids_lifecycleFirst). An executor that may answer a closed executor's unregistered injection with a refusal besides the error breaks line 1 only (ENV_002_mutant_mayRefuse). 'Answer with an error' also excludes an acceptance, which is the 'only' of AC2: an accepted request names a registered place (env002_only_registered_accept, cited for AC2).
- Line 2 is the second EARS sentence: the request changes nothing, so no token is queued (the event queue XSt.eq is unchanged), the marking is unchanged and the loop is not woken (XSt.parked is unchanged). An executor that answers with an error and still queues the token breaks line 2 only (ENV_002_mutant_errorButQueue).
- Its offers are in ExecCoversW5.Env002Covers (ConsistencyExec.lean; the convention of GlossaryExec.lean: offers are coverage clauses, never block lines). The third and the fifth EARS sentences demand an answer and are quoted whole; their safety halves are lines 1 and 3, and their existence halves are that clause. The third EARS sentence and the 'returns' of AC3 say the error is an answer the executor gives in every state, open, draining, closed, stopped or after the run finished, not a call that blocks: Env002Covers offers it in every executor state, reachable or not, which is more than 'every state of the run' and which the reference meets (env002_ref_covers). An executor without a request step for an unregistered place satisfies every line and fails that clause (env002_covers_noAnswer); it is also the reference restricted to a host that meets ENV_002_host, which is why a name-keyed executor under that assumption is indistinguishable from the reference on the host's runs.
- Line 3 is the fourth EARS sentence: a registered place is never answered with an error, in any state; once the executor is draining, closed, stopped or finished the answer is a refusal (ENV-006), a false future in Java and false in TypeScript. An executor that may answer a registered place with an error besides the reference's answer breaks line 3 only (env002_mayErrorRegistered, ENV_002_mutant_mayErrorRegistered): the shape of a registration test by object identity that misses an equal handle the caller built anew.
- The fifth EARS sentence, the 'accept' of AC2 and the 'success' of the test derivation, is the second half of Env002Covers: while the executor is open (not draining, closed or stopped) and in a phase of the run (isExecPhase, not finished), R offers to accept an injection into a registered place. That clause requires the accepting step to exist; that an open running executor never refuses a registered place instead is ENV-010's line 2, and what the accepted request does (queue the token with a ticket, FIFO) is ENV-003's. An executor that refuses every registered place meets every line and fails the clause (env002_refuseRegistered, env002_covers_refuseRegistered): the shape of a lifecycle flag that starts set. Injections before the run starts are outside the model, whose runs start at xinit in mode open.
- AC1 is the configuration field C.envs, and line 3 and Env002Covers say the executor honours it. AC2 is line 1 for 'only' and Env002Covers for 'accept'. AC3 is line 1 and Env002Covers. AC4 is the second block, ENV_002_host. A refusal is ENV-006's subject, on the same request label. The Java error is a failed future and the TypeScript error a rejected promise (inject) or a thrown exception (injectNoAwait); the model does not tell them apart, all are the answer error.
- The test derivation's Java and TypeScript clause (register 3 environment places; inject into a registered one, success; inject into an unregistered one, error) is ENV_002_nonvacuous: with places 0, 1 and 2 registered, a request into 0 is accepted and its token lands in place 0 at the next injection step, a request into 0 by the closed executor is refused, not answered with an error, and a request into place 3 is answered with an error, by an open and by a closed executor, with the state unchanged. Its Rust and Python clause (AC4 is an assumption on the host, which no executor test checks) is the kind A of the second block.

**Evidence**

- ✓ **holds** `Libpetri.Spec.ENV_002_reference` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.ENV_002): ✓ The reference executor satisfies ENV-002: its request rule answers `replyFor`, which is an error exactly for an unregistered place whatever the state, and changes the state only on an accepted answer (`requestStep_some`).
  <pre>∀ {N T : Type} [inst : DecidableEq N], ENV_002 RefExec</pre>
- ✗ **forbids** `Libpetri.Spec.ENV_002_forbids_lifecycleFirst` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.ENV_002): ✗ Testing the lifecycle before the registration violates ENV-002 (line 1): a closed executor answers the request into the unregistered place `3` with a refusal.
  <pre>¬ENV_002 env002_lifecycleFirst</pre>
- ✗ **forbids** `Libpetri.Spec.ENV_002_forbids_nameKeyed` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.ENV_002): ✗ The name-keyed executor of Rust and Python violates ENV-002 (line 1): an open executor accepts the request into the unregistered place `3` and queues it. This is why the block is scoped to the handle-typed inject and the host block covers the name-keyed one.
  <pre>¬ENV_002 env002_nameKeyed</pre>
- ✗ **forbids** `Libpetri.Spec.ENV_002_forbids_neverMatches` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.ENV_002): ✗ Registrations that never match violate ENV-002 (line 3): the open executor answers the request into the registered place `0` with an error. Lines 1 and 2 alone accept this executor (`env002Rel_unreg`).
  <pre>¬ENV_002 env002_neverMatches</pre>
- ✗ **forbids** `Libpetri.Spec.ENV_002_forbids_shrinks` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.ENV_002): ✗ Registrations removed during the run violate ENV-002 (line 3): after the injection into the registered place `0` is accepted, the still open executor answers the next injection into `0` with an error. Lines 1 and 2 alone accept this executor (`env002Rel_unreg`).
  <pre>¬ENV_002 env002_shrinks</pre>
- ✗ **mutant** `Libpetri.Spec.ENV_002_mutant_errorButQueue` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.ENV_002): Line 2 is load-bearing: an executor that answers an unregistered place with an error but queues the token meets lines 1 and 3 but not line 2.
  <pre>ENV_002_noFrameLine env002_errorButQueue ∧ ¬ENV_002 env002_errorButQueue</pre>
- ✗ **mutant** `Libpetri.Spec.ENV_002_mutant_mayErrorRegistered` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.ENV_002): Line 3 is load-bearing: an executor that may also answer a registered place with an error meets lines 1 and 2 but not line 3. The open executor answers the request into the registered place `0` with an error.
  <pre>ENV_002_noRegErrorLine env002_mayErrorRegistered ∧ ¬ENV_002 env002_mayErrorRegistered</pre>
- ✗ **mutant** `Libpetri.Spec.ENV_002_mutant_mayRefuse` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.ENV_002): Line 1 is load-bearing: an executor that may refuse an unregistered place once it is closed meets lines 2 and 3 but not line 1. A closed executor answers the request into place `3` with a refusal.
  <pre>ENV_002_noAnswerLine env002_mayRefuse ∧ ¬ENV_002 env002_mayRefuse</pre>
- ✓ **nonvacuous** `Libpetri.Spec.ENV_002_nonvacuous` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.ENV_002): Every line of ENV-002 is exercised by the reference, with places `0`, `1`, `2` registered (the test derivation's Java and TypeScript clause): a request into `0` is accepted, and its token `5` lands in place `0` at the next injection step; the closed executor refuses a request into `0` and has no error answer for it; a request into `3` is answered with an error, by the open and by the closed executor, and the state stays as it was.
  <pre>(∃ s',<br>    RefExec env002_C env002_s0 (XLbl.request 0 5 Reply.accepted) s' ∧ s'.eq.length = 1) ∧<br>  (∃ s s', RefExec env002_C s (XLbl.inject 0) s' ∧ s'.M 0 = [5]) ∧<br>    RefExec env002_C env002_sClosed (XLbl.request 0 5 Reply.refused) env002_sClosed ∧<br>      (¬∃ s', RefExec env002_C env002_sClosed (XLbl.request 0 5 Reply.error) s') ∧<br>        RefExec env002_C env002_s0 (XLbl.request 3 5 Reply.error) env002_s0 ∧<br>          RefExec env002_C env002_sClosed (XLbl.request 3 5 Reply.error) env002_sClosed ∧<br>            ¬∃ s', RefExec env002_C env002_sClosed (XLbl.request 3 5 Reply.refused) s'</pre>
- ✓ **consistent** `Libpetri.Spec.spec_consistent_exec_sketch` (Libpetri.Spec.ConsistencyExec): ✓ The executor requirements hold together, over one model: the reference validator, the reference executor with its expiry handling, the reference queue firing and the reference timed step satisfy every executor block of wave W5 and the Phase 1 blocks they share a variable with; the executor settles admitted completions as the validator decides, agrees with the queue firing (L2) and with the timed step (L3), and takes the steps of both coverage conditions.
  <pre>∀ {N T : Type} [inst : DecidableEq N],<br>  ∃ V E X Q R,<br>    (EXEC_021 E ∧ IO_015 V ∧ ValidatedBy E V) ∧<br>      (EXEC_001 E ∧<br>          EXEC_003 E ∧<br>            EXEC_022 E ∧<br>              EXEC_030 E ∧<br>                EXEC_031 E ∧ EXEC_040 E ∧ EXEC_041 E ∧ EXEC_042 E ∧ TIME_014 E) ∧<br>        (CONC_001 E ∧ CONC_002 E ∧ CONC_003 E ∧ CONC_010 E) ∧<br>          (ENV_002 E ∧<br>              ENV_003 E ∧<br>                ENV_004 E ∧<br>                  ENV_005 E ∧<br>                    ENV_006 E ∧<br>                      ENV_010 E ∧<br>                        ENV_011 E ∧ ENV_013 E ∧ ENV_014 E ∧ ENV_015 E ∧ ENV_016 E X) ∧<br>            (EXEC_002_cycle E ∧<br>                EXEC_010_cycle E ∧<br>                  EXEC_013_cycle E ∧<br>                    EXEC_020_cycle E ∧<br>                      TIME_010_cycle E ∧<br>                        TIME_012_cycle E ∧<br>                          TIME_013_cycle E ∧ TIME_015_cycle E ∧ CONC_005_cycle E) ∧<br>              (EXEC_010 Q ∧ EXEC_013 Q ∧ EXEC_020 Q ∧ QueueAgrees E Q) ∧<br>                (TIME_010 R ∧ TIME_012 R ∧ TIME_013 R ∧ TIME_015 R ∧ AtomicAgrees E R) ∧<br>                  ExecCovers E ∧ ExecCoversW5 E X</pre>

<a id="Libpetri-Spec-ENV_002_host"></a>
## ENV-002: Environment Place Registration (host of a name-keyed inject)

`Libpetri.Spec.ENV_002_host` · Kind **A** · Scope executors whose inject takes a place name (Rust, Python), and their hosts · Source **verbatim** (spec/06-environment-places.md) · Sign-off **pending** · Statement hash `e10bc7fa91cf3a17`

| Natural language | Plain reading | Lean statement |
|---|---|---|
| Where inject takes a place name (Rust, Python), the host injects only into registered environment places.<br><br>An executor whose inject takes a place name (Rust, Python) deposits an injected token into the place the name resolves to, whether or not that place is registered; for it, registration decides only whether the run waits at quiescence ([ENV-010]) and which arcs the dead-arc report lists ([CORE-037]).<br><br>*Where* an executor's inject takes a place name (Rust, Python), the host *shall* inject only into registered environment places. | 1. For a configuration C and a run tr (a list of steps, each a source state, a label and a target state):<br>2. every request step of tr asks to inject into one of C's environment places. | <pre>fun {N T} C tr ↦<br>  ∀ st ∈ tr, ∀ (p : N) (x : T) (r : Reply), st.2.1 = XLbl.request p x r → p ∈ C.envs</pre> |

**Assumptions**

- Ruling D89 (a). The block is an assumption on the host (kind A), not a behaviour of the executor: a Rust or Python executor answers a request into any place, deposits into the place the name resolves to (an unknown one is retained, CORE-072), and registration feeds only the long-running decision (ENV-010) and the dead-arc report (CORE-037, rust/libpetri-runtime/src/executor.rs). The statement reads only the labels of a run, so it is a predicate on what the host asks, whatever executor answers.
- What the assumption buys is env002_host_transfer: every run of the name-keyed executor env002_nameKeyed (the reference with the registration test removed from its answer, the Rust and Python shape) that meets ENV_002_host is a run of the reference executor RefExec, so every property proved of RefExec runs (the first block of this ID included) holds of the name-keyed executor on the runs of a host that meets it. The assumption is load-bearing: a name-keyed run with one request into an unregistered place is not a run of the reference (env002_host_needed). The verifier's open-system model makes the same assumption (Novel.EnvSemantics.StepCE injects only into a registered environment place), and CORE-037 states it for the dead-arc report ('a host injects tokens only into environment places').
- The second quoted sentence describes the name-keyed executor; it is the model env002_nameKeyed, not a line. AC4 is the one line, and the test derivation's Rust and Python clause says no executor test checks it. AC1 to AC3 and the test derivation's Java and TypeScript clause are the first block's.

**Evidence**

- ✗ **forbids** `Libpetri.Spec.ENV_002_host_forbids_unregistered` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.ENV_002): ✗ A host that injects into the unregistered place `3` does not meet the host block.
  <pre>¬ENV_002_host env002_C<br>    [(env002_s0, XLbl.request 3 5 Reply.accepted, env002Enq env002_s0 3 5)]</pre>
- ✓ **nonvacuous** `Libpetri.Spec.ENV_002_host_nonvacuous` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.ENV_002): The host block is met by a run of the reference with a request into the registered place `0` that is accepted.
  <pre>XRun RefExec env002_C env002_s0<br>    [(env002_s0, XLbl.request 0 5 Reply.accepted, env002Enq env002_s0 0 5)] ∧<br>  ENV_002_host env002_C<br>    [(env002_s0, XLbl.request 0 5 Reply.accepted, env002Enq env002_s0 0 5)]</pre>

## ENV-003: inject() Thread Safety

`Libpetri.Spec.ENV_003` · Kind **B** · Scope all executors with environment places · Source **verbatim** (spec/06-environment-places.md) · Sign-off **pending** · Statement hash `4f0ea3d47f651a6d`

| Natural language | Plain reading | Lean statement |
|---|---|---|
| The inject operation is safe to call from any thread, task, or coroutine — not just the orchestrator thread.<br><br>It enqueues the token for processing on the next orchestrator cycle.<br><br>*When* the executor accepts an `inject()` call, it *shall* append the event to the tail of its queue of accepted events, as a new entry under a fresh ticket that identifies the call, and *shall not* change the marking or any other part of its state, except that it moves its ticket supply on and wakes the orchestrator if it is waiting ([ENV-005]).<br><br>*When* the orchestrator injects an accepted event, it *shall* take the oldest entry of the queue, *shall* remove that entry from the queue, *shall* add its token at the tail of its place (glossary: Queue order) and *shall not* change any other place.<br><br>The executor *shall not* change its queue of accepted events in any other way than appending a newly accepted event, injecting the oldest entry, discarding entries once it is closed ([ENV-013]) or terminated immediately ([ENV-015]), and emptying the queue when the run ends ([EXEC-041]), so that it injects accepted events in the order it accepted them.<br><br>*When* the executor discards queued events or the run ends, the executor *shall* only remove entries from its queue of accepted events and *shall* keep the remaining entries in the order it accepted them.<br><br>The **Assumptions**

- The model is an executor R : XRel N T (glossary GlossaryExec.lean): R C s l s' says that under configuration C the step labelled l leads from executor state s to s'. A caller's inject() is the outside step request p x r with the reply r; the event queue eq holds the accepted events with their tickets, drawn from the supply nextId that firing identities share. The witness is the reference executor RefExec (Reference/Exec.lean), the graph of a step function checked rule by rule against the Rust executor.
- AC1 and AC2 (inject() callable from a thread other than the orchestrator's, concurrent calls without data races) are kind Q: threads, locks and memory visibility are not in the model. The model reads them at the grain of interleaving: request is an outside step (CONC-001), offered by the reference in every phase of a running loop, so an injection can arrive between any two executor steps; that it is offered at all is coverage of the consistency theorem, not a line here. The Java ConcurrentLinkedQueue, the TypeScript single thread and the Rust FIFO channel are what make the step atomic, and the tests are the evidence (coverage matrix: Rust only).
- The first quoted sentence ('safe to call from any thread') is AC1 and AC2, kind Q as above. The second ('It enqueues the token for processing on the next orchestrator cycle') is lines 1 and 6 and the coverage clause Env003Covers. Line 1 is the enqueue: the token does not land in the marking at the call (ENV_003_forbids_atCall: the Novel spike ApplyInPlace). Env003Covers is the processing: in step 2, with no terminal place marked and the executor neither closed nor stopped, the orchestrator can inject the oldest queued event (env003_covers_noInject: a step 2 that never injects is stuck with the event queued, a run that never finishes, which line 6 alone does not see; it meets every line and fails the clause). The cycle position is EXEC-001's and CONC-010's: an event queued when step 2 begins is injected before that cycle's enablement update (EXEC-001 line 5, step 2 ends only with an empty queue), and the wait never parks with an event queued (CONC-010 line 1, ENV-005). Ruling D70 (a) and clash env-a#8: Rust injects in the wait as well as in step 2 (the wait's signal arm), so lines 2 and 6 say 'the orchestrator injects it', never which phase; the reference offers inject in step 2 and in the wait, and Env003Covers asks only for step 2.
- The first EARS sentence is line 1: an accepted request changes only the event queue, by appending its entry at the tail (ENV_003_forbids_headQueue: a stack), the ticket supply, by moving on so that the entry has a ticket of its own (ENV_003_forbids_reusesTicket: two queued entries share a ticket, so ENV-004 cannot tell their answers apart), and the parked flag, which it clears: 'wakes the orchestrator if it is waiting' reads as the flag false after the step, a loop that was blocked is woken and one that was not stays unblocked (ENV_003_forbids_noWake: an accepted request that leaves a blocked loop blocked). ENV-005 line 3 says the same of the flag; ENV-005 builds on this block (its Depends on line names ENV-003), so the [ENV-005] of the sentence is a cross-reference, and ENV-005 is not in this block's Depends on line. Whether a request is accepted, refused or answered with an error is ENV-002's and ENV-006's subject; this block constrains the accepted ones.
- The second EARS sentence is line 2, the new sentence of ruling D48 (a) (events FIFO by acceptance, appended at the tail): an injection takes the head of the queue (ENV_003_forbids_newestFirst), removes it (ENV_003_forbids_keepsQueued: the same event would be injected again) and appends its token at the tail of its place, the glossary's queue order for a deposit (ENV_003_forbids_headOfPlace). The line fixes the marking exactly (qAppendOne), which is the sentence's 'shall not change any other place'. That an injected token writes its place, so a reaped transition with an arc on it is no longer reaped (ruling D6), is the glossary Write entry and TIME-013's companion line; where the loop goes after an injection from the wait is EXEC-001's.
- The third EARS sentence is line 3 and the fourth is line 4. Line 3: no step other than an accepted request, an injection, a discard, an immediate termination or a finish changes the queue (ENV_003_forbids_perPlaceQueues: one queue per place drains place by place and loses the order across places; ENV_003_forbids_clearsAtEnd: an end of step 2 that empties the queue, the TypeScript walk of a fixed prefix followed by clearing the whole queue, drops an event accepted during the walk). Line 4: a discard, an immediate termination and a finish only remove entries and keep the rest in order (ENV_003_forbids_rotates: a discard that moves the head to the tail keeps every event and passes lines 3 and 6). With lines 1 and 2 they give FIFO by acceptance. When a discard may come (only once the executor is closed or stopped) is ENV-004 line 2 and ENV-013; the immediate termination that drops the whole queue is ENV-015; the finish empties the queue (EXEC-041; ENV-004 for the answer each dropped call gets). The reference meets line 4: discard removes the head, and terminateNow and every finish set the queue to empty. A refused request is a step that keeps the queue, as ENV-006 also says. A close keeps the queue and later discard steps drop it, as the Java and TypeScript loops do; Java's close() on an executor whose loop is not running completes the queued calls with false at once (BitmapNetExecutor.close), which the model does not reach: it has no state before the loop starts, and after the finish the queue is already empty.
- The fifth EARS sentence is line 5, the 'fresh ticket' of the first: the supply never goes back, so with line 1 every accepted call gets a ticket no earlier call of the run had. Firing identities draw from the same supply (a start moves it on), so the line also reads EXEC-031's identity supply; the reference never lowers it. The line is load-bearing for line 6, whose watch keeps one flag per ticket: an executor that resets the supply at the enablement update and whose termination test forgets the event queue accepts 7 and 8 under the same ticket 0, injects the 7, and finishes with the 8 never injected and no close, while one injection of ticket 0 pays both acceptances (ENV_003_forbids_resetsSupply). Line 6 reads every start state, including ones whose queue already holds a ticket at or above the supply; from a start state whose queued tickets are distinct and below the supply (every initial state; ENV-004's env004_Fresh), lines 1 to 5 keep them so.
- The sixth EARS sentence is line 6 and the reading of AC3. The markdown's AC3 carries the exception (clash env-a#7, ruling D20): ENV-013 and EXEC-042 drop queued events, so a close (ENV-013), an immediate termination (ENV-015, Java) or a stop because a terminal place is marked (EXEC-042) after the acceptance releases the executor. The reference shows the exception is needed: ENV_003_allows_closeDiscards decides a reference run that finishes with an accepted event discarded after a close. A terminal stop releases only when a terminal place is marked in the state it starts from (Env003.serves): ENV_003_forbids_latchTerminal is the TypeScript terminal latch moved from processExternalEvents into inject() (or Java's isTerminal test next to externalEventQueue.offer), which stops the loop when an event for a terminal place is accepted, before its token is in the marking, and drops an event accepted earlier for another place; EXEC-042's last line catches it too. Rust injects every event sent before its close (one FIFO channel for events and the close signal); that is a run whose close step comes after those injections, and line 6 holds of it either way.
- Line 6 is liveness read on runs that reach their finish (IdealRun, an assumption of kind A of glossary GlossaryExec.lean): on a finite run 'eventually' reads 'before the finish'. A run of an open executor with environment places that is never drained or closed does not finish, and line 6 says nothing about it; there, Env003Covers says the injection is always on offer in step 2, and that the loop takes it rather than stalling is the loop's own fairness, outside the model. Line 6 is load-bearing beyond lines 1 to 5: an executor whose termination test forgets the event queue finishes quiescent with an accepted event never injected (ENV_003_forbids_forgets), the Java or TypeScript loop exit reading only the transitions and the actions in flight. ENV_003_nonvacuous decides reference runs that finish after an injection, so the assumption holds of some runs and the line is not vacuous (onIdealRuns_of_none).
- Its offers are in ExecCoversW5.Env003Covers (ConsistencyExec.lean; the convention of GlossaryExec.lean: offers are coverage clauses, never block lines). The seventh EARS sentence demands an answer and is quoted whole; it has no safety half, and its existence half is that clause: the inject step of the oldest entry exists in every such state, which the reference meets by its inject rule (env003_ref_covers); other steps (a request, a snapshot) may come first, and nothing ends step 2 while an event is queued (EXEC-001 line 5). Depends on: ENV-002 (which places accept), ENV-013, ENV-015, EXEC-041 and EXEC-042 (the releases and drops of lines 3, 4 and 6), EXEC-001 (step 2) and CONC-010 (the wait).
- Scope: Rust run_sync has no signal channel and no inject() (spec/06-environment-places.md, ENV-014's implementation status), so the requirement reads the executors that accept injections. Python rides on the Rust runtime.
- The test derivation (ten threads each inject a token, all ten are processed) is ENV_003_nonvacuous, part 5: ten requests are accepted, the executor drains, the ten tokens are injected in the order they were accepted and land at the tail of place 0 behind its initial token, and the run finishes quiescent; the threads are AC1 and AC2.

## ENV-004: inject() Completion Semantics

`Libpetri.Spec.ENV_004` · Kind **B** · Scope executors with an admission signal (Java, TypeScript); Rust and Python report acceptance only (ruling D44 (a)) · Source **verbatim** (spec/06-environment-places.md) · Sign-off **pending** · Statement hash `7d20bbf9de3d56df`

| Natural language | Plain reading | Lean statement |
|---|---|---|
| In Java and TypeScript the inject operation returns a future/promise that completes with true when the token has been added to the marking.<br><br>In Rust and Python the return value indicates whether the injection was accepted; in Java and TypeScript the future's value indicates whether the token was injected.<br><br>In Java and TypeScript the future is the admission signal of the accepted event.<br><br>The orchestrator completes it with true in the external-events step ([EXEC-001] step 2), when it adds the token to the marking.<br><br>It completes it with false when it discards the event because the executor is closed or stopped ([ENV-013], [ENV-015]), or when the run ends with the event still queued ([EXEC-041], [EXEC-042]).<br><br>A drain does not discard the events accepted before it: the orchestrator still injects them ([ENV-011]), unless close() is called or the run ends first.<br><br>Each accepted event has an admission signal of its own: an injection into a place whose earlier event is still queued neither replaces that event nor merges with it ([ENV-003]).<br><br>*When* the executor accepts an injection request, it *shall* queue the event as a new event, apart from every event already queued.<br><br>*When* the executor completes the admission signal of an accepted event with true, it *shall*, in the same step, add the event's token at the tail of its place's queue and change no other part of the marking.<br><br>*If* the executor completes the admission signal of an accepted event with false, *then* it *shall* leave the marking unchanged in that step.<br><br>*If* a step leaves the executor open or draining and does not end the run, *then* the executor *shall not* complete the admission signal of an accepted event with false in that step.<br><br>The executor *shall* complete the admission signal of an accepted event at most once. | 1. For every executor R and every configuration C, and in the first three lines for every ticket k:<br>2. an inject step of k (the admission signal of k completes with true) starts in a state whose event queue holds an event with ticket k for some place p and token x, and its marking is the source marking with x appended at the tail of p and no other change;<br>3. a step that removes the ticket k from the event queue and is not the inject step of k (the signal completes with false) leaves the marking unchanged, and after it the executor is closed or stopped, or the run has finished;<br>4. on every run of R that starts in a state whose queued events carry pairwise distinct tickets, each below the ticket supply, at most one step answers k (injects it, or removes it from the queue otherwise);<br>5. an accepted injection request made in a state whose queued events carry pairwise distinct tickets, each below the ticket supply, leaves some ticket queued that was not queued before it. | <pre>fun {N T} [DecidableEq N] R ↦<br>  ∀ (C : Cfg N T),<br>    (∀ (k : ℕ),<br>        (on fun s s' ↦ R C s (XLbl.inject k) s', shall fun s s' ↦<br>            ∃ p x, (k, p, x) ∈ s.eq ∧ s'.M = qAppendOne s.M p x) ∧<br>          (∀ (s : XSt N T) (l : XLbl N T) (s' : XSt N T),<br>              R C s l s' →<br>                env004_isDrop k (s, l, s') = true →<br>                  s'.M = s.M ∧ (s'.mode.closing = true ∨ isExecPhase s'.phase = false)) ∧<br>            ∀ (s0 : XSt N T) (tr : List (XStep N T)),<br>              env004_Fresh s0 → XRun R C s0 tr → (at-most-once env004_answers k) tr) ∧<br>      on fun s s' ↦ env004_Fresh s ∧ ∃ p x, R C s (XLbl.request p x Reply.accepted) s',<br>        shall fun s s' ↦ ∃ j ∉ env004_tickets s, j ∈ env004_tickets s'</pre> |

**Assumptions**

- The model is an executor R : XRel N T (glossary GlossaryExec.lean): R C s l s' says that under configuration C the step labelled l leads from executor state s to s'. An accepted request (request p x accepted, ENV-003, ENV-006) queues the event (k, p, x) in s.eq with the ticket k = s.nextId and advances the supply. The admission signal is not part of the state: the block reads it off the steps. The true answer of ticket k is the label inject k; the false answer is every other step after which k is no longer queued. In the reference those are discard k (once the executor is closed or stopped), terminateNow (ENV-015, ruling D47 (c): Java completes the queued events with false inside terminateNow) and the finish steps that clear the queue (finish closed, stopped or terminal; design R17). The witness is the reference executor RefExec (Reference/Exec.lean).
- One signal for ENV-004 and ENV-006. ENV-006's line 4 and this block both name the answering steps by what they do to the queue (the injection of k, or a step that takes the event with ticket k out of the event queue): ENV-006's answersTicket and this block's env004_answers are equal on every step (env004_answers_eq_answersTicket, ConsistencyExec.lean), which is what lets lines 1 and 2 constrain the value and the marking effect of every answer ENV-006 asks for. On every reference step from a state with distinct queued tickets both also agree with a label-based restatement, env004_labelAnswers (the injection or the discard of k, or an immediate termination or a finish while k is queued; ENV_004_answers_agree_reference), so the reference answers one ticket at one step in both blocks.
- Scope, ruling D44 (a). Only Java and TypeScript have an admission signal, as the first two quoted sentences now say. Rust and Python return, at the call, whether the event was accepted; that reply is the request step's, stated by ENV-006 (and ENV-002 for a place that is not an environment place). The quoted second sentence keeps the two meanings apart: the call's reply says whether the request was accepted (ENV-006's lines 1 and 2), the future's value says whether the token was injected (lines 1 and 2 here), so an accepted event can still be answered false. A run of RefExec in which the close comes after the injections of the events sent before it is Rust's behaviour at a close (ruling D44 (a)), so the shared model holds both. Result-less forms (Java injectAsync, TypeScript injectNoAwait) have no signal to complete and are outside the block.
- Ruling D44 (a), from env-a ENV-R3: the old clause that the signal completes after enablement has been recalculated is dropped. Java and TypeScript complete the signal inside the external-events step, before the enablement update of step 3, and line 1 reads exactly that step: the inject step is the one that deposits. The quoted first, third and fourth sentences are line 1 for what the answering step changes. Which loop phase the inject step runs in is EXEC-001's subject, not this block's: EXEC-001's line 5 orders the injections of step 2 before the next update, and ruling D70 (a) lets the wait itself inject (Rust, which has no signal; the reference offers inject in the phases events and await). Line 1 therefore has no phase condition, and the step-2 placement in the fourth quoted sentence is checked there.
- AC1 (true when the token is in the marking) is line 1: the inject step of k appends the event's token at the tail of its place and changes the marking in no other way. An executor that answers true and lands the token later, through another queue, breaks it (ENV_004_forbids_earlyTrue). The first part of ENV_004_nonvacuous is the test derivation: a request is accepted, the event is injected, and after the answer the token is in its place.
- AC2 has two halves. The call-time half, an inject() call made while the executor is draining, closed or finished is refused and changes nothing, is ENV-006's lines 1 and 2 (ENV_006.lean: Refusing is a mode that is not open, or a finished run, which is where the 'or finished' of AC2 comes from); this block does not restate it. The queued half is line 2 and the quoted fifth sentence: an accepted event is answered false only once the executor is closed or stopped, or when the run ends with the event still queued (ENV_004_nonvacuous parts three and four), and the false answer leaves the marking unchanged (ENV_004_forbids_discardDeposits). AC2's drain clause and the quoted drain sentence are line 2's mode half: while the executor drains and the run goes on, no queued event is answered false. An executor that discards a queued event because the executor is draining when step 2 reaches it breaks that half (ENV_004_forbids_falseWhileDraining), while the reference injects an event accepted before a drain and answers it true (ENV_004_nonvacuous part two). The clause allows a false answer during a drain when the run ends (a terminal place marked, EXEC-042) or close() escalates the drain (ENV-013), which is why AC2 does not promise true for every event queued before a drain. That such an event is in the end injected is ENV-011's and ENV-006's line 4, not this block's.
- AC3 (at most once) is line 3 and the last quoted sentence. An executor that injects the event but leaves it queued, then discards it at a close, answers it twice (true, then false) and breaks only line 3 (ENV_004_forbids_trueThenDiscard, env004_trueThenDiscard_onlyLine3). The line identifies the event by its ticket. Tickets are drawn once from one supply (the naming convention of the glossary, shared with firing identities), and the premise says that at the start of the run the queued tickets are distinct and below the supply: true at every initial state (the queue is empty) and kept by every reference step (env004_fresh_shape). Without it the reference itself answers a duplicated ticket twice (env004_needs_fresh). An executor that hands out a ticket already queued answers it twice along the run and breaks line 3 as well.
- Line 4 is the quoted sentence on an admission signal of its own and the EARS sentence on queueing the event as a new event. Without it an executor that keeps the pending injections per place, so that a second accepted request into the same place overwrites the first event's token under the first event's ticket, keeps lines 1 to 3 (env004_coalesce_onlyLine4: no ticket ever leaves the queue without its inject step), yet one of the two callers told accepted never sees its token reach the marking. Line 4 rejects it (ENV_004_forbids_coalesce). ENV-003's line 1 pins the exact ticket (the supply's next one), the place, the token and the FIFO position of the new event (ruling D48 (a)); line 4 keeps only what the signal needs, a ticket of its own.
- Lines 2 and 3 together say that a token answered false never reaches the marking through its own event: the drop leaves the marking unchanged, and no later inject step answers the same ticket. The quoted sentences on which events a close discards are ENV-013's subject, the FIFO order of injection is ENV-003's (ruling D48 (a)), and that every accepted event is eventually answered is ENV-006's line 4; this block reads only the answering step and what it changes.
- Out of the model: a deposit that throws, which Java and TypeScript report by completing the signal exceptionally (the model's deposit cannot fail, so line 3 says at most one answer, not exactly one); the TokenAdded event of the injection (the event tier, W7). Java and TypeScript leave the events queued at a close and complete them with false when the loop ends, after the firings in flight; the reference discards them in step 2 of the cycles after the close. Both are after the close and before the end of the run, and line 2 constrains only which step answers false and what it changes, not how long after the close it comes.

- ✗ **forbids** `Libpetri.Spec.ENV_004_forbids_earlyTrue` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.ENV_004): ✗ An early true answer violates ENV-004 (line 1): the inject step of ticket `0` answers while place `0` is still empty.

<a id="Libpetri-Spec-ENV_005"></a>
## ENV-005: inject() Wake-Up

`Libpetri.Spec.ENV_005` · Kind **T** · Scope all executors · Source **verbatim** (spec/06-environment-places.md) · Sign-off **pending** · Statement hash `29befa0357c21bc6`

| Natural language | Plain reading | Lean statement |
|---|---|---|
| Injecting a token wakes the orchestrator from idle immediately.<br><br>The orchestrator does not need to wait for a timer or poll.<br><br>An injection is queued from the moment inject() accepts it ([ENV-003]) until it leaves the queue: the executor puts its token into the marking, or, once the executor is closed or stopped or the run has ended, discards it ([ENV-013], [ENV-015], [EXEC-042]).<br><br>An injection that inject() accepts after the external-events step of a cycle has last read the queue counts as accepted after that step ends, and is left to the next cycle.<br><br>*While* an accepted injection is queued, the executor *shall not* block in its wait ([EXEC-001] step 6, [CONC-010]), neither at the end of a cycle nor again after it has answered something during the wait, such as a marking snapshot.<br><br>*When* inject() accepts a token, the executor *shall* end any block of its wait at once, without waiting for a timer.<br><br>*While* an accepted injection is queued and the executor is in its wait with no terminal place marked, the executor *shall* be able to leave the wait at once, by waking up or by taking a queued injection from the queue, without waiting for a timer.<br><br>*While* an accepted injection is queued, the executor *shall not* end the external-events step of a cycle and *shall not* start the enablement update of a cycle ([EXEC-001] steps 2 and 3).<br><br>Read with the definition of queued above, this means that a token accepted while the executor waits has left the queue before the enablement update of the cycle the wake-up starts, and is in the marking by then unless the run has closed, stopped or ended first; the earlier sentences mean that no timer or polling is needed to find it.<br><br>The requirement on the external-events step covers every injection queued during that step, not only those queued when it begins ([EXEC-001] step 2), so the step has no limit on how many injections it takes.<br><br>The words immediately, promptly and at once mean that nothing in the executor waits between the acceptance and the injection; the latency itself is tested, not proven.<br><br>Under a host clock an implementation may leave the wait to the host ([TIME-015]); the wait these sentences speak of is then the host's, and [TIME-015] requires its readiness predicate to observe the queued injection. | 1. For every executor R and every configuration C:<br>2. (1) no park step starts in a state whose event queue is not empty;<br>3. (2) no step of any label goes from a state that is not parked to a parked one when the event queue of its start state is not empty;<br>4. (3) for every place p and token x, a request step for (p, x) answered accepted ends in a state that is not parked;<br>5. (4) no step that ends the external-events step (endEvents) starts in a state whose event queue is not empty;<br>6. (5) no step goes from a state outside the enablement update phase into it when the event queue of its start state is not empty. | <pre>fun {N T} [DecidableEq N] R ↦<br>  ∀ (C : Cfg N T),<br>    (while fun s ↦ s.eq ≠ [], never fun s s' ↦ ∃ tmr, R C s (XLbl.park tmr) s') ∧<br>      (while fun s ↦ s.eq ≠ [], never fun s s' ↦<br>          s.parked = false ∧ s'.parked = true ∧ ∃ l, R C s l s') ∧<br>        (∀ (p : N) (x : T),<br>            on fun s s' ↦ R C s (XLbl.request p x Reply.accepted) s', shall fun x s' ↦<br>              s'.parked = false) ∧<br>          (while fun s ↦ s.eq ≠ [], never fun s s' ↦ R C s XLbl.endEvents s') ∧<br>            while fun s ↦ s.eq ≠ [], never fun s s' ↦<br>              s.phase ≠ Phase.update ∧ s'.phase = Phase.update ∧ ∃ l, R C s l s'</pre> |

**Assumptions**

- The model is an executor R : XRel N T (glossary GlossaryExec.lean): R C s l s' says that under configuration C the step labelled l leads from executor state s to s'. The outside step request p x r is a call of inject(); r = accepted is the call accepting the token, which queues it with a ticket in XSt.eq (ENV-003). Step 2 of a cycle takes queued injections into the marking one at a time (inject k, at the tail of the place, FIFO by ticket) or, once closed or stopped, discards them (discard k, ENV-013), and ends with endEvents, after which the enablement update (phase update) runs. The wait is the loop phase await; park is the loop blocking in it and XSt.parked marks the block; wake is its end (a timer, a spurious wake-up or an arrival), after which the loop runs step 1 again; an injection may also be taken straight from the wait (inject k or discard k from phase await). The witness is the reference executor RefExec (Reference/Exec.lean), checked rule by rule against the Rust executor.
- Definition of queued: an injection is queued while its ticket is in XSt.eq. The reference takes a ticket out by inject k (into the marking), by discard k (closed or stopped, ENV-013), by terminateNow (ENV-015, the queue dropped at once) and by a finish step (the end of the run: quiescent, closed, or a marked terminal place, EXEC-042). The linearization sentence is how a run places a request: the request is an atomic outside step whose place in a run is the moment the runtime's step 2 can see the event. Java polls its external queue until it is empty and Rust drains its channel with try_recv until it is empty, so an event sent after the last read is a request after endEvents; TypeScript walks the prefix queued when step 2 begins, and an inject() made inside that step (from an event store append) is likewise a request after endEvents. Such an event goes to the next cycle, which lines 1 and 2 and the coverage clause Env005Covers make the loop reach without blocking.
- AC1 (the orchestrator is idle, no ready transitions) is the precondition of the lines, not a criterion of its own, and the lines drop it: they bind every accepted injection, idle or not. The idle orchestrator is the loop in its wait, blocked (parked) or about to block. Its blocking is constrained by lines 1 and 2: it may block only with nothing queued, and the rest of the park guard (nothing Ready or Expired at the cycle reading, the timer bound) is CONC-010's.
- Its offers are in ExecCoversW5.Env005Covers (ConsistencyExec.lean; the convention of GlossaryExec.lean: offers are coverage clauses, never block lines). The third EARS sentence (the executor shall be able to leave the wait at once) demands an answer and is quoted whole; it has no safety half among the lines, and its existence half is that clause. AC2 and the first description sentence's 'wakes the orchestrator' are line 3 and Env005Covers. Line 3 is the observable block marker: an accepted request clears it (ENV_005_forbids_deafRequest: an executor whose request leaves the marker set breaks it). Env005Covers is the behaviour: a live wait with an injection queued can always be left by the executor's own step, a wake or the injection or discard of a queued ticket, so leaving it never needs a timer; the reference meets it (env005_ref_covers). An inject() that queues the token but never signals the wait, so that only a completion, a drain, a close or a timer could end it, meets every line and fails that clause (env005_covers_unsignalled). Lines 1 and 2 keep the loop from blocking again while the token is queued (ENV_005_forbids_parkWithQueued: a polling executor that blocks with the token queued; ENV_005_forbids_reblock: a wait that answers a snapshot and blocks again). Together they are the second description sentence: no timer and no poll is needed to find the token. Line 3 holds for every accepted request, whether or not the loop was blocked; a request answered refused or error queues nothing and is ENV-006's and ENV-002's.
- AC3 is lines 4 and 5 for 'within one cycle': step 2 does not end, and the enablement update does not start, while an injection is queued, so a token accepted while the loop waits has left the queue before the enablement update of the cycle the wake-up starts, and while the executor is open it is in the marking then and the transitions it enables are judged in that cycle (ENV_005_nonvacuous part 4). An executor that ends step 2 with an injection still queued, for instance one event per cycle, breaks line 4 (ENV_005_forbids_leavesQueued); one that skips step 2 and takes injections only from the wait reaches the update with the token queued and breaks line 5 (ENV_005_forbids_skipsEvents). EXEC-001 line 5 states the phase-entry form (the tickets queued when step 2 begins leave the queue before the next update); lines 4 and 5 read it on every queued ticket, as the markdown says, so no cap on the events per cycle is allowed. The consequence sentence ('Read with the definition of queued above') is lines 4 and 5 with the definition of queued; it is a reading, not a separate line.
- Kind Q, outside the lines: 'immediately' and 'promptly' in AC2 and AC3, 'at once' in the EARS sentences, and 'within milliseconds' in the test derivation, are latencies; the model gives steps no duration, so they are tested, not proven, as the markdown says. The lines say that nothing in the executor waits between the acceptance and the injection: no block, no missing way out of the wait, no deferral to a later cycle.
- Closed, stopped and ended runs: all five lines hold in every mode. Once the executor is closed or stopped a queued injection is discarded instead of put into the marking (ENV-013), an immediate termination drops the queue at once (ENV-015), and a finish clears it (EXEC-042 for a marked terminal place); these are the exits of the definition of queued and the 'unless' clause of the consequence sentence. Env005Covers asks nothing once a terminal place is marked: the loop then finishes (finish terminal). A request after a drain or a close is refused (ENV-006) and queues nothing. Java and TypeScript keep a pre-close event in their queue, unanswered, until the loop ends, and may block in the wait for the action in flight meanwhile; the sentence 'Once the executor is closed, an event that Java or TypeScript still holds in its queue counts as discarded from the first external-events step or wait after the close, though its inject() is answered only when the loop ends ([ENV-013], [ENV-004]).' is the reading: a Java or TypeScript run is the model run whose discard steps for those events come in the first step 2 or wait after the close, so the queue the lines read is empty before the wait blocks. The late answer is ENV-004's.
- Host clock (TIME-015, clash env-a#9): under an injected host clock an implementation may stop raising its own wake-up (Java returns before releasing its wake-up semaphore when a host clock is installed) and leave the wait to the host, whose wait returns when the readiness predicate holds; Java's predicate reads the external queue. The model has one wait for both cases: under a host clock, the wait and its block marker stand for the host's wait, and line 3 and Env005Covers are met when the predicate reports the queued injection, which TIME-015's visibility duty requires. The host's own wait and the predicate are TIME-015's and outside the model; the markdown sentence is informative and puts the duty on TIME-015.
- Depends on: CONC-010 (lines 1 and 3 are its park guard and arrival line restricted to the event queue), ENV-003 (acceptance and the queue), EXEC-001 (steps 2, 3 and 6), and, for the definition of queued and the consequence sentence, ENV-013, ENV-015 and EXEC-042; TIME-015 for the host-clock sentence. The test derivation (start an executor with an environment place, wait for quiescence, inject a token, check that it is processed) is ENV_005_nonvacuous: the loop blocks with nothing queued, a request is accepted and clears the block, a wake-up is offered, step 2 of the next cycle injects the token, and the transition it enables starts in that cycle.

<a id="Libpetri-Spec-ENV_006"></a>
## ENV-006: inject() Rejection on Closed or Draining Executor

`Libpetri.Spec.ENV_006` · Kind **B** · Scope all executors with environment places · Source **verbatim** (spec/06-environment-places.md) · Sign-off **pending** · Statement hash `e83694d8299d74c7`

| Natural language | Plain reading | Lean statement |
|---|---|---|
| If the executor has been closed, is draining, or execution has completed, inject() returns an error or false rather than silently dropping the token.<br><br>*If* `inject()` is called while the executor is draining, closed or stopped ([ENV-011], [ENV-013], [ENV-015]), or after the run has finished, *then* it *shall* return an error or `false`.<br><br>*If* `inject()` is called while the executor is draining, closed or stopped, or after the run has finished, *then* the executor *shall* change nothing: the token *shall not* reach the marking, and no event *shall* be queued for injection.<br><br>Each accepted injection *shall* stay an event of its own until it is injected, discarded or dropped: the executor *shall not* merge two accepted injections into one.<br><br>*Where* `inject()` returns an admission signal ([ENV-004]), *when* a run that accepted an injection finishes, the executor *shall* have completed the signal of that injection, with the value [ENV-004] gives: by injecting the token, by discarding the event on a close ([ENV-013]), by dropping it on an immediate termination ([ENV-015]), or by dropping it at the finish of the run while it is still queued. | 1. For every executor R and every configuration C:<br>2. while the executor is draining, closed or stopped, or its run has finished, it accepts no injection request;<br>3. an injection request made in such a state leaves the executor state unchanged, whatever it answers;<br>4. on every run of R, at most one injection request is accepted with a given ticket k (the next identity of the state it is made in);<br>5. on every run of R under C that reaches its finish, every injection request accepted with ticket k is followed by a step that answers k: the injection of k, or a step that takes the event with ticket k out of the event queue (a discard on a close, an immediate termination, or a finish). | <pre>fun {N T} [DecidableEq N] R ↦<br>  ∀ (C : Cfg N T),<br>    (while fun s ↦ Env006.Refusing s, never fun s s' ↦<br>        ∃ p x, R C s (XLbl.request p x Reply.accepted) s') ∧<br>      (on fun s s' ↦ Env006.Refusing s ∧ ∃ p x r, R C s (XLbl.request p x r) s', shall<br>          fun s s' ↦ s' = s) ∧<br>        (∀ (s0 : XSt N T) (k : ℕ) (tr : List (XStep N T)),<br>            XRun R C s0 tr → (at-most-once acceptsTicket k) tr) ∧<br>          ∀ (s0 : XSt N T) (k : ℕ),<br>            on-ideal-runs IdealRun R C s0, shall fun tr ↦<br>              (when acceptsTicket k, shall Env006.answersTicket k) tr</pre> |

**Assumptions**

- The model is an executor R : XRel N T (glossary GlossaryExec.lean): R C s l s' says that under configuration C the step labelled l leads from executor state s to s'. A call of inject() is the outside step request p x r: the caller asks to inject token x into place p and the executor answers r, which is accepted, refused (false) or error. An accepted request queues the event in the event queue (XSt.eq) with a ticket, the executor's next identity (XSt.nextId, the one supply of firing identities and event tickets), and the orchestrator later injects it (inject k), discards it once closed (discard k), or drops it with the whole queue on an immediate termination (terminateNow) or a finish (finish c). The witness is the reference executor RefExec (Reference/Exec.lean), checked rule by rule against the Rust executor: ExecutorHandle::inject (executor_handle.rs 67-74) refuses once the handle drained or closed, and the Event arm of handle_signal injects.
- 'Draining, closed or stopped, or finished' is the glossary-free predicate Refusing of this block: the mode is not open (draining, closed, or stopped by the immediate termination of ENV-015), or the loop phase is done. The body's 'execution has completed' is the finished run (phase done, after any finish step). The markdown's scope note on a terminal place (EXEC-042) says the same: a run whose terminal place is marked but whose finish step has not yet been taken is still running, a request there is accepted, and the finish terminal step that follows drops the event, which answers it false (line 4). TypeScript refuses at the call already once a terminal place is marked; that answer is false as well, so the two shapes agree on what the caller learns.
- Ruling D44 (a), one injector per executor: lines 1 and 2 read the lifecycle as shared by every injector, as in Java, TypeScript and Python (one handle per executor). In Rust the drained flag belongs to the ExecutorHandle: a second sender on the same channel is answered true after another handle drained or closed, and the executor drops that event on receipt (executor_core/executor.rs 1394-1396), unreported. The markdown's scope note says so; the model has one injector, an assumption of kind A for Rust, under which a handle's own drain or close is the executor's. The token still never reaches the marking in Rust, which is the part of line 2 every sender keeps.
- Line 1 is the first shall sentence: no request is answered accepted in a refusing state, so the answer is error (a place that is not an environment place, ENV-002's subject) or refused (false). AC1 (after a close, inject() returns error or false) and AC2 (after drain(), inject() returns error or false) are line 1 at a closed and at a draining state; ENV_006_nonvacuous exercises both, and a finished run as well. An executor that answers accepted while draining and drops the token, the silent drop the body sentence forbids, breaks line 1 (ENV_006_forbids_silentDrop); one that treats draining as open and queues the event breaks lines 1 and 2 (ENV_006_forbids_acceptWhileDraining).
- Line 2 is the second shall sentence, read as 'changes nothing': the state after the request is the state before it, so the token reaches neither the marking nor the event queue, nor any other queue a later step would deposit from. An executor that answers refused and queues the event all the same, so that the orchestrator injects it while draining, breaks line 2 alone (ENV_006_forbids_refusedButQueued). Java refuses after the run ended by queueing the event and discarding it at once; at the grain of the model that is one refused request that changes nothing.
- Its offers are in ExecCoversW5.Env006Covers (ConsistencyExec.lean; the convention of GlossaryExec.lean: offers are coverage clauses, never block lines). The body sentence and the first EARS sentence demand an answer and are quoted whole; their safety half is line 1, and their existence half is that clause. The 'shall return' of the first shall sentence is Env006Covers: from every refusing state a request into any place with any token has a step, so inject() returns an answer rather than blocking (ENV-015 AC3 says the same after an immediate termination). With line 1 that answer is error or refused, with line 2 it changes nothing. Env006Covers reads every refusing state, reachable or not; the reference's request rule answers in every state (env006_ref_covers). An executor whose inject() blocks once the executor drains, closes or finishes has no request step there, so it meets every line (lines 1 and 2 with no refusing request at all) and fails that clause (env006_covers_hang).
- Line 3 is the third shall sentence: an accepted injection is told apart by its ticket, so 'an event of its own' reads as at most one acceptance per ticket on every run. Without it line 4 could not tell two acceptances under one ticket apart, and one answer would pay for both. The reference draws tickets from a supply that no step lowers and an accepted request raises (env006_nextId_le). An executor that does not raise the supply on an accepted request, and so accepts a second injection under the ticket of a queued one and forgets it, meets line 4 (the injection of that ticket answers both acceptances) and breaks line 3 (ENV_006_forbids_sharedTicket): the second token never reaches the marking.
- Line 4 is the fourth shall sentence and AC3, which ruling D44 (a) rewords to 'where an admission signal exists, every accepted injection completes it'. A step answers ticket k when it injects k (the signal completes with true) or takes the event with ticket k out of the queue without injecting it (false): the discard of k on a close, an immediate termination, or a finish, each of which empties the queue in the reference. That is ENV-004's reading of an answer (env004_answers); the values of the signal, and which steps may drop an event, are ENV-004's lines, as the sentence says ('with the value ENV-004 gives'), and this line says that every accepted injection reaches one of those steps. It reads only runs that reach their finish (IdealRun, an assumption of kind A: every action returns and the executor is drained, closed or quiescent); a net that never finishes has no ideal run, so ENV_006_nonvacuous decides four ideal runs, one per kind of answer. An executor that answers accepted while open and never queues the event (accept and forget) meets lines 1 to 3 and breaks line 4 on a run that drains and finishes (ENV_006_forbids_forget). So does an executor whose finish leaves the queued events queued, the slip of dropping the end-of-run completion of what is still queued (Java's drainPendingExternalEvents() in the executeLoop finally block, TypeScript's after the loop of run): the future or promise of such an event stays pending forever (ENV_006_forbids_finishKeepsQueue).
- Scope of line 4: Java and TypeScript return an admission signal. Rust and Python report acceptance only (ENV-004, ruling D44 (a)), so an accepted event that a stop on a terminal place drops is not reported to their caller; the model still requires the executor to inject, discard or drop every accepted event by the finish, which is the step a signal would complete at, and the markdown's scope note says so for Rust and Python. The result-less forms (TypeScript's injectNoAwait, Java's injectAsync) report nothing and are outside this requirement, as the scope note says; on a draining, closed or finished executor they drop the token without an answer, which at the grain of the model is lines 1 and 2 and Env006Covers with an answer nobody reads.
- The test derivation (run to completion, inject, error; drain, inject, error) is ENV_006_nonvacuous's refused requests after a finish and after a drain.

**Evidence**

- ✓ **holds** `Libpetri.Spec.ENV_006_reference` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.ENV_006): ✓ The reference executor satisfies ENV-006: `replyFor` accepts only while open and running, a request it does not accept returns the state unchanged (`requestStep_some`), the ticket supply never goes down and an acceptance raises it (`env006_nextId_le`), and every step that does not answer a queued ticket keeps it queued and the run going (`env006_keep`).
  <pre>∀ {N T : Type} [inst : DecidableEq N], ENV_006 RefExec</pre>
- ✗ **forbids** `Libpetri.Spec.ENV_006_forbids_acceptWhileDraining` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.ENV_006): ✗ Accepting while draining violates ENV-006 (line 1, AC2): after a drain, a request into place `0` is answered `accepted` and queued.
  <pre>¬ENV_006 env006_acceptWhileDraining</pre>
- ✗ **forbids** `Libpetri.Spec.ENV_006_forbids_finishKeepsQueue` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.ENV_006): ✗ A finish that keeps the queue violates ENV-006 (line 4, AC3): the request into place `0` is accepted after step 2, the executor closes and finishes closed with the event still queued, and no step takes it out of the queue, so its future or promise stays pending forever. Its requests are the reference's, so lines 1 to 3 do not reject it.
  <pre>¬ENV_006 env006_finishKeepsQueue</pre>
- ✗ **forbids** `Libpetri.Spec.ENV_006_forbids_forget` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.ENV_006): ✗ Accept and forget violates ENV-006 (line 4, AC3): the request into place `0` is accepted while open, the executor drains and finishes quiescent, and ticket `0` is never injected, discarded or dropped by a finish. Lines 1 and 2 speak only of refusing states, and it raises the ticket supply as the reference does (line 3), so they do not reject it.
  <pre>¬ENV_006 env006_forget</pre>
- ✗ **forbids** `Libpetri.Spec.ENV_006_forbids_refusedButQueued` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.ENV_006): ✗ Refusing and queueing all the same violates ENV-006 (line 2): after a drain, the refused request into place `0` queues the event, which a later step 2 would inject. Its reply is `refused`, so line 1 alone does not reject it.
  <pre>¬ENV_006 env006_refusedButQueued</pre>
- ✗ **forbids** `Libpetri.Spec.ENV_006_forbids_sharedTicket` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.ENV_006): ✗ The shared ticket violates ENV-006 (line 3, the third shall sentence): two requests into place `0` are accepted with ticket `0`, the second event is never queued, and the run finishes with only token `5` in place `0`. Line 4 alone does not reject it: the injection of ticket `0` answers both acceptances, so the run meets line 4 (decided below).
  <pre>¬ENV_006 env006_sharedTicket</pre>
- ✗ **forbids** `Libpetri.Spec.ENV_006_forbids_silentDrop` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.ENV_006): ✗ The silent drop violates ENV-006 (line 1, the body sentence's "rather than silently dropping the token"): after a drain, a request into place `0` is answered `accepted`.
  <pre>¬ENV_006 env006_silentDrop</pre>
- ✓ **nonvacuous** `Libpetri.Spec.ENV_006_nonvacuous` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.ENV_006): Every line of ENV-006 is exercised by the reference: a request is refused after a drain (AC2, the test derivation), after a close (AC1) and after the run finished (the test derivation); and four ideal runs accept ticket `0` and answer it, one per kind of answer: the injection that lands the token in place `0`, the discard after a close, the finish closed with the event still queued, and the immediate termination (line 4, AC3).
  <pre>(∃ s s',<br>    RefExec env006_cfg s (XLbl.request 0 5 Reply.refused) s' ∧ s.mode = Mode.draining) ∧<br>  (∃ s s',<br>      RefExec env006_cfg s (XLbl.request 0 5 Reply.refused) s' ∧ s.mode = Mode.closed) ∧<br>    (∃ s s',<br>        RefExec env006_cfg s (XLbl.request 0 5 Reply.refused) s' ∧<br>          isExecPhase s.phase = false) ∧<br>      (∃ tr,<br>          IdealRun RefExec env006_cfg env006_s0 tr ∧<br>            (occurs acceptsTicket 0) tr ∧<br>              (when acceptsTicket 0, shall Env006.answersTicket 0) tr ∧<br>                (occurs fun e ↦ Env006.answersTicket 0 e &amp;&amp; env006_kind e == 1) tr ∧<br>                  (XRun.last env006_s0 tr).M 0 = [5]) ∧<br>        (∃ tr,<br>            IdealRun RefExec env006_cfg env006_s0 tr ∧<br>              (occurs acceptsTicket 0) tr ∧<br>                (when acceptsTicket 0, shall Env006.answersTicket 0) tr ∧<br>                  (occurs fun e ↦ Env006.answersTicket 0 e &amp;&amp; env006_kind e == 2) tr) ∧<br>          (∃ tr,<br>              IdealRun RefExec env006_cfg env006_s0 tr ∧<br>                (occurs acceptsTicket 0) tr ∧<br>                  (when acceptsTicket 0, shall Env006.answersTicket 0) tr ∧<br>                    (occurs fun e ↦ Env006.answersTicket 0 e &amp;&amp; env006_kind e == 3) tr) ∧<br>            ∃ tr,<br>              IdealRun RefExec env006_cfg env006_s0 tr ∧<br>                (occurs acceptsTicket 0) tr ∧<br>                  (when acceptsTicket 0, shall Env006.answersTicket 0) tr ∧<br>                    (occurs fun e ↦ Env006.answersTicket 0 e &amp;&amp; env006_kind e == 4) tr</pre>
