<a id="Libpetri-Spec-ENV_010"></a>
## ENV-010: Implicit Long-Running Behavior

`Libpetri.Spec.ENV_010` · Kind **B** · Scope executors with environment places · Source **verbatim** (spec/06-environment-places.md) · Sign-off **pending** · Statement hash `d28528ce9303a4cb`

| Natural language | Plain reading | Lean statement |
|---|---|---|
| When environment places are registered with the executor, the executor does NOT terminate at quiescence (no transition armed, no firing in flight, and no completion, publication or external event queued, as in [EXEC-040]) while it has not been drained ([ENV-011]), closed ([ENV-013]) or stopped by an immediate termination ([ENV-015]) and no terminal place is marked ([EXEC-042]).<br><br>Instead, it waits for external events that may enable new transitions.<br><br>This behavior is derived from the presence of environment places: no explicit flag is needed.<br><br>*While* environment places are registered, the executor is open (it has not been drained, closed or stopped by an immediate termination) and no terminal place is marked ([EXEC-042]), the executor *shall not* terminate as quiescent ([EXEC-041]).<br><br>*While* environment places are registered, the executor is open and running and no terminal place is marked, *when* a caller asks to inject a token into a registered environment place, the executor *shall* answer the request and *shall* accept the injection.<br><br>*While* environment places are registered, the executor is open and no terminal place is marked, *when* the loop reaches its termination test ([EXEC-040]), the executor *shall* go on to its firing pass ([EXEC-001]).<br><br>*While* environment places are registered, the executor is open and no terminal place is marked, *when* an accepted injection is queued, the executor *shall* leave its wait ([ENV-005]) and *shall* inject the oldest queued injection in its event step ([ENV-003]).<br><br>The executor *shall not* need a long-running flag or any setting other than the registered environment places to wait at quiescence. | 1. For every executor R and every configuration C that registers at least one environment place:<br>2. (1) while no terminal place is marked and the executor's mode is open (not draining, closed or stopped), R takes no finish quiescent step;<br>3. (2) on every request step of R that asks to inject into a registered environment place while no terminal place is marked, the mode is open and the run has not finished, the reply is accepted. | <pre>fun {N T} [DecidableEq N] R ↦<br>  ∀ (C : Cfg N T),<br>    C.envs ≠ [] →<br>      (while fun s ↦ Live C s ∧ s.mode = Mode.open, never fun s s' ↦<br>          R C s (XLbl.finish Cause.quiescent) s') ∧<br>        ∀ (p : N) (x : T) (r : Reply),<br>          on fun s s' ↦<br>            R C s (XLbl.request p x r) s' ∧<br>              p ∈ C.envs ∧ Live C s ∧ s.mode = Mode.open ∧ isExecPhase s.phase = true,<br>            shall fun x x_1 ↦ r = Reply.accepted</pre> |

**Assumptions**

- The model is an executor R : XRel N T (glossary GlossaryExec.lean): R C s l s' says that under configuration C the step labelled l leads from executor state s to s'. The registered environment places are C.envs (glossary: Environment place, ENV-001); 'environment places are registered' is C.envs ≠ []. The run has not finished ('running') while its phase is not done (isExecPhase), and a run ends with a step finish c, where c is the termination cause of EXEC-041; 'terminate as quiescent' is finish quiescent. A request step request p x r is a caller asking to inject x into p and getting the reply r (accepted, refused or error). The mode is open until a drain (draining, ENV-011), a close (closed, ENV-013) or an immediate termination (stopped, ENV-015): 'open (it has not been drained, closed or stopped by an immediate termination)' is mode = open. 'No terminal place is marked' is the glossary term Live. 'The termination test' is the phase test, 'its firing pass' is the phase pass that the step begin enters, 'its wait' is the phase await (step 6), 'its event step' is the phase events (step 2), and the queued injections are the event queue eq, oldest first. The witness is the reference executor RefExec (Reference/Exec.lean), checked rule by rule against the Rust executor: the termination checks of executor_core/executor.rs (1084-1095), the exit test of the wait (1137-1143) and ExecutorHandle::inject (executor_handle.rs 67-74); and against Java and TypeScript, whose shouldTerminate (BitmapNetExecutor.java 1264-1276, bitmap-net-executor.ts 697-711) ends an executor with environment places only when draining or closed.
- Guard (ruling D73 (a)). Line 1 forbids only the quiescent finish, which is what the requirement is about. The other causes are tied to their own conditions by EXEC-041 (finish closed only once closed or stopped, finish stopped only once stopped, finish terminal only with a terminal place marked, and no step but a finish ends the run), so an executor that meets EXEC-041 and line 1 does not end at all under the guard. The reference offers no finish of any cause there. The guard is the open mode and not the registered places alone: a drained executor with environment places ends at quiescence (ENV-011), which line 1 allows (ENV_010_allows_drainedQuiescence). A marked terminal place ends the run whatever is registered (EXEC-042), which is why both lines and the coverage clause carry Live. Runtime exits that sit outside the guard: in Rust an executor whose signal channel has closed, every sender dropped, accepts no injection and ends at quiescence as a drained one does (dropping an ExecutorHandle sends a drain first), which is a drain in the model; Rust's run_sync has no signal channel and accepts no injection, so it is not an executor this requirement binds; a Java interrupt taken while the loop waits ends the run as interrupted, a cause EXEC-041 keeps out of the model (N), as are faults of the host runtime.
- Quiescence (rulings D5, D13 (a) and D20, ENVB-R7 item 1) is EXEC-040's rest: no transition armed, no firing in flight, no completion, publication or external event queued (Rest of GlossaryExec). A reaped transition that is still enabled does not count. Line 1 does not need the term: it forbids the quiescent finish in every state under the guard, at rest or not, and EXEC-040 and EXEC-041 already allow that finish only at rest.
- The first shall sentence and the first quoted body sentence are line 1, and so is AC3 (an executor with environment places does not terminate at quiescence). ENV_010_forbids_quiesceAnyway is an executor that ends at quiescence whatever is registered: started with an environment place and nothing to do, it ends at its first termination test.
- The second shall sentence is line 2 and the first part of Env010Covers: the request is answered (the clause, a step that is offered in every state under the guard) and the answer is an acceptance (line 2). Line 2 alone does not make the executor answer, since it speaks only of the request steps R takes; the clause does. ENV_010_forbids_deafWait answers an injection refused while its wait is parked, as if it had ended (it breaks line 2). env010_covers_muteWait does not answer at all while parked, so the caller can not inject (it meets both lines and fails the first part of the clause). Line 2 and the clause carry Live: once a terminal place is marked the run is about to end with finish terminal (EXEC-042), and what a request there gets is ENV-006's, where the reference accepts it and the finish answers it false, and TypeScript refuses it at the call (bitmap-net-executor.ts 611 and 652, the terminalReached test). The caller learns false either way, and ENV_010_allows_terminalRefusal shows that ENV-010 allows the TypeScript shape.
- AC1 and the sentence 'Instead, it waits for external events that may enable new transitions.' are line 1 together with the first two parts of Env010Covers: at quiescence the executor does not end (line 1), goes on from its termination test to its firing pass (the second part), whose end leads to the wait (EXEC-001, CONC-010), and accepts a caller's injection there (the first part). The third shall sentence is the second part. env010_covers_hold is an executor that holds at its termination test once its only work is queued injections: it accepts every request and never goes on to inject them (it meets both lines and fails the second part). That the end of the pass leads to the park (endPass, park) is EXEC-001's and CONC-010's.
- AC5 (injecting a token resumes execution from quiescence) and the fourth shall sentence are the first, third and fourth parts of Env010Covers: the injection is accepted while the executor idles (the first part), the wait does not stay idle with an injection queued, it wakes or injects (the fourth part), and step 2 injects the oldest queued injection (the third part). env010_covers_stuckWait is a wait that an arrival does not end, and env010_covers_noInject a step 2 that never injects; each meets both lines and fails its part of the clause. What the inject step does to the queue and the marking is ENV-003's, that an accepted request clears the park is ENV-005's (CONC-010), and that the injected token arms the transition it enables is the injected-token clause of TIME-010 and TIME-013 (the inject step writes its place, ruling D6). ENV_010_nonvacuous decides the test derivation on the reference: an executor with one environment place reaches a test at rest and does not end, parks, accepts an injection while parked, injects it, fires the transition it enables, reaches a test at rest again and does not end, is drained, and then ends quiescent with the token moved.
- AC2, the fifth shall sentence and the body sentence on the flag: the only premise on the configuration, of the statement and of Env010Covers, is C.envs ≠ [], and the configuration has no long-running field, so the waiting is derived from the registered places alone. An executor that waits only when a separate long-running flag is set (env010_flagStep) is the reference when the flag is set (env010_flagStep_true) and the quiesceAnyway executor when it is not, so with the flag at its unset default it is forbidden (ENV_010_forbids_quiesceAnyway). An executor with such a flag set by default meets the statement; that no such flag exists on the executor API is API shape (kind Q), with no Lean witness beyond the unset flag: Rust derives the waiting from the registered set (rust/libpetri-runtime/src/executor.rs 142), Java and TypeScript from the environment places given to the builder (BitmapNetExecutor.java 351, bitmap-net-executor.ts 345).
- AC4 and the sentence 'When no environment places are registered, the executor terminates at quiescence per [EXEC-040].' belong to EXEC-040, whose block is premised on C.envs = [], the complement of this block's premise. env010_finish_iff_noEnvs is the bridge on the reference: at a termination test at rest, with no terminal place marked and the mode open, a finish quiescent step is offered exactly when no environment place is registered. ENV_010_allows_noEnvQuiescence shows the same net without environment places ending at its first test.
- Its offers are in ExecCoversW5.Env010Covers (ConsistencyExec.lean; the convention of GlossaryExec.lean: offers are coverage clauses, never block lines), as ENV-002's are in Env002Covers. The second, third and fourth EARS sentences demand an answer and are quoted whole; the safety half of the second is line 2, and their existence halves are that clause: in every state where environment places are registered, no terminal place is marked and the mode is open, R offers the accepted request, the begin step at the test, the inject step in step 2 and the way out of the wait. The clause reads every such state, reachable or not, and the reference meets it (env010_ref_covers). Requests into a place that is not an environment place are ENV-002's (Java and TypeScript answer error, Rust and Python deposit, ruling D89 (a)); line 2 and the first part of Env010Covers speak only of registered environment places, where all four runtimes accept. Requests while draining, closed, stopped or after the finish are refused (ENV-006, ENV-011, ENV-013). Injections before the run starts are outside the model, whose runs start at xinit in mode open.

## ENV-011: Graceful Drain

`Libpetri.Spec.ENV_011` · Kind **B** · Scope executors with a drain operation · Source **verbatim** (spec/06-environment-places.md) · Sign-off **pending** · Statement hash `e57a00136af2c828`

| Natural language | Plain reading | Lean statement |

| The executor provides a `drain()` method that signals graceful shutdown.<br><br>After `drain()` is called:<br><br>New `inject()` calls are rejected (return error/false).<br><br>Already-queued external events are processed normally.<br><br>In-flight actions are allowed to complete.<br><br>The executor terminates when quiescent (no armed transitions, no in-flight, no pending events).<br><br>Items 2 to 4 hold while no terminal place is marked: a marked terminal place stops the executor at once, abandoning the actions in flight and ending the run with the queued external events unapplied ([EXEC-042]).<br><br>For executors without environment places, a drain does not change when the executor terminates, since the executor already terminates at quiescence.<br><br>*When* an open executor is drained, it *shall* enter the draining mode and *shall* leave the rest of its state as it was, apart from waking its wait ([CONC-010]): its marking, its queued external events and its firings in flight stay as they were.<br><br>*If* an executor that is not open (draining, closed or stopped) is drained, *then* the drain *shall* change nothing.<br><br>*While* the executor is draining, *when* an injection is requested, the executor *shall* reject it (error or false) and *shall* change nothing.<br><br>*While* the executor is draining, it *shall not* discard a queued external event.<br><br>*While* the executor is draining, it *shall* take every step of its cycle as it takes it while open, with the same effect: it *shall* inject the queued external events, let the actions in flight complete, settle their outcomes and start ready transitions as an open executor does; **Assumptions**

- The model is an executor R : XRel N T (glossary GlossaryExec.lean): R C s l s' says that under configuration C the step labelled l leads from executor state s to s'. The executor state carries a lifecycle mode (open, draining, closed, stopped); drain is the outside step of a caller calling drain(), request p x r a caller's inject() of x into p answered r (accepted, refused or error), discard k the executor dropping queued event k unapplied, park and wake the start and the end of the wait of step 6, and finish c a termination with cause c (EXEC-041). The witness is the reference executor RefExec (Reference/Exec.lean), checked rule by rule against the Rust executor: ExecutorHandle::drain and inject (executor_handle.rs 67-113), the Drain arm of handle_signal, the draining termination check and the draining exit before the wait (executor_core/executor.rs 1087-1089, 1138-1143, 1424-1426); Java BitmapNetExecutor.drain, shouldTerminate and awaitWork, TypeScript drain, its termination check and its latched wake run the same rules.
- Scope (ruling D20, clash env-b#4, ENVB-R7 item 7): items 2 to 4 hold while no terminal place is marked; a marked terminal place stops the executor at once and abandons the actions in flight, and the run ends with the queued events unapplied (EXEC-042), in every runtime whatever the mode. That end is the finish terminal, not a discard step, so it does not touch line 3. Lines 5 and 6 carry the premise (Live). Lines 1 to 4 and 7 need none: the reference's rules are mode-blind there too, and EXEC-042's own lines govern the terminal stop.
- 'After drain() is called' is the mode draining: the drain step sets it, and only a close (ENV-013) or an immediate termination (ENV-015) leaves it, both lifecycle steps with their own requirements; the quoted sentence on a close or an immediate termination of a draining executor says so, and line 4 leaves the lifecycle calls out of its comparison for that reason. A drained executor that later closes is governed by ENV-013 from that step on. After the run ends the mode stays draining, so line 2 also answers a request to a drained executor that has finished; ENV-006 states the replies in every mode.
- The first and second shall sentences are line 1. A drain wakes the wait (CONC-010, ruling D13 (a): a drain is a wake reason), which is the parked flag of the state; nothing else changes. An executor whose drain also drops the queued events breaks line 1 (ENV_011_forbids_drainDrops), and so does one whose drain leaves a parked wait asleep (ENV_011_forbids_drainKeepsParked). A drain of an executor that is not open, whether draining, closed or stopped (ENV-015), changes nothing: Rust's drain() returns false and sends no signal once the handle is drained, Java and TypeScript set a flag that is already set (a closed executor stays closed, closed is tested first, and a stopped one stays stopped). The reference has no drain step there, which line 1's second half allows; an executor whose drain reopens a closed executor into draining breaks it (ENV_011_forbids_reopenClosed).
- The third shall sentence and item 1 (AC2) are line 2: while draining, an inject() is not accepted (it is refused, or error for a place that is not an environment place) and changes nothing. An executor that accepts it breaks the first half (ENV_011_forbids_acceptWhileDraining), one that answers refused and queues the event anyway breaks the second (ENV_011_forbids_queueRefused). In Rust the draining flag is a field of the handle (executor_handle.rs 44, 68), and an event sent through a second sender after the Drain signal is answered true and discarded (executor_core/executor.rs, the Event arm with draining set); the model has one injector per executor, an assumption for Rust and Python (ruling D44 (a), ENVB-R3). Events accepted before the drain were queued before the Drain signal in the one channel, so they are 'already queued'.
- The fourth shall sentence and item 2 (AC3) are lines 3, 4 and 5. Line 3: a draining executor never discards a queued event (ENV_011_forbids_discardWhileDraining). Line 4 for the inject label: a queued event is injected while draining exactly as while open (ENV_011_forbids_stallEvents, an executor that stops injecting once drained). Line 5: a draining executor terminates only with the event queue empty, so no queued event is lost to the finish. 'Processed before termination' as liveness is an ideal run (IdealRun, kind A: every action returns) together with coverage; ENV_011_nonvacuous decides one.
- The fifth shall sentence is line 4, and with it item 3 (AC4) and the no-op sentence. Line 4 compares a draining state with the same state in mode open, label by label: the steps an action takes (write, flush, return, expiry of its budget), the settle steps (commit, fail, tdeposit), the publication steps, injection, the update, the deadline step, the firing pass and, away from rest, the wait. 'Allowed to complete' is that the actions' own steps and the settle steps are those of an open executor; line 5 adds that a draining executor does not terminate before they are settled. The answers that do differ are named in the sentence: a request is refused (line 2), a snapshot request is rejected (ENV-014 AC4, which every runtime applies after a drain, with or without environment places), and at rest an executor with environment places ends its wait and terminates where an open one waits for an arrival (ENV-010, lines 5 to 7).
- Line 4 restates an open-mode requirement where the two modes agree: without environment places begin, finish, park and wake are compared at rest too, so with line 6 an open executor without environment places takes no executor step at a termination test at rest but a finish. That is EXEC-040's own line, which the no-op sentence presupposes.
- The no-op sentence (ruling D20, clash env-b#6, ENVB-R7 item 2) is line 4 without environment places: then begin, finish, park and wake are compared at rest too, so a drained executor without environment places terminates exactly where it would have terminated had it not been drained. The literal reading 'drain() is a no-op', a drain step that changes nothing, is the mutant ENV_011_mutant_noop: it is told apart from the requirement by an executor that ignores the drain of an executor without environment places, which meets the literal reading and breaks line 1. The rewording is what every runtime does: after a drain, snapshot() is rejected whatever the net (ENV-014 AC4), so the state does change.
- The sixth shall sentence is line 5 and item 4 read with 'armed' for 'enabled' (ruling D5, ENVB-R7 item 1): quiescent is the glossary term Rest of GlossaryExec (restB), nothing armed, nothing in flight, nothing queued (ruling D13 (a)), and the finish is taken at the termination test of a cycle (EXEC-001), not elsewhere in the cycle. A firing counts as in flight until it is settled and its publications are deposited (EXEC-040). An executor that terminates while an action is in flight breaks line 5 (ENV_011_forbids_finishInFlight), and so does one that terminates from its wait (ENV_011_forbids_finishInWait). Rust leaves its loop from step 6 when it is draining and quiescent (executor_core/executor.rs 1138-1143); the model reads that exit as the wake and the next cycle's termination test, which change nothing at rest. The cause of a draining finish is not fixed here: ENV-011 alone admits a draining executor that finishes with cause closed at quiescence, and EXEC-041 excludes it (a finish closed needs a closing mode, a finish stopped a stopped one, a finish terminal a marked terminal place), leaving quiescent.
- The seventh shall sentence and AC5 are line 6: at a termination test with no terminal place marked and at rest, a draining executor takes no executor step but a finish (in particular no firing pass, begin). An executor that treats a draining executor with environment places as an open one there, beginning a pass where it should terminate, breaks it (ENV_011_forbids_neverEnds). Java's draining termination check reads no external event queue: it is empty there because step 2 of the same cycle emptied it and a draining executor accepts no new event.
- The eighth shall sentence is line 7: a draining executor at rest that enters its wait changes only the parked flag, and one that ends it changes only that flag and the phase, which returns to step 1 of the cycle; an executor whose drained wait at rest skips to the termination test, past the enablement update, breaks it (ENV_011_forbids_wakeSkipsCycle). The reference may park a draining executor at rest (parkStep does not read the mode), where no runtime waits: Rust leaves the loop before its wait, Java's awaitWork does not wait when draining (BitmapNetExecutor.java 2012, hasEnvironmentPlaces && !draining), TypeScript returns on the latched wake. That is harmless because the reference's wake is offered in every live wait, so line 7 constrains the effect of such a park and does not forbid it.
- Existence is coverage, not a line, and belongs to the consistency theorem: Env011Covers below is the conjunct ENV-011 asks of it, a clause of ExecCoversW5 (ConsistencyExec.lean), with three clauses. AC1 (drain() is available): a drain step is offered from every open state. The seventh shall sentence and AC5 ('shall terminate'): finish quiescent is offered at every termination test of a draining executor with no terminal place marked and at rest. The ninth shall sentence (the wait ends at once): a wake is offered in every wait of a draining executor with no terminal place marked and at rest. The reference meets all three (env011_ref_covers, from env011_drain_offered, env011_finish_offered and env011_wake_offered). AC1, AC5's 'shall terminate' and the ninth shall sentence are therefore enforced by the consistency theorem and not by this block's lines: an executor with an edge-triggered wait, whose parked loop wakes only after an arrival cleared its flag or on a timer (the hazard TypeScript's latched wake guards against, bitmap-net-executor.ts 225-242), meets every line (env011_lostWake_meets) while a drain raised before it parks leaves it asleep for good; it fails Env011Covers (env011_lostWake_not_covered, on the run: the open executor with an environment place reaches its wait at rest, is drained, then parks).
- The test derivation (inject, drain, the queued event processed, a new inject rejected, termination at quiescence) is ENV_011_nonvacuous's run.
- The model reads one executor per configuration with its own queue; Rust's run_sync and the exits of a dropped handle (the handle's Drop sends a Drain) are ENV-010's notes (ruling D73 (a)).

## ENV-013: Immediate Close

**Assumptions**

- The model is an executor R : XRel N T (glossary GlossaryExec.lean): R C s l s' says that under configuration C the step labelled l leads from executor state s to s'. The close is the outside step close; the closed mode is Mode.closed. The witness is the reference executor RefExec (Reference/Exec.lean), whose close rule (closeStep) takes a close from the open or the draining mode.
- Naming: the markdown's 'the executor takes a close' is the close step. In Java and TypeScript that is the call of close(), which sets the closed flag the loop and inject() read. In Rust it is the executor reading the Close signal in Phase 2 (executor_core/executor.rs handle_signal, Close arm); the handle refuses injections from the call of close() (executor_handle.rs close sets drained), and every event sent before the call travels the channel ahead of the Close. A Rust run is therefore the model run in which the injections of those events come before the close step and the requests refused by the handle come after it: a refused request changes nothing (line 2), so placing it after the close step changes no state. One injector per run is assumed (Rust's events from a second sender, sent after the Close, are answered true and dropped by the Close arm), as in the reference's own notes on D44 (a).
- Item 1 and AC4 ('inject() returns error/false after close') are line 2: a request to a closed executor is refused (an environment place) or an error (not one, Java and TypeScript), never accepted, and queues nothing (ENV_013_forbids_closedAccepts). Which of refused and error, and the false or error value inject() hands the caller, are ENV-002's and ENV-006's subject.
- Item 2, AC2 and ruling D44 (a): line 5 is the common line, 'a closed executor injects no queued event' (ENV_013_forbids_closedInjects), and line 6 says no event is left queued when a closed run ends (ENV_013_forbids_finishKeepsQueue). An event still queued after the close leaves the queue by a discard step or by the finish. Java completes it with false at loop exit (drainPendingExternalEvents); the reference also offers the discard in step 2 and in the wait, so the markdown's informative sentence on when Java and TypeScript answer such an inject() names no instant and is not a line. That the answer is false exactly at the discard or the finish is ENV-004's line. Which accepted events are still queued at the close is implementation shape, kind N: Java and TypeScript discard every event still queued when the flag is set; Rust and Python inject every event sent before the close (the run of the naming assumption) and answer inject() at enqueue time.
- Item 3, AC3 and the shutdown being a close, not a stop: line 1 keeps the firings in flight, their queued outcomes and their queued publications at the close (ENV_013_forbids_closeAbandons), line 9 says a firing leaves the firings in flight while closed only by being settled (ENV_013_forbids_closedDropsInFlight: a closed executor that abandons its firings at step 1 and then finishes closed with nothing in flight), line 10 says a closed executor ends step 1b only with no publication queued, so a batch an action flushed is still published after the close, as ruling D17 has it for every published token (ENV_013_forbids_closedSkipsPublications: a closed executor that stops publishing and finishes with the batch lost), and line 7 says the run ends, with no terminal place marked, only when none is in flight (ENV_013_forbids_finishInFlight). Together they are 'in-flight actions complete before termination'. Line 9 does not say where a settle happens (step 1, the wait or the pass); that is EXEC-001's. That the actions do return, and that a returned outcome is settled, is coverage, not a line here: ExecCovers (every firing in flight can return) and ValidatedBy (every completion the loop may settle is settled) in the consistency theorem (ConsistencyExec.lean), neither of which depends on the mode; settlement in the closed mode is the reference's commit, as spec/04-execution-model.md says of a close (it waits for the actions in flight and takes their completions up in step 1), exercised by ENV_013_nonvacuous. An executor that takes no step at all after the close passes every line here; it fails that coverage. The seventh shall sentence's 'or on a cancellation it observes in its wait ([EXEC-041])' is out of the model, which has no interrupt (EXEC-041's assumes): line 7 states the sentence without it, and Java's interrupt path (awaitCompletionPolling ending the loop interrupted while closed with actions in flight, BitmapNetExecutor.java 2062-2070) is that cancellation, allowed by EXEC-041 and not a run of the model.
- Item 4 and ruling D85 (a): line 7 is 'terminates after in-flight actions complete'; line 8 is 'it terminates at the first termination test that finds no action in flight': at such a test, with no terminal place marked, a closed executor takes no executor step but a finish (EXEC-040's line 3 read with nothing in flight in place of Rest), in particular it begins no firing pass (ENV_013_forbids_closeWaitsForQuiescence: a close that behaves as a drain, starting a ready transition with nothing in flight). That a finish is in fact offered at such a test is coverage: Env013Covers, a clause of the consistency theorem's ExecCoversW5 (ConsistencyExec.lean), asks for finish closed at every such test, and the reference offers it (env013_finish_offered). Line 8 alone is safety: an executor that offers no step at such a test (one whose finish closed also waits for the event queue to empty, which no closed step ever empties) passes this block and fails Env013Covers. Line 8 bans loop steps only: answering a snapshot request, which is not a step of the loop (EXEC-041, EXEC-042), is allowed at the test provided it changes nothing (the exemption EXEC-042's line 1 makes). The permission 'may start ready transitions' while an action is in flight is the reference starting a firing after the close (ENV_013_nonvacuous); a close therefore does not bound the run (the quoted 'A close alone therefore does not bound ...' sentence), and the bound is ENV-015's immediate termination; a run budget (ENV-016) bounds only the caller's wait, since its expiry ends the wait and not the loop (EXEC-041; under the close policy it is a close, ENV-016's line 2).
- 'A close does not stop the firing pass.' is line 1 at the close step: the phase, the pass's remaining order, its hidden tail and its started flag stay (ENV_013_forbids_closeStopsPass: a close taken mid-pass that empties the order, so the ready transitions left in it never start). The steps after the close are EXEC-003's: its endPass line, which reads no mode, ends a pass only with the order exhausted, so an executor that ends a closed pass early breaks EXEC-003, not this block. Line 1 also keeps the clock readings now and cyc, at which steps 4 and 5 judge readiness, and the identity supply.
- Scope (ENVB-R7 item 7, D20): the markdown's 'unless a terminal place is marked ([EXEC-042])' is the premise Live C s of lines 7 and 8. A terminal stop ends the run whatever is in flight, the firings abandoned (EXEC-042's finish terminal, which keeps them in the state); lines 6 and 9 hold across it (the finish clears the event queue, and an abandoned firing is not removed). The cause the finish reports is EXEC-041's: at a rest reached after a close the reference offers both quiescent and closed (ruling D53 (c), ENV_013_nonvacuous).
- The mode lines 3 and 4 pin what EXEC-041's lines 6 and 7 read as 'a close was requested': the mode becomes closed only by a close (ENV_013_forbids_drainCloses) and stays closed until the run ends unless an immediate termination ([ENV-015], Java, Mode.stopped) replaces it (ENV_013_forbids_drainReopens). The escalation sentence 'Calling `close()` after `drain()` escalates from graceful to immediate shutdown.' is the reference's close from the draining mode (ENV_013_nonvacuous), after which every closed line applies. That the close is offered at all, from the open mode ('provides a `close()` method') and from the draining mode (the escalation), is coverage, not a line: inside the consistency theorem ENV-016's coverage clause Env016Covers and its line 2 carry it (an expiry under the close policy is offered in every executing phase and is a close step from the open and the draining mode), and the reference offers the close from both modes in every phase (env013_close_offered). A second close of a closed executor is no step of the reference (Rust and Java return without effect); line 1 does not need it.
- AC1 ('close() signals immediate shutdown') is line 1: the close step enters the closed mode, which every other line reads. Waking the wait on a close is CONC-010's (the reference's close clears parked), which is why line 1 leaves the parked flag free.
- The test derivation (an executor with an action in flight is closed; the action completes; queued events are discarded; the executor terminates) is ENV_013_nonvacuous's run: an event queued before the close is discarded, a request after it is refused, the firing in flight is committed after the close, and the run finishes closed with nothing in flight. A second run of ENV_013_nonvacuous publishes, after the close, a batch the action flushed before it.

<a id="Libpetri-Spec-ENV_014"></a>
## ENV-014: Mid-Execution Marking Snapshot

`Libpetri.Spec.ENV_014` · Kind **B** · Scope all executors · Source **verbatim** (spec/06-environment-places.md) · Sign-off **pending** · Statement hash `1e2865e7f5502dd3`

| Natural language | Plain reading | Lean statement |
|---|---|---|
| The executor exposes a `snapshot()` operation that returns a point-in-time copy of the current marking **without affecting lifecycle** — unlike `drain()` ([ENV-011]) and `close()` ([ENV-013]), it neither stops nor pauses execution.<br><br>**Work in flight** means either of two things: an **action** that has started and not completed, or an **external event the executor has accepted but not yet injected** ([ENV-003], [ENV-004]).<br><br>Consequently a snapshot offered as a restore point for [CORE-073] MUST be taken at a moment when no work is in flight — no action, and no accepted external event still awaiting injection.<br><br>A firing therefore counts as in flight **from the moment its inputs are consumed** — not from the moment its action first suspends — so the window covers the action's synchronous prefix and any event-store callback the firing triggers, and the indication MUST report work in flight throughout it.<br><br>**The answer and its two readings.** An answer to `snapshot()` is either a rejection or a marking, and a marking either reports a restore point (no work in flight) or reports work in flight.<br><br>A refusal of a restore-point snapshot while work is in flight reports work in flight; the rejection is reserved, while the run lasts, for an executor that has been drained, closed or terminated.<br><br>An answer that reports a restore point describes the instant at which the executor captured it.<br><br>An answer to a request the orchestrator could not serve reports work in flight and may describe an earlier instant of the same run, while a parked executor still answers with the current marking (AC9).<br><br>*When* the executor answers a `snapshot()` request, it *shall* leave its whole state as it was, among it the marking, the lifecycle, the firings in flight, the queued completions, publications and external events, the clocks of the transitions, and the orchestrator's place in its cycle, a wait it is parked in included ([CORE-071]).<br><br>*If* the executor has been drained or closed ([ENV-011], [ENV-013]), or terminated immediately ([ENV-015]), *then* it *shall* reject a `snapshot()` request.<br><br>*While* the executor is running and has been neither drained, closed nor terminated, it *shall not* reject a `snapshot()` request.<br><br>*If* a firing is in flight at the instant the executor captures the marking for a `snapshot()` answer, counted from the moment its inputs are consumed until the executor has processed its completion and deposited every token its action published ([IO-015]), *then* the executor *shall not* report that answer as a restore point.<br><br>*If* an external event that the executor accepted before a `snapshot()` request is still queued for injection at the instant the executor captures the marking for that request's answer, *then* the executor *shall not* report that answer as a restore point. | 1. For every executor R and every configuration C:<br>2. for every answer a, a snapshot step answered a ends in the state it starts from;<br>3. for every answer a, a snapshot step answered a from a state whose mode is not open (draining, closed or stopped) answers none;<br>4. for every answer a, a snapshot step answered a from a state whose mode is open and whose loop is running (an executing phase) does not answer none;<br>5. a snapshot step answered some false starts in a state with no firing in flight;<br>6. a snapshot step answered some false starts in a state whose event queue is empty;<br>7. on every run of R that starts in a state with no firing in flight and no published batch queued, a snapshot step answered some false starts in a state whose publication queue is empty. | <pre>fun {N T} [DecidableEq N] R ↦<br>  ∀ (C : Cfg N T),<br>    (∀ (a : Option Bool),<br>        on fun s s' ↦ R C s (XLbl.snapshot a) s', shall fun s s' ↦ s' = s) ∧<br>      (∀ (a : Option Bool),<br>          on fun s s' ↦ R C s (XLbl.snapshot a) s', shall fun s x ↦<br>            s.mode ≠ Mode.open → a = none) ∧<br>        (∀ (a : Option Bool),<br>            on fun s s' ↦ R C s (XLbl.snapshot a) s', shall fun s x ↦<br>              s.mode = Mode.open → isExecPhase s.phase = true → a ≠ none) ∧<br>          (on fun s s' ↦ R C s (XLbl.snapshot (some false)) s', shall fun s x ↦<br>              s.fl = []) ∧<br>            (on fun s s' ↦ R C s (XLbl.snapshot (some false)) s', shall fun s x ↦<br>                s.eq = []) ∧<br>              ∀ (s0 : XSt N T) (tr : List (XStep N T)),<br>                s0.fl = [] →<br>                  s0.pq = [] →<br>                    XRun R C s0 tr →<br>                      ∀ x ∈ tr, x.2.1 = XLbl.snapshot (some false) → x.1.pq = []</pre> |

**Assumptions**

- The model is an executor R : XRel N T (glossary GlossaryExec.lean): R C s l s' says that under configuration C the step labelled l leads from executor state s to s'. A snapshot request and its answer are one step labelled snapshot a, taken at the instant the executor captures the marking. The answer a is none for a rejection, some true for a marking that reports work in flight, some false for a marking that reports a restore point. The witness is the reference executor RefExec (Reference/Exec.lean): it answers snapAnswer s (some of whether a firing is in flight or an event is queued while the mode is open, none otherwise), in step 2 after the injections, at entry to the enablement update and in the wait, which is Rust's handle_signal Snapshot arm (executor_core/executor.rs 1433-1446) and Java's serviceMarkingRequest after the external-events phase.
- Which marking an answer returns is a modelling assumption (kind A), not a line. The label carries no marking: the model reads the marking of an answer as the marking s.M of the state the step starts from, which line 1 makes the marking of the state it ends in too, and an executor that answers with any other marking cannot be written in the model, so no mutant can break what follows. Four quoted duties rest on that reading alone: 'An answer that reports a restore point describes the instant at which the executor captured it'; the second half of 'An answer to a request the orchestrator could not serve ...', a parked executor answers with the current marking, which is AC9's 'MUST return the current marking, not an earlier published one'; the first half of that sentence, that an answer describing an earlier instant (Java's unserved request, ruling D43 (a)) reports work in flight; and the marking side of the body's 'MUST be decided at the same instant the marking is captured'. The lines pin the flag side of that last duty: the flag is read off the state of the step, so an indication computed at another instant shows as an answer some false from a state with work in flight, which lines 4 to 6 forbid. The first two duties become lines of their own once the label carries the marking (an answer some (m, b) with m = s.M when b is false, and when the loop is parked); the glossary has no such label yet.
- The three conforming shapes of the body (refuse, indicate, defer) are one abstraction. An indication is the flag of the answer. A refusal of a restore-point snapshot while work is in flight is an answer some true: the caller can tell it from a restore point, and the rejection none is reserved for a drained, closed or stopped executor (the quoted paragraph 'The answer and its two readings'). A deferral is an answer step taken later, at a state with nothing in flight. An executor that never answers some false meets the block: it never offers a restore point. The reference answers some false exactly when nothing is in flight and nothing is queued, and ENV_014_nonvacuous decides such an answer.
- Work in flight (the quoted definition) is read off the state. A firing is in flight while it is in XSt.fl, from the start step that consumes its inputs to the settle step that commits or fails its completion (EXEC-001, EXEC-031), so a firing whose action returned but whose completion is not yet processed still counts (Rust decrements in_flight_count only when it processes the completion, executor_core/executor.rs 1046 and 1169). Tokens its action published mid-action (IO-015) wait in XSt.pq as flushed batches until step 1b deposits them, which can come after the settle step (EXEC-001 step 1b, executor_core/executor.rs 1043-1058). An accepted external event is queued while it is in XSt.eq, from the request step answered accepted (ENV-003) to its inject or discard step (ENV-004). The fourth quoted shall sentence keeps a firing in flight until its completion is processed and every token its action published is deposited: line 4 is the part up to the settle step, line 6 the part after it.
- Line 1 is the first quoted shall sentence and the first quoted body sentence ('without affecting lifecycle', 'neither stops nor pauses execution'): the answer changes no field of the state, which is the sentence's 'its whole state': the marking, the clock reading of the host and of the cycle, the clocks of the transitions, the mode, the firings in flight, the completion, publication and event queues, the identity supply, the phase, the pass order and its same-pass counts, and the parked flag. It owns CORE-071's 'MUST NOT mutate the live marking' for a snapshot (plan section 7). An executor whose answer drains it, as a snapshot taken through drain() would, breaks it (ENV_014_forbids_drainingSnapshot), and so does one that serves a request in the wait by waking the orchestrator (ENV_014_forbids_wakingSnapshot, AC9).
- Line 2 is the second quoted shall sentence and AC4: once the mode is draining (ENV-011), closed (ENV-013) or stopped (ENV-015, the immediate termination; Java's terminateNow sets closed, so snapshot() throws), the answer is none. ENV_014_nonvacuous parts 5 to 7 decide a rejection after a drain, after a close (the test derivation's 'call after close() and verify rejection') and after an immediate termination. An executor that answers a drained request with a marking breaks it (ENV_014_forbids_answersAfterDrain); Rust's executor arm has no draining test (executor_core/executor.rs 1433-1446), and Rust meets the line at its handle, which refuses once drained (executor_handle.rs 200-203): with one sender per run, a request sent before the drain is a snapshot step before the drain step, in channel order (map note, with ENV-011).
- Line 3 is the third quoted shall sentence and AC1 (reworded under ruling D20, ENVB-R7 item 3, to 'while the executor is running and has been neither drained, closed nor terminated'): a running open executor answers with a marking, whatever is in flight. An executor that rejects while work is in flight, a refusal the caller cannot tell from a closed executor, breaks it (ENV_014_forbids_rejectsWhileBusy). Line 3 binds only a running loop, and so does the quoted 'reserved, while the run lasts': after a run ended on its own the runtimes differ (Java and TypeScript still answer, BitmapNetExecutor.java 2380-2381, bitmap-net-executor.ts 1599-1608; the Rust handle answers Err once the channel is gone, executor_handle.rs 204-207), and the block leaves that open.
- That a snapshot step is offered at all is coverage, and no line says it. An executor with no snapshot step meets every line: line 2's 'shall reject' and line 3's 'shall not reject' are both met by never answering, and so are AC2's 'serviced within one orchestrator cycle' and AC8's 'does not park the orchestrator against itself', which rest on the same coverage. The consistency theorem excludes it: its coverage conjunct ExecCoversW5 (ConsistencyExec.lean) has the clause Env014Covers, that a live state in step 2, at entry to the update or in the wait has a snapshot step; env014_snapshot_offered proves it of the reference.
- Line 4 is the fourth quoted shall sentence up to the settle step, the action half of 'Consequently a snapshot offered as a restore point ... MUST be taken at a moment when no work is in flight', AC5 and AC6. The start step that consumes a firing's inputs is the step that puts it in flight, synchronous or not, so 'from the moment its inputs are consumed' (the quoted sentence and the first half of AC8) needs no line of its own: an executor that counts a firing as in flight only once its action suspends answers some false from inside a synchronous action and breaks line 4 (ENV_014_forbids_suspendOnlyInFlight; Java's inline capture on the orchestrator thread answers true, BitmapNetExecutor.java 2427-2431). So does an executor that always reports a restore point (ENV_014_forbids_alwaysRestorePoint). AC6 is ENV_014_nonvacuous part 1: the net's only marked place feeds a transition whose action is in flight, the consumed token is in no place of the marking, and the answer is some true.
- Line 5 is the fifth quoted shall sentence, the event half, the paragraph 'Two conforming shapes for the pending-event half' and AC7: an answer some false comes from a state whose event queue is empty. An executor whose indication reads the actions alone breaks it (ENV_014_forbids_actionsOnlyFlag): an event accepted while the loop waits is in neither the marking nor the flag. TypeScript and Java read the marking outside the event queue and OR the pending queue into the flag (the reference's reading). Rust and Python serve the request on the same FIFO channel as injections (executor_core/executor.rs 1433-1446): every event accepted before the request is injected before the answer, so the event queue holds no such event when the marking is captured; an event accepted after the request was sent is a request step after the snapshot step, in channel order, which is what the quoted sentence's 'accepted before a snapshot() request' allows. ENV_014_nonvacuous part 4 is AC7's test derivation: an event accepted while the loop is parked, the snapshot flagged.
- Line 6 is the fourth quoted shall sentence after the settle step, with reason (1) ('those tokens are simply absent'), AC8's 'outputs deposited, no token missing' and the pending-event paragraph's 'a token the executor has accepted is never absent from a snapshot that reports itself a restore point': an answer some false comes from a state with no flushed batch waiting for step 1b. An executor that serves the request before step 1b (Rust's loop with Phase 2 moved before Phase 1b, its flag still in_flight_count or a queued event) answers some false after the settle and before the deposit, with the published token in no place, and breaks line 6 alone (ENV_014_forbids_answerBeforeDeposit). Line 6 reads runs that start with no firing in flight and no batch queued: the initial state xinit, or a restored marking. From an arbitrary state the reference itself answers some false with a batch queued (env014_needs_runStart), because its flag reads the firings and the events only; on its own runs a batch is queued only while its firing is in flight or in steps 1 and 1b, where it does not answer (env014_pubInv_step). ENV_014_nonvacuous part 8 decides a reference run whose action flushes a batch in the wait, answers some true with the batch queued and some false only once step 1b has deposited it.
- AC8: a snapshot requested by a running action is a snapshot with that firing in flight (line 4), from its synchronous prefix on. The deferred arm is an answer step taken after that firing settled and its published tokens were deposited (Rust and Python serve the request of an inline synchronous action at the next cycle), which may be some false when nothing else is in flight; the block allows it. That the orchestrator does not park against itself, that the deferred reply is not blocked on from the orchestrator's own thread of control, and the body's 'An implementation with that shape MUST detect the case and capture directly on the calling thread, after whatever synchronisation of internal token storage any other marking read performs' (the inline-action form of the same duty) are thread properties (kind Q): the model has no threads, and a step relation cannot wait for itself.
- AC9: a parked executor answers without waking: line 1 keeps the parked flag and the phase of an answer in the wait (ENV_014_nonvacuous part 3 answers from a parked state and stays parked, and ENV_014_forbids_wakingSnapshot breaks it), and that the answer carries the current marking is the modelling assumption of the second paragraph. 'Without the orchestrator's participation' (Java's park epoch, Rust's race of the clock's wait against its signal channel) is a thread property (kind Q). AC9's marking() half is not a step of the model: a foreign marking() read is a read of s.M, current by construction, and its thread half is kind Q under ruling D43 (a), which CONC-001's block records for foreign reads. The last published marking of Java's unserved request after its 2 s best-effort cap (ruling D43 (a), ENVB-R4 (a)) is an answer whose marking is earlier than the state's, outside the model by the second paragraph; its flag is forced true, which is the duty the second paragraph accounts for.
- Kind Q, outside the lines: AC2's 'within one orchestrator cycle' is a latency, which rests on coverage (the reference offers an answer at entry to every enablement update, env014_snapshot_offered, so a request is answered in the cycle it arrives in or in the wait); AC2's 'keeps running afterwards' is line 1 (the answer changes neither the mode nor the phase). AC3 (an owned copy, independent of subsequent executor state) is a property of the returned value: in the model the marking of an answer is a value, so later steps cannot change it; aliasing is tested, not proven. Java's 2 s cap and 50 ms recheck are implementation choices (kind N).
- CORE-073: a restore-point answer restores, through the snapshot form, to the marking of the state it was taken from, with nothing in flight and nothing queued (env014_restorePoint_restores). The test derivation's second half (snapshot again at quiescence and restore to an equivalent marking) is that theorem together with ENV_014_nonvacuous part 2. The guarantee 'restore and resume' needs CORE-073's own block for the seeding (refSeed).

## ENV-015: Immediate Termination

`Libpetri.Spec.ENV_015` · Kind **B** · Scope all executors; the operation itself is optional (MAY) and only Java provides it · Source **verbatim** (spec/06-environment-places.md) · Sign-off **pending** · Statement hash `fc7ce336802a1f41`

| Natural language | Plain reading | Lean statement |
|---|---|---|
| An implementation MAY provide an immediate-termination operation (`terminateNow()`) that stops the orchestrator loop **without** waiting for in-flight actions, unlike `close()` ([ENV-013]) which lets them complete.<br><br>New `inject()` calls are rejected (return error / false), as after [ENV-013].<br><br>Queued external events are discarded (completed with false).<br><br>The loop stops at the end of its current cycle; it does NOT wait for in-flight actions, and their results are discarded rather than admitted to the marking.<br><br>In-flight actions keep running where the runtime cannot cancel them ([IO-013]); their consumed tokens are lost ([EXEC-031]).<br><br>It is an explicit escape hatch and MUST NOT be invoked implicitly by `close()`.<br><br>The executor is **stopped** from the moment `terminateNow()` takes effect.<br><br>The call takes effect between two steps of the loop ([EXEC-001]): a call that lands while a step is under way takes effect when that step ends.<br><br>The current cycle is the one under way when the call takes effect; **Assumptions**

- The model is an executor R : XRel N T (glossary GlossaryExec.lean): R C s l s' says that under configuration C the step labelled l leads from executor state s to s'. A call of terminateNow() is the outside step terminateNow, and 'the executor is stopped' is the lifecycle mode Mode.stopped (ruling D47 (c)). The witness is the reference executor RefExec (Reference/Exec.lean): terminateStep sets the mode stopped, keeps the phase, empties the event queue (Java completes the queued events with false inside terminateNow) and clears the parked flag, which ends the wait; settleOk refuses step 1 and the wait once stopped and lets the pass settle only a synchronous firing, publishStep refuses a stopped wait, endPass needs an empty order, endCompletions refuses a stopped state, and finish stopped is offered at phase completions.
- Naming: 'takes effect' is the terminateNow step, which sits between two steps of the loop. Java sets its flags at the call and reads stopRequested at the top of its loop (BitmapNetExecutor.executeLoop), so a call that lands during step 1 lets Java finish that step and the rest of the cycle; the model reads such a call as taking effect at the end of the step under way. A request that lands between the call and that point is, in the model, accepted and then dropped by the terminateNow step, which the quoted sentence 'A request that lands before the call takes effect may still be accepted; ...' allows: Java refuses it at once, and the caller learns false either way (ENV-004 reads the terminateNow step as the false answer of every ticket it drops). 'The start of a cycle' is the phase completions (EXEC-001 step 1, entered by endPass after a pass that started a transition, by wake, or by a settle in the wait); the current cycle ends where the next would start. 'The firing pass of the current cycle' is the phase pass: once stopped, line 7 lets no later cycle get past its start, so the only pass a stopped executor is in is the current cycle's. 'A synchronous action that pass waits for' is a firing in flight whose sync flag is set (the pass waits for it, passFree). 'Move its loop to another step' is a change of phase; 'end a wait under way' is clearing the parked flag. 'Step 1b' is the phase publications. 'Process the outcome of a firing' is a settle step (commit, fail, tdeposit, EXEC-020, EXEC-030, EXEC-022). 'Ends a run because it is stopped' is finish stopped. 'Ending the run' in line 7 is any finish: the quoted reason sentence leaves the reason to EXEC-041 (ruling D53 (c): closed and quiescent also conform after an immediate termination), and a terminal place stops the run from any phase (EXEC-042).
- Lines 1 and 2 are the shall sentence 'The executor shall become stopped only when terminateNow() takes effect, and once stopped it shall stay stopped; close() shall not stop it' and 'It is an explicit escape hatch and MUST NOT be invoked implicitly by close()'. They pin what EXEC-041's lines 6 and 7 read as 'an immediate termination was requested': the mode of the source state. A close that terminates immediately breaks line 1 (ENV_015_forbids_closeAsStop); a close after the stop that reopens a lifecycle that admits completions breaks line 2 (ENV_015_forbids_closeAfterStop; Java's close() after terminateNow() only sets flags that are already set). That a close itself changes only the mode to closed is ENV-013's line 1.
- Line 3 is the two shall sentences on the moment terminateNow() takes effect, item 2 ('Queued external events are discarded') and item 4's 'their consumed tokens are lost'. A stop written as a close, which waits for the actions in flight and admits their completions, breaks it (ENV_015_forbids_terminateAsClose), and so does a stop that puts back the tokens the firings in flight consumed (ENV_015_forbids_rollbackAtTerminate). The phase conjunct is 'shall not move its loop to another step' and item 3's 'The loop stops at the end of its current cycle': a stop that ends the run at the call (Java's terminateNow() completing the run future itself) breaks it (ENV_015_forbids_endsAtCall), and so would a stop that jumps to the start of the next cycle. The queue conjunct is 'shall discard every external event still queued': a stop that keeps the queue and drops it later, in step 2 or at the finish, breaks it (ENV_015_forbids_queueKeptAtStop). The parked conjunct is 'shall end a wait under way in step 6': a stop that leaves a parked loop parked breaks it (ENV_015_forbids_stopKeepsWait). A second terminateNow() of a stopped executor is no step of the reference (Java's second call sets flags already set); line 3 does not need it.
- Line 4 is item 1 and the shall sentence on inject(): a stopped executor answers refused (false) or error, never accepted (ENV_015_forbids_acceptWhileStopped). That a refused request changes nothing is ENV-006's. AC3's 'does not hang' is coverage: the third clause of Env015Covers (a request to a stopped executor is answered), which the reference meets (env015_ref_covers).
- Line 5 is item 2 and the shall sentence on injection: no queued event reaches the marking once the executor is stopped. An executor that keeps the queue at the stop and injects what was sent before it (the Rust reading of a close, ENV-013, carried over to the stop) breaks it (ENV_015_forbids_injectWhileStopped). The reference drops the queue at the stop, and line 8 drops what is left at the finish; the admission signal of every dropped event completes with false (ENV-004).
- Line 6 is item 3's 'their results are discarded rather than admitted to the marking' and its shall sentence: once stopped, no outcome is processed in step 1 or in the wait (EXEC-001), so a late return is never committed or failed. The firing pass of the current cycle is part of that cycle: a synchronous action it waits for still completes inside it (Java runs it inline on the orchestrator thread and deposits its output there; the Java test that calls terminateNow() from inside an action), and ENV_015_nonvacuous commits such a firing in a stopped pass. The exemption is the synchronous firing only: an asynchronous firing whose outcome is queued when the pass is under way is not settled there (settleOk), so an executor that admits a late completion in the wait (ENV_015_forbids_lateAdmit) or that commits an asynchronous firing's queued outcome in a stopped pass (ENV_015_forbids_asyncInPass) breaks the line.
- Line 7 is item 3's 'The loop stops at the end of its current cycle' and its shall sentence: at the start of a cycle a stopped executor ends the run and goes no further. An executor that runs on into another cycle once stopped breaks it (ENV_015_forbids_goesOn). Answers to a snapshot request are exempt, as the sentence's parenthesis and EXEC-041's naming say: a snapshot answer reads the state and is not a step of the loop, and what it answers is ENV-014's (the reference offers none at phase completions).
- The shall sentence 'When the executor is stopped and its loop reaches the start of a cycle, it shall end the run without waiting for the actions still in flight' and item 3's 'it does NOT wait for in-flight actions' say that the end of the run is offered at once, firings in flight or not (AC1). That is coverage, which a safety line cannot state: Env015Covers below is the conjunct for the consistency theorem, a clause of ExecCoversW5 (ConsistencyExec.lean) (finish stopped offered at a live stopped start of a cycle, wake offered in a live stopped wait, a request answered). An executor whose stop waits for every action in flight to return (env015_wait, the stop written in the shape of a close) meets every line (env015_wait_meets) and fails the conjunct (env015_wait_not_covered). The wait the stop ends: line 3 clears the parked flag, and the second clause offers the wake; the reference still offers a park after the stop (parkStep has no mode guard), which with the wake that follows is a stutter, and 'does not wait' rests on the wake being offered.
- Line 8 is the last shall sentence: finish stopped happens at the start of a cycle, not in the middle of one (ENV_015_forbids_stopMidCycle), keeps the marking, so the tokens the abandoned firings consumed stay consumed (ENV_015_forbids_rollbackOnStop; EXEC-041 line 1 also keeps the marking at every finish), and drops the queued events (ENV_015_forbids_keepQueued: an executor that keeps them queued past the end never answers them).
- Item 4's 'In-flight actions keep running where the runtime cannot cancel them ([IO-013])': no line requires the firings in flight to stay in the list of firings, since a runtime that can cancel an action may; the reference keeps them (finish stopped keeps fl), and their outside steps go on after the finish (ENV_015_nonvacuous returns t's action after the finish). That nothing such a late result does changes the returned marking is EXEC-041's lines 2 and 3; whether the action is stopped is IO-013's.
- Termination reason: the reference reports stopped. Java reports CLOSED after terminateNow(), because terminateNow() also sets the closed flag, and the reason chain in executeLoop's finally reads closed before STOPPED; EXEC-041 allows closed after an immediate termination. Java's CLOSED with an action still in flight matches no reference finish closed (which needs nothing in flight); that is the reason's question (EXEC-041, ENV-013), not this block's: the sentence 'Which termination reason the run reports is [EXEC-041]'s.' says so.
- Line 9 is the shall sentence on mid-action publications (IO-015, step 1b) and the sentence 'the executor never deposits its result': once stopped, no flushed batch lands in the wait or anywhere outside step 1b. A step 1b under way when the call took effect still finishes (the call takes effect when that step ends), which the reference allows at phase publications; a stopped executor reaches that phase only that way, since line 7 holds it at the start of a cycle. A Rust or Python wait whose flush arm deposits unconditionally, given a stop flag read at the top of the loop as Java reads it, breaks the line (ENV_015_forbids_publishWhileStopped: the batch t flushed lands on the wake the stop caused, and the run ends stopped with 70 in place 1). Publications are a Rust and Python feature, and only Java has terminateNow(); the line binds a runtime that has both.
- Line 10 is the shall sentence on the firing pass of the current cycle: the stop does not cut the pass short, so the transitions left in its ready order are still offered, each started or lost as EXEC-002 and TIME-014 say (whether a head can start is theirs). An executor whose pass breaks off at the stop (an early exit in Java's fireReadyTransitions or the TypeScript firing loop) breaks it (ENV_015_forbids_passBreaksOff: stopped with t at the head of the order, the pass ends without starting t, and the run then ends with 7 still in place 0). ENV_015_nonvacuous starts t in a stopped pass.
- Scope: the Status is Proposed and the operation is a MAY. Rust, TypeScript and Python take no terminateNow step, so lines 3 to 8 say nothing about them, and line 1 holds of them (no step stops them).
- AC1 (terminateNow() stops the loop without awaiting an outstanding in-flight action) is lines 3, 6, 7 and 8 with the coverage conjunct; ENV_015_nonvacuous takes terminateNow with t's action in flight, offers no endCompletions at the next start of a cycle and finishes stopped with t still in flight.
- AC2 (the in-flight action's eventual output is not admitted to the marking) is lines 6 and 9, with EXEC-041's lines 2 and 3 after the finish; ENV_015_nonvacuous offers no commit of t's returned output in a stopped wait or a stopped pass, no publication of its flushed batch in a stopped wait, and t's return after the finish leaves place 1 empty.
- AC3 (inject() after terminateNow() returns error / false, does not hang) is line 4 with the third coverage clause; ENV_015_nonvacuous answers a request for the environment place refused and one for another place error, and offers no accepted answer. A call made after terminateNow() returns but before the call takes effect is the quoted sentence on a request that lands before the call takes effect: its answer may be accepted, and its admission completes with false (line 3 and ENV-004).
- The test derivation (a gated in-flight action, terminateNow(), the loop ends without releasing the gate, the output never reaches the marking) is ENV_015_nonvacuous's run: t starts asynchronously, the executor stops, finishes stopped, and t's later return deposits nothing.

<a id="Libpetri-Spec-ENV_016"></a>
## ENV-016: Observable Termination

`Libpetri.Spec.ENV_016` · Kind **B** · Scope executors that provide run-with-timeout with a timeout policy (Java, TypeScript) · Source **verbatim** (spec/06-environment-places.md) · Sign-off **pending** · Statement hash `e4509d265396eb2f`

| Natural language | Plain reading | Lean statement |
|---|---|---|
| Independently, run-with-timeout (`run(timeout)`, whose timeout is the caller's run budget named in [EXEC-041]; its expiry fails the caller's wait and does not by itself end the run) MAY expose a policy for what happens to the loop when the caller's timeout expires: *abandon* (leave the loop running; the historical default, rarely desirable) or *close* (stop it per [ENV-013]).<br><br>The expiry of the caller's timeout MUST NOT complete the loop's own result: an abandoned loop can still report its real final marking.<br><br>*Where* an implementation exposes this policy, *when* the caller's timeout expires while the loop is running, the implementation *shall* act on the expiry under the policy the caller chose.<br><br>*When* the caller's timeout expires under *abandon*, the implementation *shall* leave the executor as it was, including its marking, its lifecycle mode, its queues, its firings in flight and the position of its loop, and a running loop *shall* go on running.<br><br>*When* the caller's timeout expires under *close* while the executor is open or draining, the implementation *shall* close the executor as a call of `close()` does ([ENV-013]), even while its loop is running.<br><br>*When* the caller's timeout expires under *close* after the executor is already closed or stopped, the implementation *shall* leave the executor as it was.<br><br>*When* the caller's timeout expires while the loop is running, the implementation *shall not* end the run and *shall not* change the marking.<br><br>Under a *close* policy the executor is closed on timeout and the loop then stops as [ENV-013] says, once its in-flight actions complete; under *abandon* it keeps running. | 1. For every executor R, every expiry handling X of its run-with-timeout and every configuration C:<br>2. an expiry under abandon from state s ends in s itself;<br>3. an expiry under close from a state s whose mode is open or draining ends in a state that a close step of R reaches from s, and from a state s whose mode is closed or stopped it ends in s itself;<br>4. an expiry from a state in which the loop is running ends in a state in which the loop is still running, with the same marking. | <pre>fun {N T} [DecidableEq N] R X ↦<br>  ∀ (C : Cfg N T),<br>    (on fun s s' ↦ X C TimeoutPolicy.abandon s s', shall fun s s' ↦ s' = s) ∧<br>      (on fun s s' ↦ X C TimeoutPolicy.close s s', shall fun s s' ↦<br>          (s.mode = Mode.open ∨ s.mode = Mode.draining → R C s XLbl.close s') ∧<br>            (s.mode = Mode.closed ∨ s.mode = Mode.stopped → s' = s)) ∧<br>        ∀ (pol : TimeoutPolicy),<br>          on fun s s' ↦ X C pol s s' ∧ isExecPhase s.phase = true, shall fun s s' ↦<br>            isExecPhase s'.phase = true ∧ s'.M = s.M</pre> |

**Assumptions**

- The model is a pair: an executor R : XRel N T (glossary GlossaryExec.lean), where R C s l s' says that under configuration C the step labelled l leads from executor state s to s', and the expiry handling X : ExpiryRel N T of its run-with-timeout, where X C pol s s' says that the expiry of the caller's timeout under policy pol (TimeoutPolicy: abandon or close) takes the executor from s to s'. The expiry is an event of the host's clock, which the model does not carry (ruling D18 (b)), so it is a relation beside R and not a label of XLbl. The caller's own result (Java's returned stage failing with a TimeoutException, TypeScript's rejected promise) is not executor state and is outside the model. The witnesses are the reference executor RefExec (Reference/Exec.lean) and refExpiry: abandon changes nothing, close is RefExec's close step, or nothing when the executor is already closed or stopped.
- That the expiry is handled under the policy the caller chose, and not another, is the meaning of X's policy argument: X C pol s s' is the handling of a run whose caller chose pol, so lines 1 and 2 say what each choice does, and the coverage clause Env016Covers says that the handling takes effect at all. The binding of the caller's argument to pol is not modelled further; an implementation that swapped the two policies breaks line 1 on the abandon side (ENV_016_forbids_abandonCloses) and line 2 on the close side (ENV_016_forbids_closeIgnored).
- Scope (Status Proposed, priority MAY, ruling D47 (c)): the block applies to the implementations that expose the policy, Java (run(Duration, RunTimeoutPolicy) in BitmapNetExecutor and PrecompiledNetExecutor) and TypeScript (run(timeoutMs, onTimeout) in both executors). Rust and Python have no run-with-timeout policy. Java's PetriNetExecutor interface has a default run(timeout, policy) that ignores the policy and abandons: an executor that keeps that default does not provide the close policy, and one that claimed to would break line 2 (ENV_016_forbids_closeIgnored).
- Its offer is in ExecCoversW5.Env016Covers (ConsistencyExec.lean; the convention of GlossaryExec.lean: offers are coverage clauses, never block lines). The third EARS sentence demands an answer and is quoted whole; its safety halves are lines 1 and 2, and its existence half is that clause: from every state in which the loop is running, an expiry under either policy has an outcome in X, which the reference meets (env016_ref_covers). AC3 is lines 1 to 3 with that clause. Under abandon the expiry changes nothing and the loop keeps running (line 1; ENV_016_forbids_abandonCloses: an expiry that closes the executor under abandon breaks it). Under close, from an open or draining executor, the expiry is the executor's own close step (line 2; ENV_016_forbids_closeIgnored: an expiry that leaves the executor open breaks it, and so does ENV_016_forbids_closeTerminates, an expiry that stops the loop without waiting for its firings in flight, as terminateNow does under ENV-015). Line 2 reads 'already closed or stopped' on the lifecycle mode, not on the steps R offers, so line 2 and Env016Covers together require R to have a close step from every open or draining state in which its loop runs: an executor that refuses close() while its loop runs, so that the close policy acts as abandon, breaks line 2 (ENV_016_forbids_closeRefusedWhileRunning), and an expiry handling that gave such an executor no outcome there instead would fail Env016Covers. The expiry under close does not stop the loop at once (line 3; ENV_016_forbids_closeFinishes). That the loop then stops once its in-flight actions complete is ENV-013's requirement (its item 4), not a line of this block; ENV_016_nonvacuous part 3 shows it on the test derivation's run. Env016Covers makes the expiry take effect at all: an implementation whose expiry handler never runs meets every line and fails the clause (env016_covers_unhandled). The clause asks for an outcome only while the loop runs: once the run has returned, Java's orTimeout and TypeScript's cleared timer no longer fire.
- The MUST NOT sentence is line 3 with line 1: no expiry while the loop runs ends the run or changes the marking, so the result the loop reports, the marking at its finish and the fact that it ended (EXEC-041), is fixed only by a finish step of the loop. Line 3 adds to line 1 only under close, where it constrains R's own close step; under abandon it follows from line 1. An implementation whose timer completes the loop's own result with the marking at the expiry, the defect Java's loop.copy() avoids, breaks line 1 (ENV_016_forbids_expiryCompletes); one whose close finishes the run at once, reporting the marking at the expiry, breaks line 3 although its expiry is its own close step (ENV_016_forbids_closeFinishes). 'An abandoned loop can still report its real final marking' is ENV_016_nonvacuous part 2: after an expiry under abandon the action in flight returns, its output is deposited, and the loop finishes quiescent with that output in the marking it reports.
- The termination reason an abandoned run reports is EXEC-041's question, not this block's (env-b ENVB-R6 (a), ruling D53 (c)): TypeScript sets its reason to stopped when the caller's timeout expires and keeps it if the loop later ends on its own. That field is reporting state outside the executor state of the model, and D53 (c) allows it, since stopped is not a completed reason. Lines 1 and 3 speak of the executor state and the marking only.
- Java closes the executor from a callback that runs after the returned stage has failed (whenCompleteAsync), so loop steps may come between the expiry and the close. The model places the expiry at the moment close() takes effect; a run in which loop steps come first is a run of R whose close step comes later. TypeScript calls close() in the turn that rejects the promise.
- Which policy is the default is configuration (kind N) and not a line: run(timeout) without a policy abandons in Java and TypeScript, the historical default of the text. The lines hold for whichever policy the caller chooses.
- Deferred to wave W7 (ruling D47 (c), plan W7): AC1, AC2 and the first paragraph, awaitTermination answering false while the loop runs and true once it has stopped and finished its termination bookkeeping (pending inject() futures completed, ExecutionCompleted emitted), returning promptly when the loop was never started, and not being defeated by a failure in that bookkeeping such as a throwing event store. Its answer depends on the emission of ExecutionCompleted, which needs the event model RefEvents; that line will join this block. Blocking, the timeout of awaitTermination and 'promptly' are kind Q.
- The test derivation (a net with an action still in flight when a short timeout expires, under each policy; the executor closed under close and the loop stopping once the action completes, the loop still live under abandon and reporting the action's output) is ENV_016_nonvacuous: at the expiry the loop is still running, parked with a firing in flight; under close the executor is closed by R's close step and the loop finishes closed after the action completes; under abandon the executor is unchanged and the loop goes on to finish quiescent with the action's output. The awaitTermination half of the test derivation is W7's.

**Evidence**

- ✓ **holds** `Libpetri.Spec.ENV_016_reference` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.ENV_016): ✓ The reference executor with the reference expiry handling satisfies ENV-016: abandon is the identity; close is `closeStep`, which is RefExec's close step from an open or draining executor and undefined, so the identity, from a closed or stopped one; and `closeStep` changes only the mode and the parked flag, so the phase and the marking stay (`closeStep_some`).
  <pre>∀ {N T : Type} [inst : DecidableEq N], ENV_016 RefExec refExpiry</pre>
- ✗ **forbids** `Libpetri.Spec.ENV_016_forbids_abandonCloses` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.ENV_016): ✗ Closing under abandon violates ENV-016 (line 1, AC3 "under *abandon* it keeps running"): an open executor is closed by an expiry under abandon.
  <pre>¬ENV_016 RefExec env016_abandonCloses</pre>
- ✗ **forbids** `Libpetri.Spec.ENV_016_forbids_closeFinishes` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.ENV_016): ✗ A close that finishes the run at the expiry violates ENV-016 (line 3, "MUST NOT complete the loop's own result"), although the expiry is that executor's own close step: the run is reported finished, with the marking it had at the expiry.

- ✗ **forbids** `Libpetri.Spec.ENV_016_forbids_expiryCompletes` (Libpetri.Spec.Req.ENV_016): ✗ Completing the loop's result at the expiry violates ENV-016 (line 1, "MUST NOT complete the loop's own result"): under abandon a running loop is finished by the expiry, so the executor is not left as it was.
